qkIZk06Rvc.problem: SMC alignment of diffusion models suffers weight degeneracy and needs many particles when high-reward outputs are rare, and learning twisting functions in high-dimensional diffusion models is unstable.
qkIZk06Rvc.method: TRI-TSMC builds an intermediate trajectory distribution that moves toward the reward-tilted target within a KL trust region around the current proposal (closed form via tempered importance weights), then fits the twisting function to it by weighted maximum likelihood.
qkIZk06Rvc.key_idea: Temper importance weights to stay within a KL trust region around the current proposal, then fit the twist to that tempered distribution by weighted maximum likelihood.
qkIZk06Rvc.evidence: Theory (optimal twist via a soft value function, zero-variance sampler, escort-path variance reduction, forward-KL projection) and experiments on discrete and continuous diffusion models with baselines such as FK-Steering and BoN per reviews; the abstract is cut off before results.
qkIZk06Rvc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and gradient-free, works with black-box rewards on both discrete and continuous diffusion, and that the trust region stabilizes importance weights.
qkIZk06Rvc.main_concern: Baseline and related-work coverage is incomplete (e.g., TDS, Feynman-Kac Correctors, SP-gSMC, DOIT, prior twist learning) and gains appear mainly on the same rewards being optimized, with unmatched settings.

ydfMuRo9tQ.one_liner: Shares each queried label across candidate prediction rules, queries unresolved comparisons, and stops when more labels cannot change the winner.
ydfMuRo9tQ.problem: A test-time model update can raise average accuracy yet damage the next batch, and spending a fixed label budget on every batch wastes feedback on settled decisions.
ydfMuRo9tQ.method: PORTAL chooses among candidate prediction rules per batch: each acquired label evaluates every candidate on the same image, shared successes and mistakes drive comparisons, labels are queried where the remaining budget can still change the choice, and querying stops when labels cannot change the winner or their benefit falls below their cost.
ydfMuRo9tQ.key_idea: Evaluate all candidates on every queried label to compare them via shared errors, and stop querying when the winner cannot change or expected benefit is below label cost.
ydfMuRo9tQ.evidence: Experiments on CODA's benchmarks, CIFAR-C, PACS (class-block arrival), and ImageNet-C, comparing model-selection regret, label savings, and accuracy with identical candidates and label budgets.
ydfMuRo9tQ.claimed_gains: PORTAL cuts cumulative model-selection regret by up to 91.6% on CODA's benchmarks, saves up to 94.6% of labels on CIFAR-C, and raises class-block PACS accuracy from 22.58% to 51.28%.
ydfMuRo9tQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that harm from test-time interventions on individual batches is an overlooked, practical problem and that sharing every label across all candidates uses feedback efficiently.
ydfMuRo9tQ.main_concern: Practical feasibility and baselines: it needs target-domain labels at deployment under a same-label-distribution assumption, lacks direct comparison with CODA and other active model selection methods, and is not more accurate than the best fixed rule on most streams.

OWpcn5nJq2.one_liner: Characterizes regret when updates occur only at adversarial batch boundaries, using relative batch growth and batch-length 2-norm.
OWpcn5nJq2.problem: Standard online learning assumes the decision rule can change every step, but in practice updates may be restricted to certain time steps, with a fixed policy within each batch.
OWpcn5nJq2.method: Formalizes adversarially batched online learning for stochastic bandits, online convex optimization, prediction with expert advice, and adversarial bandits; gives gap-dependent and gap-independent bounds for stochastic bandits via relative batch growth and batch-length 2-norm bounds for the other three, with an upper bound met by a batch-oblivious learner using an adaptive doubling trick.
OWpcn5nJq2.key_idea: Measure batch difficulty by relative batch growth (stochastic) and the 2-norm of the batch-length sequence (other settings), achieved by a batch-oblivious adaptive doubling trick.
OWpcn5nJq2.evidence: Theoretical regret upper and lower bounds across four canonical problems; no experiments are stated.
OWpcn5nJq2.claimed_gains: Regret is tightly characterized by the 2-norm of the batch-length sequence for online convex optimization, experts, and adversarial bandits, and for stochastic bandits the multiplicative penalty can grow superlinearly in batch hardness.
OWpcn5nJq2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and the analysis is coherent and comprehensive, with a natural relative-growth complexity measure for stochastic bandits and upper and lower bounds across the settings.
OWpcn5nJq2.main_concern: Technical novelty is unclear: the OCO, experts, and adversarial-bandit bounds appear recoverable from delayed-feedback work and standard methods, and the stochastic gap-dependent bounds are not tight (alpha^2 upper versus alpha^(3/2) lower).

hXqLI5v51m.one_liner: Segments human-LLM documents by dynamic programming over sentence-score sequences, combining segment residuals with windowed contrast and AIC-style count selection.
hXqLI5v51m.problem: Sentence-level detector scores fluctuate even within one source, so localizing LLM-authored spans in co-authored documents with unknown boundary locations and counts risks spurious boundaries.
hXqLI5v51m.method: Given scores from a frozen local detector, LA-CPD combines a length-weighted within-segment residual with a windowed two-mean contrast, uses dynamic programming to place cuts for each candidate count, and selects the final partition with an AIC-style criterion.
hXqLI5v51m.key_idea: Score candidate cuts with both within-segment consistency and a sustained windowed two-mean change, optimize placement by DP per cut count, and pick the count with an AIC-style criterion.
hXqLI5v51m.evidence: Experiments on a held-out human-LLM co-authored dataset (the abstract is cut off) with component ablations, an oracle-count analysis, and baselines that share the same frozen-detector scores.
hXqLI5v51m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the structured segmentation formulation is well motivated and cleanly combines segment consistency with boundary evidence, with ablations and shared sentence-score inputs that isolate the segmentation stage.
hXqLI5v51m.main_concern: Boundary-count selection is the weak point (AI-F1 of 0.040 with unknown count versus 0.914 with oracle count), the AIC criterion is heuristic, and overlap with the prior WCP change-point method is not clearly separated.

C3TIsOmStE.one_liner: Adds a compact adapter that injects irregular numerical clinical measurements as corrections to a frozen vision-language model's chart-token representations.
C3TIsOmStE.problem: Language models' text abilities do not ensure accurate prediction from structured, high-dimensional clinical time series.
C3TIsOmStE.method: ViSTA is a compact adapter that learns corrections to visual tokens from irregular numerical measurements while leaving all pretrained parameters unchanged, applied to acute kidney injury and mortality prediction and to temporal question answering.
C3TIsOmStE.key_idea: Learn residual corrections to chart visual tokens from numerical event features via pooling and position-conditioned queries, keeping the pretrained backbone frozen.
C3TIsOmStE.evidence: MIMIC-IV acute kidney injury and mortality prediction across models with 2-9 billion parameters, plus temporal question answering, against LoRA on charts or numerical text and other adaptations.
C3TIsOmStE.claimed_gains: Highest mean scores among compared adaptations on all four metrics; with 0.516 million trainable parameters the 2-billion-parameter model reaches an AUROC of 0.7376 for acute kidney injury versus 0.7380 for GPT-5.6 Sol with text input, and temporal QA reaches 69.27% accuracy at 4 billion parameters with over 90% fewer trainable parameters than low-rank adaptation, at a 2.82-4.88 percentage-point accuracy gap.
C3TIsOmStE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, clearly described, and parameter-efficient, with competitive prediction using far fewer trainable parameters than LoRA baselines across many baselines, datasets, and model sizes.
C3TIsOmStE.main_concern: Limited novelty and weak isolation of the benefit: components resemble STraTS and Flamingo-style resamplers, MLLM4TS and ITFormer cover similar ground, and inference-time modality ablations do not show an advantage over a comparably trained numerical-only adapter.

HXok21UQfd.one_liner: Benchmark linking 5,000 human Chinese texts to over 240,000 AI-involved variants for evaluating machine-text detectors under collaborative writing.
HXok21UQfd.problem: Most machine-generated-text detectors are tested only on fully human versus fully AI text, which can overstate reliability when human-AI collaboration weakens or redistributes detection cues, and controlled Chinese resources are scarce.
HXok21UQfd.method: C-HAT-Bench links 5,000 human-written source texts from five domains to more than 240,000 variants made by six generative models under a Prefix-Conditioned Continuation reference setting and three collaborative production modes, and evaluates detectors under four protocols: zero-shot and pretrained supervised document-level detection, boundary localization, and cross-condition generalization.
HXok21UQfd.key_idea: Pair each human source text with controlled machine-involved variants across production modes, domains, and generators, so detector reliability can be measured per collaboration mode.
HXok21UQfd.evidence: Evaluation of detectors (TLDR says 21, abstract says 24) under four protocols across five domains, six generators, a reference setting, and three collaborative production modes.
HXok21UQfd.claimed_gains: Relative to Prefix-Conditioned Continuation, mean AUROC across document-level detectors is 11.0% lower on the collaborative production modes.
HXok21UQfd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is large and comprehensive across domains, generators, production modes, and detectors, and fills a gap for Chinese human-AI collaborative text detection.
HXok21UQfd.main_concern: Novelty and coverage: main findings largely repeat prior results from other languages, the collaborative scenarios may not represent real-world writing, and trained BERT-based or representation-space detectors are not evaluated.

8GO5IO2nmq.one_liner: Uses correct-answer likelihood relative to incorrect-answer likelihood from the same rollout group as a per-prefix baseline in GRPO-style RLVR.
8GO5IO2nmq.problem: RLVR's sequence-level rewards give coarse credit assignment, and prefix-level answer-likelihood signals also reflect spurious context and answer syntax rather than reasoning progress alone.
8GO5IO2nmq.method: CIPS uses the likelihood of plausible incorrect answers from the same rollout group as a control, so a prefix counts as progress only if it raises correct-answer likelihood relative to incorrect ones, and it replaces the group-mean baseline with this prefix-dependent baseline without a learned reward model or extra rollouts.
8GO5IO2nmq.key_idea: Contrast correct-answer and incorrect-answer likelihood given each reasoning prefix to cancel spurious context effects, and use the result as a prefix-dependent advantage baseline.
8GO5IO2nmq.evidence: Two model scales (Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B per reviews) on mathematical and combinatorial reasoning, three seeds, against outcome-only training, prior dense-credit methods, and Dr. GRPO, with ablations.
8GO5IO2nmq.claimed_gains: CIPS consistently outperforms outcome-only training and prior dense-credit methods, and with essentially unchanged step time reaches the final performance of Dr. GRPO with about 25% fewer training (the abstract is cut off after this).
8GO5IO2nmq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea is simple and well motivated, plugs into existing RLVR pipelines without extra reward models or rollouts, and improves math and combinatorial reasoning across two Qwen model scales with useful ablations.
8GO5IO2nmq.main_concern: Evaluation is limited to Qwen3-1.7B and 4B, it is unclear how much of the gain comes from prefix-level credit versus a changed advantage distribution, and the unbiasedness guarantee covers only idealized on-policy sampling.

vwsfTsPMgw.one_liner: Quantizes omni-modal KV caches training-free and query-free, using a transform coder guided by a query-projection-weight logit metric.
vwsfTsPMgw.problem: Streaming omni-modal inputs make the KV cache a memory bottleneck, and existing quantizers minimize reconstruction error or need query activations unavailable at caching time, ignoring how attention reads the cache and cross-modal differences.
vwsfTsPMgw.method: LMTC quantizes Keys with a Modality-Conditioned Transform Coder guided by a Query-Free Logit Metric from query projection weights, allocating precision by reverse water-filling, and quantizes Values with Phase-Offset Rounding that offsets the rounding grids of adjacent visual tokens so errors cancel in attention aggregation.
vwsfTsPMgw.key_idea: Allocate key bits by attention-logit sensitivity derived from query projection weights, and offset value rounding grids across neighboring visual tokens so rounding errors cancel.
vwsfTsPMgw.evidence: Three OmniLLMs on eight benchmarks per the abstract; reviewers also mention ablations, streaming evaluations, and packed-cache decoding measurements.
vwsfTsPMgw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and that optimizing attention-logit distortion rather than reconstruction error, with separate treatment of Keys and Values, is a sound design backed by ablations and streaming evaluations.
vwsfTsPMgw.main_concern: The weight-derived query metric is weakly justified and may not hold for models without query bias or with QK-Norm, and the surrogate objective only approximates attention distortion.

d1XpDdMGhv.one_liner: A hypernetwork generates LoRA adapters for a world model from a few test-time transitions in one forward pass.
d1XpDdMGhv.problem: Adapting a world model to an unknown test-time environment trades computational cost against expressivity: in-context learning is cheap but limited, while gradient-based adaptation is expressive but expensive.
d1XpDdMGhv.method: CLAW jointly trains a hypernetwork and base world model by simulating adaptation across environments during pretraining; at test time the base model is frozen and one hypernetwork forward pass on a small batch of transitions generates the low-rank adapters.
d1XpDdMGhv.key_idea: Amortize adaptation by training a hypernetwork to emit LoRA adapters from context transitions, so test-time adaptation needs no gradient steps.
d1XpDdMGhv.evidence: Locomotion and manipulation environment families varying in dynamics, embodiment, and reward, compared with gradient-based adaptation, in-context learning, Concat, and FiLM, with LoRA-rank studies.
d1XpDdMGhv.claimed_gains: Using only seconds of test-time data, CLAW outperforms gradient-based adaptation during online adaptation, and outperforms in-context learning when base-model capacity is limited; no numeric figures are given.
d1XpDdMGhv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adaptation by a single forward pass without gradient descent is appealing, and note clear pseudocode, relevant baselines, and an experiment where gradient-based methods degrade with more SGD steps while CLAW does not.
d1XpDdMGhv.main_concern: The evaluation does not establish generalization to unseen environments (training covers the full small family), baselines such as meta-trained gradient adaptation are missing, and the notation is hard to parse.

pjN4ibY0Gh.one_liner: Adds auxiliary conditional denoising tasks to CRPS training via a proper scoring rule across noise levels, keeping one-step ensemble sampling.
pjN4ibY0Gh.problem: CRPS-trained one-step weather forecasters learn the predictive distribution from forecast context alone, which becomes hard at long horizons where uncertainty is high.
pjN4ibY0Gh.method: Auxiliary tasks predict the same future state from the context plus a corrupted version of it, and a single stochastic predictor learns these conditional distributions by minimizing a proper scoring rule across noise levels, building on distributional diffusion models; at inference each ensemble member still takes one forward pass at the fully corrupted endpoint.
pjN4ibY0Gh.key_idea: Train the one-step predictor with the corrupted future state as extra conditioning across noise levels, recovering CRPS as the endpoint-only case.
pjN4ibY0Gh.evidence: Controlled experiments across architectures (FGN, FCN3, Swin, U-Net, MOSAIC, U-Cast per reviews) and high-dimensional global weather forecasting with training from scratch and fine-tuning.
pjN4ibY0Gh.claimed_gains: The abstract reports better one-step forecasting across architectures with larger gains at longer forecast horizons, with no numeric figures.
pjN4ibY0Gh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is practical and clearly written, adds only extra conditioning inputs to existing CRPS forecasters, and shows consistent gains across many architectures.
pjN4ibY0Gh.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited (it mostly adapts distributional diffusion models to weather), and the overfitting explanation for the gains, stronger regularized CRPS baselines, and spectral-blurring metrics are not validated.

CRO4nTqblR.one_liner: Uses the rank of the cross-Hessian of the observed log-density to identify latent variables and causal structure under nonlinear mixing.
CRO4nTqblR.problem: Latent causal discovery methods typically assume linear relations or invertible mixing functions, which fails under general nonlinear mixing.
CRO4nTqblR.method: Shows that when two groups of observed variables are d-separated by lower-dimensional latent variables, the cross-Hessian of the observed log-density has rank equal to the latent dimension under a local linearity assumption on conditional log-density derivatives, then uses it to locate latent variables and recover latent causal relations up to the Markov equivalence class.
CRO4nTqblR.key_idea: The cross-Hessian rank between two d-separated variable groups equals the latent dimension, generalizing Tetrad constraints from linear Gaussian to nonlinear models.
CRO4nTqblR.evidence: Theory (Theorem 1 on approximate cross-Hessian rank under d-separation) plus experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, mostly synthetic per reviews.
CRO4nTqblR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory is rigorous and well presented, extending rank-based constraints from Tetrad and cross-covariance to cross-Hessian rank for nonlinear latent causal discovery, with encouraging synthetic results.
CRO4nTqblR.main_concern: The sufficient conditions (local linearity of conditional scores, small residuals relative to the spectral gap) are hard to verify in practice, and the empirical validation is largely synthetic with inadequate real-data evidence.

vs7XUUjf4i.one_liner: Shows source-critic transfer explains much of world-model adaptation's advantage, then adds dynamics ensembles and tethered proposal-policy fine-tuning.
vs7XUUjf4i.problem: Model-based cross-domain adaptation looks more sample-efficient partly because it keeps source-trained value functions while model-free baselines learn critics from scratch, confounding the comparison.
vs7XUUjf4i.method: DomainADEPT improves model-based planning with a dynamics ensemble for accuracy and 'tethered' proposal-policy fine-tuning that limits policy drift during data collection, after analysis showing ensembles and prior-guided data collection jointly improve Dyna-style adaptation.
vs7XUUjf4i.key_idea: Control for value transfer, then combine a dynamics ensemble with a proposal policy tethered to the source policy to limit drift during target data collection.
vs7XUUjf4i.evidence: Four contact-rich manipulation tasks and one locomotion task under matched target-domain interaction budgets (10 random seeds per reviews), plus sim-to-real experiments on two manipulation tasks.
vs7XUUjf4i.claimed_gains: Improves average success by 25 percentage points over the strongest baseline, and reaches 90-100% success after 50 real-world episodes in sim-to-real experiments (the comparison is cut off in the abstract).
vs7XUUjf4i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled separation of value transfer from world-model adaptation is insightful and that the resulting dynamics-ensemble and tethering design is well motivated.
vs7XUUjf4i.main_concern: Generality is limited: each manipulation task uses one fixed target dynamics configuration, the tethering coefficient is chosen per task, and the frozen source value may not stay reliable under larger dynamics shifts.

kXfSP8LLOs.one_liner: Predicts personalized segmentation prompts from one RGB reference image by distilling a hard-negative-trained teacher into a feed-forward offset predictor.
kXfSP8LLOs.problem: Foundation-model prompt spaces generalize semantically but are insufficient for personalization, where one subject must be distinguished from visually similar same-category instances.
kXfSP8LLOs.method: PerSeg-DPT learns a personalized prompt teacher with positive supervision and hard negatives including same-class distractors; PerSegDelta predicts an identity-specific offset from a semantic base prompt using the RGB reference; PerSeg-Adapt predicts similarity-gated prompt updates for appearance change in video.
kXfSP8LLOs.key_idea: Distill a hard-negative-trained personalized prompt teacher into a network that predicts an identity-specific offset from a semantic base prompt, with no mask or per-identity optimization.
kXfSP8LLOs.evidence: The new PODS/DreamBooth composite benchmark (2x2 protocol varying distractor difficulty), plus PODS, DreamBooth, YouTube-VOS, retrieval, and ablations on negatives per reviews; the abstract is cut off before results.
kXfSP8LLOs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating a target from same-category look-alikes is well motivated and that ablations show hard negatives (image and prompt distractors) drive identity discrimination.
kXfSP8LLOs.main_concern: Headline comparisons are confounded: PerSegDelta trains on PODS identities while baselines are training-free, gains shrink on DreamBooth and YouTube-VOS, and the task largely reduces to instance selection without an obvious mask-free baseline.

wgAXxOgnEE.one_liner: Single reward-weighted cross-entropy RL objective that fine-tunes diffusion and flow language models using each model's own pretraining loss.
wgAXxOgnEE.problem: RL methods for diffusion and flow models are built one model type at a time, and none applies across the range of corruption processes, state spaces, and samplers.
wgAXxOgnEE.method: Tilted Generator Matching (TGM) casts each step of KL-regularized RL as the model's own pretraining loss tilted by exponentiated reward, for any model expressible in the generator matching framework, making it likelihood-free, sampler-agnostic, and on-policy; it is studied on diffusion and flow language models with masked, uniform, and Gaussian noise and few-step flow maps.
wgAXxOgnEE.key_idea: Each step of KL-regularized RL is solved exactly by the model's pretraining loss weighted by exponentiated reward, so RL reduces to weighted pretraining.
wgAXxOgnEE.evidence: Sudoku, GSM8K, and sentiment tasks on masked, uniform-noise, Gaussian, and flow-map diffusion language models, compared with family-specific methods such as RAFT and Flow-GRPO per reviews.
wgAXxOgnEE.claimed_gains: A single configuration improves every DLM family and matches or beats family-specific methods, in one case more than doubling accuracy (17.0 to 37.2).
wgAXxOgnEE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the common formulation is useful because it needs neither sequence likelihoods nor stored trajectories, and that it gives substantial gains, including first RL results on uniform-noise and flow-map language models.
wgAXxOgnEE.main_concern: Novelty and comparison fairness: the idea traces to reward-weighted regression, tilt matching, and discrete tilt matching, and the advantage over GRPO baselines is confounded by different anchors and update budgets.

H8qAbQjg0C.one_liner: Training-free controller that steers a pretrained flow editor's sampling trajectory in three phases toward observation-consistent image restoration.
H8qAbQjg0C.problem: Flow-based image editors give plausible restorations that can deviate from the scene supported by the degraded observation, limiting restoration fidelity.
H8qAbQjg0C.method: RestoreSteer matches correction target and magnitude to sampling phases: RouteCal redirects early scene formation using observation-supported structure and coarse appearance, StructAlign corrects persistent geometric disagreement once boundaries emerge, and ObsRefine optimizes a bounded late latent residual through the frozen decoder and forward degradation model, with each stage evaluating bounded candidates before modifying the state.
H8qAbQjg0C.key_idea: Apply different bounded corrections at different sampling phases (scene formation, geometry, late residual) rather than inverting the observation to a fixed pseudo-clean target.
H8qAbQjg0C.evidence: Six restoration tasks on Qwen-Image-Edit and FLUX.2 backbones with component ablations; the abstract is cut off before results.
H8qAbQjg0C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is training-free, transfers across backbones and degradation types, and shows consistent gains across six tasks with an intuitive phase-dependent design.
H8qAbQjg0C.main_concern: Evidence that phase-adaptive control itself drives the gains is weak: ablations only remove components, no alternative schedules are compared under matched compute, and baseline fairness and overhead are unclear.

nKiFotcuWh.one_liner: Streaming model that decides when to start speaking, how long to continue, and where the user is in a procedure.
nKiFotcuWh.problem: Existing MLLMs and streaming video assistants lack unified procedural assistance that tracks task progress, intervenes proactively at the right moment, and answers user queries as the task unfolds.
nKiFotcuWh.method: Introduces the ProactiveCooking dataset with 6,526 human-verified question-answer interactions across six interaction types (Main set and an Advanced set with reordered, repeated, and skipped steps) and ONSTEP, an end-to-end streaming framework that models speaking onset, continuation, and procedural position; reviewers add onset prediction, cross-chunk response control, and step-aware contrastive learning.
nKiFotcuWh.key_idea: Separate predicting utterance onset from continuation and anchor each decision to the current procedure step, trained end-to-end on streaming egocentric video.
nKiFotcuWh.evidence: ProactiveCooking Main and Advanced sets in egocentric cooking, comparing ONSTEP with baseline streaming and MLLM assistants, with cumulative ablations of the onset formulation and step objective per reviews.
nKiFotcuWh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified proactive and interactive formulation is useful, the human-verified dataset adds value, and separating utterance onset from continuation is simple and well motivated.
nKiFotcuWh.main_concern: Baseline training conditions are under-specified (no same-backbone streaming baseline trained on the same data), and failure analysis shows wrong procedural answers and incorrect positive feedback despite better timing.

PGikNTA3D4.one_liner: Co-generates video and 3D rig motion by coupling a separate arbitrary-skeleton motion model to a pretrained video model via cross-attention.
PGikNTA3D4.problem: Video models depict realistic motion but cannot return it as replayable 3D motion for a specific 3D asset placed in a 3D scene, and prior joint video-motion models copy billions of parameters from the video model to generate motion.
PGikNTA3D4.method: A separate motion model supporting arbitrary skeletons is pretrained on motion-only data and linked to a pretrained video model through a small set of cross-attention layers; the model also learns to locate each joint in video frames to recover the camera and register motion to the scene, trained on edited-scene data from a generative video editor plus human and robot video.
PGikNTA3D4.key_idea: Keep 3D motion in its own arbitrary-skeleton model coupled to the video model by cross-attention, and use joint localization in frames to recover the camera.
PGikNTA3D4.evidence: Evaluations of animating diverse rigs from text, human synchronization, and conditional animal motion recovery, with bridge ablations and comparisons to Puppeteer and ActionMesh per reviews; the abstract is cut off.
PGikNTA3D4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the architecture is practical and flexible, with an independently pretrainable motion model, parameter-efficient bidirectional coupling, and camera recovery that support video-to-motion, motion-to-video, and keyframe control.
PGikNTA3D4.main_concern: Validation is insufficient: no direct measure that generated non-human video and 3D motion agree, limited ablations of coupling directions and joint localization, and missing baselines such as Wan2.2 plus motion recovery.

u0ebS4XwJF.one_liner: Feed-forward transformer that compresses a driver's frozen-encoder features into a compact whole-human motion embedding for face, upper-body, and full-body animation.
u0ebS4XwJF.problem: Body animation methods usually need external pose estimators and many denoising steps, while compact learned motion representations mostly cover only the face.
u0ebS4XwJF.method: A Q-Former compresses the driver's features from a frozen visual encoder into a motion embedding, disentangled from appearance by a contrastive loss that pulls it toward the embedding of the driver's rendered keypoint image and away from that of the same person in another pose; no pose estimators, keypoints, or body models are needed at inference.
u0ebS4XwJF.key_idea: Contrast the motion embedding with rendered keypoint-image embeddings of the same pose versus the same person in another pose, so motion separates from appearance.
u0ebS4XwJF.evidence: Retrieval comparison against ten vision encoders, an upper-body benchmark with self- and cross-reenactment metrics, and face and full-body evaluations.
u0ebS4XwJF.claimed_gains: Same-person retrieval rate is 0.1% against 9.5% for its own DINOv3 backbone, it outperforms all baselines on every self-reenactment metric and on cross-reenactment identity similarity on the upper-body benchmark, and it runs at up to 38.9 FPS at 512x512 on a single RTX 4090.
u0ebS4XwJF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that a single feed-forward model covering face, upper-body, and full-body animation in real time without pose estimators or iterative denoising is valuable, with a well-analyzed motion embedding.
u0ebS4XwJF.main_concern: Limited novelty and under-explained design: the contrastive loss resembles prior motion-embedding methods, the contribution largely combines existing components, and choices such as a DINOv3-only motion branch and two tokens are not justified.

6sGz2fVREg.one_liner: Generates inductive-inference items whose difficulty is measured in bits by Levin's Kt, using an LLM as the reference machine.
6sGz2fVREg.problem: Benchmarks calibrated with humans or current AI systems become circular or saturate, so they cannot evaluate machines that may exceed both current systems and test writers.
6sGz2fVREg.method: Presents the first test based on Levin's Kt with LLMs as representational machines: a formalized difficulty measure and a lightweight generation and certification pipeline that produces fresh items, with difficulty on a ratio scale in bits, before frontier models can solve them.
6sGz2fVREg.key_idea: Define item difficulty as an upper bound on Levin's Kt relative to an LLM reference machine, found by prompt search with weaker models.
6sGz2fVREg.evidence: Experiments across multiple reference models and complexity measures, with a main Qwen3-14B analysis of certified items and a high-difficulty 'supraintelligence window' where frontier models fail, per reviews.
6sGz2fVREg.claimed_gains: Fresh test items can be produced at high difficulties, in bits, before any frontier model can solve them; no numeric results are visible in the abstract.
6sGz2fVREg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation problem is real and that defining difficulty by construction with an LLM as reference machine is new and potentially valuable, with extensive analysis across models and complexity measures.
6sGz2fVREg.main_concern: Calibration and validity are weakly supported: Kt estimates are loose upper bounds from limited search, certification checks only a limited set of rival programs, and the supraintelligence window rests on few items (ten above 190 bits).

reogedwLME.one_liner: Mitigates LLM conformity by unlearning socially shifted answers under peer-pressure contexts while retaining reference-supported answers.
reogedwLME.problem: LLMs may answer correctly alone but switch to incorrect answers after seeing peer responses, and prompt-level or reflection mitigations only reshape the inference-time context rather than correcting parameters.
reogedwLME.method: A conformity-targeted unlearning framework identifies answer shifts, constructs forget-retain pairs from conformity-inducing interaction traces, and applies selective unlearning that lowers the likelihood of socially shifted responses while retaining supervision preserves reference-supported behavior.
reogedwLME.key_idea: Treat socially induced wrong answers as the forget set and reference-supported answers for the same context as the retain set.
reogedwLME.evidence: Comparisons with prompting methods and parameter-update baselines under simulated unanimous-majority and social-guidance protocols, with a question split and three training seeds per reviews; the abstract is cut off.
reogedwLME.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that casting conformity mitigation as unlearning is a new framing, building forget-retain examples from observed failures is practical, and results improve on prompting and parameter-update baselines.
reogedwLME.main_concern: It is unclear why unlearning is preferable to standard fine-tuning, preference training, or context engineering, and the evaluation relies on narrow simulated settings of uncertain practical relevance.

50V6SPxzIO.one_liner: Compares successful and unsuccessful reasoning trajectories only within the same question and relative phase to isolate path-quality directions.
50V6SPxzIO.problem: Probes trained across heterogeneous questions with final-answer labels can exploit question-level variation rather than path quality, and states aligned by absolute step index may correspond to different reasoning phases.
50V6SPxzIO.method: PAIR samples multiple trajectories per question, maps variable-length paths onto shared relative phases using normalized trajectory progress, and compares successful and unsuccessful trajectories within the same question and phase to derive phase-specific path-quality directions.
50V6SPxzIO.key_idea: Normalize trajectories to relative phases and contrast hidden states of correct versus incorrect paths only within one question and phase.
50V6SPxzIO.evidence: Multiple models and reasoning benchmarks, evaluating trajectory ranking, Best-of-N selection, and steering against across-question correctness probes and a normalized-step baseline per reviews; the abstract is cut off.
50V6SPxzIO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the within-question analysis exposes a real limitation of across-question correctness probing, and that PAIR is well motivated with consistent gains in trajectory ranking, Best-of-N selection, and steering.
50V6SPxzIO.main_concern: The contribution of phase alignment is not isolated: a strong normalized-step baseline suggests relative-position normalization explains part of the gain, and token-based alignment may not match functional phases.

H44QwuOIxw.one_liner: Replaces Rashomon-set search with ensembling over models that beat the risk minimizer on affected groups, plus multicalibration for fairness.
H44QwuOIxw.problem: Searching a Rashomon set for a fairer, equally accurate model is computationally expensive and does not easily give generalization guarantees.
H44QwuOIxw.method: Defines meaningful multiplicity as whether any hypothesis outperforms the risk minimizer on a target group, gives efficient ensembling techniques over models that witness it and outperform the risk minimizer on all affected groups, shows suitably multiaccurate models preclude meaningful multiplicity, and for constraint-based fairness metrics builds a multicalibrated predictor and post-processes it (the abstract is cut off).
H44QwuOIxw.key_idea: Ask whether some model beats the risk minimizer on a group, then combine group-wise improvements by ensembling rather than searching the Rashomon set.
H44QwuOIxw.evidence: Theoretical results with proofs and finite-sample guarantees; reviewers note there is no empirical validation.
H44QwuOIxw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written and rigorous, and that the reframing yields a more tractable route to fairness under multiplicity with constructive guarantees for combining improvements across overlapping groups.
H44QwuOIxw.main_concern: The technical contribution beyond existing multigroup learning (bias bounties, multicalibrated postprocessing) is insufficiently distinguished, and the paper lacks concrete examples, limitations, and empirical validation.

BcSLVt0VMu.one_liner: Platform-side Delivery-Evidence Credit policy that reallocates selection opportunities using recorded delivery outcomes in a content-agent ecosystem.
BcSLVt0VMu.problem: In the Agentic Web, content agents compete by optimizing submitted profiles before any documents are seen, and this competition lowers website-selection quality and settles at a harmful stable point.
BcSLVt0VMu.method: Builds WildRegistry, a simulation framework and benchmark from a real agentic-search request stream modeled as a dynamic game under private monitoring, and designs DEC, which uses recorded delivery outcomes to reallocate later opportunities and reduce information asymmetry.
BcSLVt0VMu.key_idea: Use recorded delivery outcomes to credit or withhold later selection opportunities, so profile optimization no longer pays without delivering.
BcSLVt0VMu.evidence: Long-horizon simulation experiments on WildRegistry with multiple backbones, a second group of adaptive websites, component ablations, and human relevance checks per reviews.
BcSLVt0VMu.claimed_gains: DEC raises website-selection quality while preserving most of providers' exposure gains, for a Welfare Gain of +2.01 points.
BcSLVt0VMu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is timely and the benchmark captures a useful feedback loop between selection and provider adaptation, with component ablations and several backbones supporting DEC in the tested settings.
BcSLVt0VMu.main_concern: Simulation realism and claim scope are limited: providers edit only profiles with fixed documents, the equilibrium result covers one prescribed updater, and confidence intervals lack independent repetitions of the full adaptation process.

3VNF2Hp0SE.one_liner: Splits large images into independently fitted competitive regional diagrams used as shared units of primitive fitting, coding, and rendering.
3VNF2Hp0SE.problem: Explicit primitive-based image representations are costly to scale to large images because geometry-dependent per-pixel competition is repeatedly updated during fitting, altered by quantization, and rediscovered during rendering.
3VNF2Hp0SE.method: CORD localizes competition within regional diagrams, using bounded competitive fitting with early pruning, decoded-state coding that adapts appearance to decoded geometry and picks alternatives by decoded distortion and encoded size, image-wide rate allocation reused across budgets, and persistent contributor mapping that compiles contributor lists into compact GPU state.
3VNF2Hp0SE.key_idea: Localize the recurring geometry-dependent competition into regional diagrams that serve as the common unit for fitting, coding, and rendering.
3VNF2Hp0SE.evidence: The abstract cites 39 large images from four datasets with rate-distortion and fitting-time comparisons against SGI and SAD, while reviewers cite only nine test images; ablations cover color re-adaptation.
3VNF2Hp0SE.claimed_gains: States that CORD achieves better rate-distortion trade-offs on 39 large images from four datasets; the rest of the abstract is cut off.
3VNF2Hp0SE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the system is well designed and coherent, giving better reconstruction quality with less storage and fitting time than SGI and SAD, with a native GPU implementation and clear ablations.
3VNF2Hp0SE.main_concern: The evaluation is small (reviewers cite nine images, three also used for tuning), there is no comparison with modern codecs, and novelty is limited because regional decomposition, quantization-aware refinement, and rate allocation follow prior work.

wNtoGVhSSn.one_liner: Applies post-hoc retrieval corrections to frozen multimodal models only when a calibrated gate says correction is safe, controlling harmful intervention.
wNtoGVhSSn.problem: A deployed multimodal predictor with frozen weights may face missing modalities, and it is unclear how much of the resulting error is correctable from the remaining information versus irreducible ambiguity.
wNtoGVhSSn.method: Characterizes correctable error via the Bayes gap, shows the Bayes prediction can be estimated without retrieval labels when a model seeing more modalities is conditionally correct, and introduces GUARD, which estimates a candidate correction by retrieval, learns from deployment-matched labeled data when correction helps, and calibrates a threshold on a held-out split by conformal risk control.
wNtoGVhSSn.key_idea: Separate building a candidate correction from deciding to apply it, and set the decision threshold by conformal risk control on the joint probability of harmful intervention.
wNtoGVhSSn.evidence: Theory (Bayes gap, finite-sample risk guarantee) and experiments on seven benchmarks across diverse tasks and architectures, including IEMOCAP, with ablations on scoring, calibration, correction targets, and data per reviews; the abstract is cut off.
wNtoGVhSSn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between correctable error and irreducible ambiguity is clear and well supported by theory, and that GUARD keeps most performance gains while reducing harmful interventions.
wNtoGVhSSn.main_concern: The methodological increment is unclear because GUARD combines existing retrieval correction, a learned action score, and conformal risk control, and its joint-harm guarantee still allows many applied corrections to be harmful (83.15% on IEMOCAP).

URUpv3vkIA.one_liner: Open-source configurable multi-echelon logistics simulator generating scenario-conditioned time-series datasets and forecasting benchmarks for foundation models.
URUpv3vkIA.problem: Open time-series forecasting benchmarks cover retail, energy, weather, and traffic, but supply-chain logistics, with its network-level dynamics, is underserved.
URUpv3vkIA.method: ISOMORPH advances a directed routing graph in discrete time through demand, stock or backlog, and replenishment, tracking on-hand inventory, outstanding orders, in-transit shipments, and smoothed demand so the dynamics form a Markov chain with three structurally encoded conservation laws; a step-by-step calibration uses partial observations from SupplyGraph, and datasets are released at two catalogue scales.
URUpv3vkIA.key_idea: Specify the supply chain as a Markov chain over a full network-state vector with conservation laws, yielding interpretable, configurable synthetic data with verification checks.
URUpv3vkIA.evidence: Simulated data reproduce the bullwhip effect at magnitudes consistent with industry evidence, calibration against SupplyGraph, and foundation-model benchmarks under baseline and perturbed conditions.
URUpv3vkIA.claimed_gains: Calibration against SupplyGraph matches 33/39 statistics (reviewers report only 15 of 39 within the simulated ranges).
URUpv3vkIA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the supply-chain domain is under-served and that the configurable, mechanistically specified simulator with network-state variables and conservation-law checks is a useful released resource.
URUpv3vkIA.main_concern: Real-world validation is limited (only 15 of 39 SupplyGraph statistics fall within simulated ranges, with large gaps in demand variability and bullwhip ratios), and the digital-twin label is not backed by real-time synchronization.

5cD7BnOSVh.one_liner: Fits a repetition-aware scaling law for mixing scarce target data with abundant generic data, from over 2,000 training runs.
5cD7BnOSVh.problem: Mixing scarce target data (low-resource languages, specialized domains) with generic data forces a trade-off between underexposing the model to the target and repeating target examples so often that returns diminish and overfitting sets in.
5cD7BnOSVh.method: Studies more than 2,000 LM training runs across model sizes, target dataset sizes, and data types (multilingual, domain-specific, quality-filtered), then introduces a repetition-aware mixture scaling law that accounts for the decreasing value of repeated target tokens and the regularizing role of generic data, and optimizes it to compute mixture configurations.
5cD7BnOSVh.key_idea: Model target-domain loss with a scaling law that discounts repeated target tokens and credits generic data as a regularizer, then optimize mixture ratio and repetition from it.
5cD7BnOSVh.evidence: More than 2,000 training runs across multiple model and target dataset sizes and data types; reviewers note cross-model-scale prediction was tested only on models from 101M to 805M parameters.
5cD7BnOSVh.claimed_gains: Scarce target corpora can be reused 15-20 times in mixture training, with the optimal number of repetitions depending on target data size, compute budget, and model scale.
5cD7BnOSVh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the practical problem is important and the empirical study is extensive, with controlled variation of data quantity and quality and coverage of low-resource-language, quality-filtered, and multi-domain settings.
5cD7BnOSVh.main_concern: Scale and fit: experiments use small models with unverified extrapolation to larger ones, and the fitted formula appears unable to produce the non-monotonic overfitting curves shown in the figures.

ywAK3xn6mK.one_liner: Trains top-k selectors for RAG and MoE with a hybrid gradient combining a supervised component and policy gradients.
ywAK3xn6mK.problem: Training top-k selection modules (document selection in RAG, expert routing in MoE) suffers from weak gradient signals, poor exploration-exploitation tradeoffs, and heuristic objectives.
ywAK3xn6mK.method: Proposes a principled objective whose gradient has a hybrid form with a supervised component and policy gradients, proves convergence at rate O(1/sqrt(T)) with the optimal bound reached by balancing bias and variance, and applies it to synthetic regression, RAG, and MoE.
ywAK3xn6mK.key_idea: Add a lambda-scaled score-function policy-gradient term on the sampled subset to the supervised selection gradient, trading bias against variance.
ywAK3xn6mK.evidence: Synthetic regression, RAG, and MoE experiments measuring next-token prediction perplexity and QA accuracy, plus a convergence analysis; reviewers note small-scale tasks and k fixed at three.
ywAK3xn6mK.claimed_gains: Converges at rate O(1/sqrt(T)) and outperforms baselines in next-token prediction perplexity and QA task accuracies; no numeric results are stated.
ywAK3xn6mK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and clearly modeled, with a useful split between learning which items to select and how to combine them and a well-motivated bias-variance trade-off.
ywAK3xn6mK.main_concern: Experiments are small (simple RAG tasks, tiny MoE, k fixed at three), related stochastic-selection RAG training is not compared, and the algorithmic addition over standard score-function plus pathwise gradients is modest.

RKKGxm7O4L.one_liner: Benchmark of 90 financial-audit tasks over synthetic engagements generated from differentially private statistics and auditor expertise.
RKKGxm7O4L.problem: Measuring AI agents on financial audit work is limited by lack of access to proprietary or privacy-sensitive data, and existing benchmarks rely on public data, authored tasks, or simplified settings.
RKKGxm7O4L.method: A task-generation framework uses differentially private aggregate statistics from historical audits plus over 1,100 hours of audit-expertise development and review to build six synthetic audit engagements, each averaging 179 files, with 90 workpaper completion and review tasks.
RKKGxm7O4L.key_idea: Generate synthetic audit engagements from differentially private aggregate statistics of real audits, shaped by auditor-built generators, so privacy-sensitive tasks can be benchmarked.
RKKGxm7O4L.evidence: Evaluation of eleven frontier models on 90 tasks across six synthetic engagements, with failure analysis and domain-expert review.
RKKGxm7O4L.claimed_gains: Eleven frontier models complete substantial portions of staff-level audit tasks well but sometimes perform inappropriate procedures or produce incorrect documentation; the benchmark has 90 tasks over six engagements averaging 179 files.
RKKGxm7O4L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the audit domain is under-explored, the differential-privacy design is principled, the benchmark is well constructed and expert-reviewed, and the failure analysis of frontier models is informative.
RKKGxm7O4L.main_concern: Synthetic-data realism is not quantitatively validated (only auditor feedback, no blinded assessment, no evidence that benchmark scores track production audits), and the auditor-defined generator may embed inductive bias.

tOOsjxJtjh.one_liner: Models multiple Earth observation products jointly as hybrid neural fields sharing a factored feature volume with lightweight per-product decoders.
tOOsjxJtjh.problem: Satellite observations, embeddings, and map products describing the same Earth are stored as independent petabyte-scale products, calling for compact joint representations that keep spatial and temporal detail.
tOOsjxJtjh.method: PFFs are spatially local explicit-implicit neural fields in which each field shares a factored feature volume (an explicit 3D grid decomposed into smaller factors) across products, and lightweight implicit decoders reconstruct each product over multiple timesteps; new timesteps extend the volumes and new products attach new decoders, leaving existing outputs unchanged.
tOOsjxJtjh.key_idea: Share one factored feature volume across all products and add products through new decoders, exploiting redundancy across data products.
tOOsjxJtjh.evidence: Reconstruction of 14 heterogeneous EO products spanning 2017-2025 over 100 global tiles (16 TB of source data), plus downstream segmentation, change detection, patch classification, and retrieval-latency tests per reviews.
tOOsjxJtjh.claimed_gains: At 1800x compression relative to the source data, reconstructed features retain approximately 90% or more of the performance of the original features on pixel-level segmentation, change detection, and patch-level classification, and feature access latency drops by an order of magnitude (the comparison is cut off).
tOOsjxJtjh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is strong and broad (14 products, 16 TB, downstream and latency tests) and that freezing existing parameters to add timesteps and products without changing earlier outputs is a smart design.
tOOsjxJtjh.main_concern: The claim of a general-purpose Earth representation is not substantiated: downstream tests mostly use reconstructed products, fields are fitted per region without transfer to unseen areas, and compression baselines omit conventional codecs.

7vCTvCbDep.one_liner: RTS benchmark in Beyond All Reason with full matches and diagnostic mini-games for VLM strategic reasoning, plus an agent harness.
7vCTvCbDep.problem: Existing RTS benchmarks cover limited agent configurations, lack controlled evaluation of distinct strategic demands, and stay confined to fixed scenarios.
7vCTvCbDep.method: RTSGameBench offers full-game match-ups, diagnostic mini-games each emphasizing a focal strategic demand, and a self-evolving framework that turns free-form queries into new mini-games; RTSGameAgent combines scalable group-level trajectory planning with short- and long-term memory.
7vCTvCbDep.key_idea: Pair holistic full-game evaluation with focused mini-games and an extensible query-to-mini-game generator, run through a group-level trajectory-planning agent.
7vCTvCbDep.evidence: Evaluation of eight VLMs per reviews in 1v1, 2v2, 3v4, and four-player free-for-all matches plus mini-games, with human raters, comparison to prior agents, and ablations of agent components.
7vCTvCbDep.claimed_gains: RTSGameAgent outperforms existing agents, and state-of-the-art VLMs fall far behind humans, especially when coordinating with allies or facing multiple opponents; the abstract gives no numeric results.
7vCTvCbDep.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree RTS games are a rich testbed, that building on Beyond All Reason broadens strategic coverage (team and free-for-all play) beyond StarCraft II-based benchmarks, and that the holistic, diagnostic, extensible design addresses a real gap.
7vCTvCbDep.main_concern: The reasons agents fail are poorly explained, the group-control ablation removes a composite of mechanisms, and the human-versus-VLM and agent comparisons use under-specified, protocol-sensitive settings.

SqO8ngZucD.one_liner: Scales PCMCI-style temporal causal discovery with GPU global screening, blockwise discovery, and cross-block reconciliation, plus a selection-corrected final pass.
SqO8ngZucD.problem: Temporal causal discovery must consider N^2 L candidate relationships for N series and L lags, which becomes prohibitive as the number of variables grows.
SqO8ngZucD.method: VL-PCMCI screens all lagged pairs with GPU matrix operations, performs causal discovery independently within sparse blocks, reconciles relationships across blocks, and can run a same-data final pass with a selection correction to cut false positives from data-dependent screening.
SqO8ngZucD.key_idea: Separate cheap global screening from expensive blockwise causal reasoning, and correct the statistical tests for the data-dependent screening.
SqO8ngZucD.evidence: Experiments up to millions of variables on planted linear systems, with counterexamples and stress tests characterizing three requirements: true causes survive screening, tested non-edges get separating sets, and testing accounts for screening.
SqO8ngZucD.claimed_gains: Scales to millions of variables with high accuracy; on planted linear systems with millions of variables, the selection-corrected final pass recovers nearly every true edge with accuracy matching that on small systems (the abstract is cut off).
SqO8ngZucD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method gives impressive scalability to millions of variables, the three-stage design is well structured, and the analysis separates computational feasibility from statistical reliability.
SqO8ngZucD.main_concern: The recovery guarantees do not cover the pipeline used in the main scaling results, which skips the final confirmation step and shows rising false discovery (14.51% at two million variables).

4Tvfm46q4p.one_liner: Learns a router choosing, each iteration, the solver predicted to cut error most, blending neural operators and classical solvers.
4Tvfm46q4p.problem: Classical PDE solvers are expensive and ML solvers suffer spectral bias; optimal hybrid iterative scheduling is combinatorial, and exact greedy selection needs the true error, which is unavailable in practice.
4Tvfm46q4p.method: Proposes an approximate greedy router that mimics greedy solver selection from an ensemble at each iteration, trained with a surrogate loss and DAgger per reviews, motivated by a constant-factor approximation guarantee for oracle greedy selection under Lipschitz assumptions.
4Tvfm46q4p.key_idea: Predict which solver gives the largest immediate error drop and select it greedily each step, since greedy selection approximates the optimal schedule under Lipschitz assumptions.
4Tvfm46q4p.evidence: Poisson, convection-diffusion, and anisotropic diffusion equations, on 128x128 periodic grids per reviews, compared with single-solver baselines and HINTS.
4Tvfm46q4p.claimed_gains: Consistently reduces time-to-solution relative to single-solver baselines and existing hybrid approaches such as HINTS; no numeric results are stated.
4Tvfm46q4p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree adaptive per-step routing is a clean, general formulation that improves on fixed hybrid schedules like HINTS, with a theoretical analysis of greedy routing and consistent gains on three PDE benchmarks.
4Tvfm46q4p.main_concern: The theory relies on strict contraction assumptions that some solvers violate and does not cover the learned router, and experiments are narrow (constant-coefficient 2D linear PDEs, limited baselines).

I8dR1Vqxf9.one_liner: Trains students to prefer teacher redrafts of uncertain reasoning segments over their own, on top of token-wise on-policy distillation.
I8dR1Vqxf9.problem: Token-wise on-policy distillation gives no coherent alternative reasoning step showing how a student step could be revised, and degenerate student prefixes can keep teacher supervision conditioned on poor reasoning.
I8dR1Vqxf9.method: Seg-OPD selects student segments with an uncertainty metric, obtains teacher redrafts of them, and trains the student to prefer the redraft over the paired student segment while retaining dense token-wise OPD supervision.
I8dR1Vqxf9.key_idea: Select uncertain student segments, have the teacher redraft them, and train a preference for the redraft over the student's segment alongside token-wise distillation.
I8dR1Vqxf9.evidence: Controlled reasoning interventions showing teacher redrafts improve subsequent accuracy, then experiments on mathematical reasoning and competitive programming with four student models and eight benchmarks against four OPD methods per reviews.
I8dR1Vqxf9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation spans four student models and eight benchmarks with encouraging overall gains, and that uncertainty-based segment selection is supported by intervention comparisons against random anchors.
I8dR1Vqxf9.main_concern: The mechanism claim is weakly supported: selected segments are only masked from the token loss so later distillation still conditions on the original prefix, gains are not uniform (e.g., Qwen3-4B on MATH500 at 89.10 versus 90.71 for OPD), and revision success relies on LLM judgments.

9VHRghku5f.one_liner: Training-free KV-cache eviction that refines recent-window queries and reuses earlier queries to score cached KV pairs.
9VHRghku5f.problem: Eviction scores based only on recent-token queries undervalue KV pairs that future decoding still needs, because those queries cover only recent context and cannot see later tokens under causal masking.
9VHRghku5f.method: QUEEN refines the queries of the most recent tokens so each reflects all of them (intra-window refinement) and reuses refined queries from earlier reasoning and the input prompt (cross-context reuse). A batch-scalable reuse schedule reduces peak GPU memory of the reused queries.
9VHRghku5f.key_idea: Score cached KV pairs with queries enriched by the full recent window and by refined queries from earlier reasoning and the prompt, rather than raw recent-token queries.
9VHRghku5f.evidence: Evaluated on three long-reasoning benchmarks (AIME 2025, MATH500, LiveCodeBench) across several KV budgets and model sizes, with component ablations and a retained-key analysis.
9VHRghku5f.claimed_gains: On LiveCodeBench it matches full-KV accuracy with 5.2x less KV memory and 4.1x higher throughput.
9VHRghku5f.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the accuracy gains are substantial across benchmarks, KV budgets and model sizes, the method is training-free, and the ablations and analyses are useful.
9VHRghku5f.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty and motivation: overlap with DapQ and BeaconKV, no clear case for storing and rescoring old queries instead of keeping historical importance scores, and cross-context reuse tested only on reasoning traces.

YuF0QT9OI7.one_liner: Rollout-free RAG post-training that weights human responses by a value combining pretrained-model likelihood and context faithfulness.
YuF0QT9OI7.problem: Human-written RAG supervision can be out-of-distribution for the pretrained model, causing distributional drift, while the model must also stay faithful to the retrieved context.
YuF0QT9OI7.method: TIDE derives an analytical target LLM by optimizing a value-based objective that combines length-normalized likelihood under the pretrained model with faithfulness to retrieved evidence. Implicit target distillation then trains directly on observed human-written data without constructing or sampling from the target.
YuF0QT9OI7.key_idea: Distill an analytically defined target LLM implicitly, by training on human responses weighted by an exponentiated value of pretrained-model compatibility and faithfulness.
YuF0QT9OI7.evidence: Theoretical analysis of the optimal target (Theorems 3.1 and 4.1) and evaluation across five RAG benchmarks; the remaining experimental details are cut off in the batch text.
YuF0QT9OI7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the formulation principled and the theory clean, with a useful view of the trade-off between human supervision, pretrained-distribution compatibility and faithfulness.
YuF0QT9OI7.main_concern: The final objective (Equation 4) reduces to instance-weighted SFT, a form of reward-weighted regression that the paper does not position or compare against, and the static weights are not empirically validated as the model drifts.

zNMUu0NUQx.one_liner: 4-bit post-training quantization for video diffusion transformers using propagated-error sensitivity and activation-subspace code edits.
zNMUu0NUQx.problem: Local reconstruction error is an incomplete predictor of final impact, because quantization errors in video diffusion transformers are amplified or attenuated by later denoising updates.
zNMUu0NUQx.method: Isolated block-step interventions estimate propagation risk, which prioritizes sensitive trajectory states when selecting row radii. With radii fixed, response-subspace correction uses neighboring-code edits to reduce residual components along dominant activation directions while keeping the original 4-bit weight format.
zNMUu0NUQx.key_idea: Select quantization row radii by measured multi-step propagated error from isolated block-timestep pulses, then edit neighboring weight codes along dominant activation directions.
zNMUu0NUQx.evidence: Controlled interventions show short-horizon propagated error predicts final latent error better than immediate block-output error; evaluated on Wan models, Self Forcing and MiniMax-H3.
zNMUu0NUQx.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports better key consistency and dense-reference metrics, and competitive other attributes, without numbers)
zNMUu0NUQx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the local-to-global error mismatch is a meaningful problem and that the two-stage offline method preserves the 4-bit weight format, with broad evaluation across several generators.
zNMUu0NUQx.main_concern: The contribution of propagation-guided weighting is not isolated from a generic radius search on top of OrbitQuant, gains over the strongest baseline are mixed, and simulated-codebook quality tables are not tied to the deployed packed NVFP4 timing.

uVTqeLYYqq.one_liner: Training-free time-series diffusion constraint sampling via trajectory-level adjoint control parameterized in Fourier and wavelet subspaces.
uVTqeLYYqq.problem: Guidance- and projection-based constrained sampling enforce constraints only locally at each diffusion step, which is suboptimal in path space with a first-order error in the guidance direction that no guidance weight removes.
uVTqeLYYqq.method: Constrained sampling is reformulated as trajectory-level stochastic optimal control, and TTC applies an inference-time adjoint scheme with the control parameterized in Fourier and wavelet subspaces. A single backward pass estimates the first-order term of the optimal control, extra iterations tighten it, and a terminal projection supplies exact feasibility.
uVTqeLYYqq.key_idea: Backpropagate the terminal constraint through the remaining sampler to get a trajectory-level control, restricted to Fourier and wavelet subspaces, instead of per-step local guidance or projection.
uVTqeLYYqq.evidence: Experiments on four datasets with multiple constraint types, ablations on the control parameterization (Table 4), and a theorem (Theorem 4.1) bounding the effect of projecting the optimal control.
uVTqeLYYqq.claimed_gains: TTC reaches exact constraint satisfaction with the best distributional quality among compared methods on four datasets, while running up to an order of magnitude (comparison cut off in the abstract).
uVTqeLYYqq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the trajectory-level optimal-control view of constrained sampling is useful and that the Fourier and wavelet parameterization gives a practical time-series bias supported by ablations and results across datasets.
uVTqeLYYqq.main_concern: The theory does not establish posterior correctness or a controlled approximation for the proposed adjoint algorithm, and Theorem 4.1 only bounds projection error without showing the Fourier or wavelet subspace captures the optimal control.

8lU2VdpD18.one_liner: Label-diffusion ultrasound classifier conditioned on adaptively selected wavelet high-frequency features, aligned to noisy label and timestep.
8lU2VdpD18.problem: Label diffusion classifiers learn frequency information only implicitly from deep semantic conditioning, even though ultrasound high-frequency responses mix fine anatomy with speckle and acquisition variation.
8lU2VdpD18.method: WDFNet adds wavelet-reconstructed high-frequency evidence to the image guidance pathway. An Adaptive Frequency Guide selects complementary frequency responses by semantic context, and a Frequency Alignment Module adjusts the fused condition according to the current noisy label, diffusion timestep and auxiliary class prior.
8lU2VdpD18.key_idea: Condition label diffusion on wavelet high-frequency features chosen by semantic context, then modulate the fused condition by noisy label, timestep and class prior.
8lU2VdpD18.evidence: Experiments on six medical image datasets, with repeated runs, capacity-matched controls, fixed fusion controls, paired label-noise analyses and controlled corruption experiments.
8lU2VdpD18.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports consistent improvements over evaluated discriminative and diffusion-based classifiers on six datasets without numbers)
8lU2VdpD18.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written, evaluated on six datasets with thorough ablations, and that the frequency design is well matched to ultrasound.
8lU2VdpD18.main_concern: Evidence strength is limited: baseline numbers are copied from prior papers, most datasets use a single run without significance testing, FAM novelty is not isolated, and it is unclear that label diffusion is needed rather than a simple classifier on the same features.

YUUe0ur1Re.one_liner: Frozen-WAM residual adapter that aligns future-induced action deltas with beneficial ones, plus a gate, to fix negative transfer.
YUUe0ur1Re.problem: In World Action Models, generated visual futures barely change average success but add 1.7-1.9x inference latency and cause concentrated future-induced negative transfer on a few tasks.
YUUe0ur1Re.method: A residual adapter on a frozen shared WAM aligns induced velocity deltas with beneficial ones. Reviews also describe a gate, trained from an action-MSE utility label, that routes between future-conditioned and corrected paths.
YUUe0ur1Re.key_idea: Train a residual adapter on a frozen WAM so the future-conditioned action delta matches beneficial deltas, repairing harmful future influence without discarding long-horizon benefit.
YUUe0ur1Re.evidence: Analysis of one shared WAM checkpoint on LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0 (task-level deltas, independent FAST-WAM variants), with ablations of the adapter and gate.
YUUe0ur1Re.claimed_gains: Method gains are cut off in the abstract; it reports uncorrected losses of 54.0 and 34.0 points on Press Stapler and Place Can Basket, which a review says correction reduces to 6 and 14 points.
YUUe0ur1Re.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the task-level diagnosis of future-induced negative transfer, under a controlled same-checkpoint comparison, is the most useful contribution, and that the adapter is lightweight with clear ablations.
YUUe0ur1Re.main_concern: The negative-transfer finding rests on one shared checkpoint with failures concentrated on two tasks, the cause of the failures is not explained, and the action-MSE gate label may not predict closed-loop task success.

El1mIjDbGj.one_liner: Autoregressive VLA with a multi-scale residual action tokenizer whose scales are supervised by coarse-to-fine trajectory targets.
El1mIjDbGj.problem: Existing action tokenizers impose an ordering or multi-scale grouping but do not align each token group with the trajectory structure it should represent, and fine-grained tokens make autoregressive sequences long.
El1mIjDbGj.method: A multi-scale residual tokenizer is trained with a multi-scale trajectory refinement (MTR) objective that aligns cumulative reconstructions with targets at progressively finer temporal resolutions. A policy then predicts the token groups autoregressively across scales and in parallel within each scale.
El1mIjDbGj.key_idea: Give each tokenizer scale its own trajectory reconstruction target at a finer temporal resolution, so early tokens carry coarse motion and later tokens add local detail.
El1mIjDbGj.evidence: Two simulation benchmarks (LIBERO, RoboCasa-GR1) and a real-world insertion task, with supervision ablations against StarVLA baselines.
El1mIjDbGj.claimed_gains: TrajScale-VLA outperforms all compared StarVLA baselines (success figures cut off in the abstract); a review reports 59.8% versus 50.8% without MTR on RoboCasa-GR1.
El1mIjDbGj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that giving each scale its own trajectory target is a clear, sensible idea, that the supervision ablation is the strongest evidence, and that RoboCasa-GR1 and real-robot results are encouraging.
El1mIjDbGj.main_concern: The method is seen as incremental (existing multi-scale quantization plus a new objective), and evidence is thin: small LIBERO gains, few real-world trials, no seeds or confidence intervals, and baselines from different training setups.

hT5MpfcmG8.one_liner: Allocates sparse attention and compresses KV history for spacetime autoregressive video using shared post-correction output residuals.
hT5MpfcmG8.problem: Spacetime autoregressive video models concentrate attention cost at late high-resolution scales and accumulate a persistent KV cache, and attention sparsification and KV compression are usually optimized with different proxy objectives.
hT5MpfcmG8.method: Output-Sensitive Routing (OSR) allocates token-level attention using a proxy for post-correction residual risk after a cheap pooled correction replaces omitted attention. Residual-Interaction Quantization (RIQ) preserves pooled statistics and fits low-bit history representations to residual K-V interactions.
hT5MpfcmG8.key_idea: Treat the output residual left unexplained by the pooled-corrected approximate attention as the shared quantity for both attention routing and low-bit KV fitting.
hT5MpfcmG8.evidence: Evaluated on InfinityStar with end-to-end latency measurements, local attention-error analyses, and comparisons with KIVI and QVG.
hT5MpfcmG8.claimed_gains: OSR achieves up to 1.86x end-to-end on InfinityStar; the rest of the abstract, including RIQ results, is cut off.
hT5MpfcmG8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the operator-aware view, using the residual after pooled correction rather than attention mass or tensor error, is well motivated and backed by substantial implementation and evaluation effort.
hT5MpfcmG8.main_concern: The end-to-end contribution of interaction-aware fitting is not isolated, kernel optimizations differ across compared baselines, and comparisons with closest alternatives such as SVG-EAR and SparSTAR are missing.

2kGnKikg38.one_liner: Post-training adapter that gives a frozen diffusion macro placer new spatial priors from target layout samples.
2kGnKikg38.problem: Spatial preferences inherited by pretrained diffusion macro placers may not match target design objectives.
2kGnKikg38.method: Spatial Prior Adaptation adjusts how features of the current layout enter graph message passing and feature fusion, updating 3.03% of parameters with the backbone frozen. Minkowski Guided Refinement reduces residual geometric conflicts, and size-adaptive constraint evaluation speeds inference on large circuits.
2kGnKikg38.key_idea: Adapt how current-layout features enter graph message passing and feature fusion in a frozen pretrained placer, using target context-placement samples and about 3% trainable parameters.
2kGnKikg38.evidence: Comparisons against a matched pipeline without SPA, controls that hold circuit context fixed and change only target coordinates, and routing and post-route results among evaluated methods.
2kGnKikg38.claimed_gains: Updates only 3.03% of parameters, improves downstream outcomes relative to the matched pipeline without SPA, and is competitive on routing and post-route performance (no further numbers stated).
2kGnKikg38.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that post-training a placer on high-quality placements to target real PPA beyond HPWL is practical, and that matched controls show SPA changes the learned spatial behavior.
2kGnKikg38.main_concern: Novelty is seen as incremental (residual adapters, LoRA, synthetic data), and data quality and cost, sensitivity to poor samples, generalization to unseen real chips, and runtime versus DREAMPlace and commercial tools are not established.

Xfg1WuXpGO.one_liner: Sketch-to-CAD generation that recovers backward construction states, decodes forward to CAD sequences, and redraws erroneous operations.
Xfg1WuXpGO.problem: Raster-sketch CAD generation either needs stroke recovery or lacks intermediate-state context, so errors accumulate and produce invalid geometry.
Xfg1WuXpGO.method: CAD Construction Process Recovery (CCPR) recursively recovers preceding-state features from the final input to an empty state, then decodes adjacent-state transitions forward into a parametric CAD sequence. Error-Aware Redrawing (EAR) detects and locally redraws erroneous operations and optimizes sketch parameters under predicted geometric constraints.
Xfg1WuXpGO.key_idea: Formulate sketch-to-CAD as construction-process recovery: supervise backward intermediate-state features, decode forward transitions, and locally redraw operations flagged as erroneous.
Xfg1WuXpGO.evidence: Experiments on DeepCAD and Fusion 360, with cross-dataset and hand-drawn evaluations and ablations of backward recovery and state supervision.
Xfg1WuXpGO.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports accurate, executable and geometrically consistent CAD models without numbers)
Xfg1WuXpGO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the backward state recovery plus forward decoding is a well-motivated design that outperforms compared methods on DeepCAD and Fusion 360 and improves geometric validity.
Xfg1WuXpGO.main_concern: Evaluation details and baseline adaptations (shared DINOv2 encoder, Free2CAD keeping stroke access) are not specified well enough to verify the comparisons, and scope is limited to sketch-and-extrude with only parallel and perpendicular constraints.

EqeZPgXnAr.one_liner: Pixel-space diffusion model that expands channels and resolution progressively, using coarse attention maps to pre-sparsify fine-scale global attention.
EqeZPgXnAr.problem: Pixel diffusion models either lose detail with large-patch tokenization or refine only within patches, which limits cross-boundary continuity and long-range token interaction.
EqeZPgXnAr.method: PixSGR starts from a supervised low-channel bottleneck and progressively expands channel dimensionality and spatial resolution. At the spatial refinement stage, coarse-scale attention maps preselect globally relevant interactions to sparsify fine-scale attention.
EqeZPgXnAr.key_idea: Use coarse-scale attention maps to select which fine-scale token interactions to compute, giving non-local refinement without dense quadratic attention.
EqeZPgXnAr.evidence: ImageNet experiments at 256x256 and 512x512 with ablations; reviews cite comparisons with pixel-space baselines such as AsymFlow, FrequencyBooster and PixelDiT.
EqeZPgXnAr.claimed_gains: Achieves an FID of 1.51 on ImageNet (abstract cut off); reviews report 1.51 at 256x256 and 1.60 at 512x512.
EqeZPgXnAr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the coarse-guided sparse attention is a reasonable way to add cross-patch interaction at controlled cost, with strong ImageNet results at two resolutions and comprehensive ablations.
EqeZPgXnAr.main_concern: The gain from sparse global refinement is not isolated from training-recipe choices (LPIPS, REPA, internal guidance), same-recipe baseline controls are missing, and SiD2 with lower FID is absent from the results table.

vZ4upwJomY.one_liner: Zero-shot defense against adversarial camouflage on depth estimation: localize camouflage masks, then reconstruct vehicle textures with edge-guided diffusion.
vZ4upwJomY.problem: Existing defenses target imperceptible perturbations or localized patches and fail against full-surface adversarial camouflage textures on vehicles in monocular depth estimation.
vZ4upwJomY.method: A low-confidence-threshold detector finds candidate vehicles, then semantic-aware localization and multi-domain texture anomaly localization produce camouflage masks. A geometry-guided diffusion model conditioned on vehicle edges reconstructs textures, and boundary-aware blending merges them into the image.
vZ4upwJomY.key_idea: Localize camouflage by combining semantic and texture-anomaly cues, then inpaint the masked vehicle surface with edge-conditioned diffusion to restore texture without distorting geometry.
vZ4upwJomY.evidence: Experiments across six depth models and four attacks (per reviews), with ablations of masking versus reconstruction and an adaptive-attack test.
vZ4upwJomY.claimed_gains: Reduces vehicle-region depth discrepancy by 84.5% (comparison cut off in the abstract; a review says this figure is for the masking variant versus no defense).
vZ4upwJomY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the full-surface vehicle camouflage threat is realistic and relevant, and that combining semantic and texture-anomaly localization with reconstruction is a clear and thoroughly evaluated pipeline.
