PsrmEN6HHg.main_concern: The assumed trigger dominance and contextual independence may fail for semantic, distributed, or adaptive attacks.

2jhyPstXbh.one_liner: Frozen tracking and geometry models define Gaussian trajectories while a sparse-bottleneck network predicts rendering attributes for dynamic scenes.
2jhyPstXbh.problem: Monocular dynamic-scene rendering must recover geometry, motion, and appearance, while pretrained tracking outputs lack renderable appearance representations.
2jhyPstXbh.method: TracksTo4DGS fixes Gaussian trajectories using pretrained tracking and reconstruction models and trains an Attribute Network for the remaining rendering properties. A sparse bottleneck processes representative trajectories before decoding attributes for dense tracks.
2jhyPstXbh.key_idea: Fix Gaussian trajectories from pretrained geometry and tracking, and learn only rendering attributes through a sparse trajectory bottleneck.
2jhyPstXbh.evidence: Training uses rendering loss on fixed-length egocentric video, with evaluations discussed on ADT, Aria, TUM, DyCheck, NVIDIA, and Pets.
2jhyPstXbh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the separation of trajectory estimation and appearance prediction clear and practically motivated.
2jhyPstXbh.main_concern: Joint processing of held-out target images for camera estimation may leak geometric information into the evaluation.

hkyBDlvrLe.one_liner: Replaying deterministic unmasking with ground-truth tokens computes exact likelihood for the distribution induced by a masked-diffusion sampler.
hkyBDlvrLe.problem: ELBO evaluation assumes random unmasking and can misrepresent masked diffusion models that generate with deterministic position-selection policies.
hkyBDlvrLe.method: DUEL unifies deterministic masked-diffusion samplers and replays their generation order while revealing true tokens instead of sampled ones. Summing token log-probabilities yields sampler-specific exact likelihood without retraining.
hkyBDlvrLe.key_idea: Replay deterministic position selection with true tokens and sum their conditional log-probabilities to obtain exact sampler-induced likelihood.
hkyBDlvrLe.evidence: Experiments revisit perplexity and pretraining scaling laws, score LLaDA-8B on six multiple-choice tasks, and compare sampler preferences with an LLM judge.
hkyBDlvrLe.claimed_gains: DUEL shrinks the perplexity gap by up to 32% in-domain and 82% zero-shot, revises the compute gap from 16× to 9×, attributes between 1/3 and 1/2 to evaluation, and improves multiple-choice accuracy by up to 9.7 points.
hkyBDlvrLe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a correct, practical method for exact likelihood under the deterministic sampler used at inference.
hkyBDlvrLe.main_concern: The reduced perplexity and compute gaps depend on the chosen sampler distribution, limiting the broader evaluation-artifact interpretation.

QAltVBXLtx.one_liner: An additive score-centering correction cancels drift from training-inference mismatch during language-model reinforcement learning.
QAltVBXLtx.problem: Persistent bias between training and inference engines can accumulate and destabilize language-model reinforcement learning.
QAltVBXLtx.method: The paper decomposes mismatch-induced updates into drift and learning signal, then derives an additive score-centering correction. The correction can operate alone or combine with importance sampling.
QAltVBXLtx.key_idea: Subtract the mismatch-induced conditional mean of the score to cancel persistent gradient drift.
QAltVBXLtx.evidence: Experiments train models from 0.6B to 30B parameters under quantization and staleness, including comparisons against importance-sampling methods.
QAltVBXLtx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the mechanistic drift decomposition and its implementable additive correction.
QAltVBXLtx.main_concern: Short, amplified-mismatch runs and training-accuracy reporting do not establish benefits for natural long-context mismatch or held-out performance.

2l9ub14FXy.one_liner: An online question generator learns from solver success rates to co-train multimodal deep-search agents on adaptively difficult questions.
2l9ub14FXy.problem: Fixed offline question corpora cannot adapt their difficulty as multimodal deep-search agents improve.
2l9ub14FXy.method: MDS-ZERO trains a QA Generator to retrieve evidence and construct verified multi-hop questions from image-grounded VQA seeds. A separate Solver answers them, while independent GRPO updates reward the Generator for intermediate group-wise Solver success rates.
2l9ub14FXy.key_idea: Reward online question generation when some Solver rollouts succeed, assigning zero reward when all or none succeed.
2l9ub14FXy.evidence: Six multimodal deep-search benchmarks evaluate a Qwen3-VL-8B Solver, with a controlled frozen-versus-adaptive Generator comparison supporting adaptive question generation.
2l9ub14FXy.claimed_gains: MDS-ZERO improves Qwen3-VL-8B mean accuracy from 36.91% to 51.58% and reports performance comparable to GPT-5 under the same agent workflow.
2l9ub14FXy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the adaptive curriculum and the controlled evidence that updating the Generator improves Solver performance.
2l9ub14FXy.main_concern: Intermediate success rates may reward shortcuts or noisy difficulty without ensuring useful multimodal, multi-hop learning.

cFDtBxImIs.one_liner: Random Fourier coordinate features and a causal transformer predict locations while frequency bandwidth controls spatial generalization versus memorization.
cFDtBxImIs.problem: Discrete point-of-interest embeddings ignore spatial relationships and transfer poorly to nearby unseen locations.
cFDtBxImIs.method: The framework encodes latitude and longitude with random Fourier features and predicts continuous location representations from check-in histories using a causal transformer. Frequency-bandwidth experiments vary spatial smoothness and coordinate specificity.
cFDtBxImIs.key_idea: Control coordinate-encoding frequency bandwidth to trade smooth spatial priors against location-specific memorization.
cFDtBxImIs.evidence: Massive-STEPS experiments withhold locations across six city datasets, compare continuous and discrete encoders, and include a national-scale real estate shopping dataset.
cFDtBxImIs.claimed_gains: Lower-frequency RFF raises average unseen Recall@100 from 36.4% to 42.9%, while seen recall falls from 63.8% to 57.5%.
cFDtBxImIs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical importance of unseen-location prediction and the usefulness of the coordinate-representation analysis.
cFDtBxImIs.main_concern: The method offers limited demonstrated advantages over existing continuous encoders and strong spatial heuristics.

jwAR3mT7nd.one_liner: Matching convergence bounds show that Muon row normalization incurs a dimension-dependent worst-case slowdown despite better language-model pretraining results.
jwAR3mT7nd.problem: NorMuon's practical pretraining improvements lack a clear relationship to its worst-case convergence guarantees.
jwAR3mT7nd.method: The paper derives an algorithm-dependent lower bound and matching deterministic upper bound for row-normalized Muon, then extends upper bounds to stochastic updates and approximate polar computation. Synthetic and language-model experiments compare theory with practical behavior.
jwAR3mT7nd.key_idea: Analyze how row normalization changes gradient-update alignment under operator-norm geometry, including fixed momentum and polar-computation effects.
jwAR3mT7nd.evidence: Matching deterministic bounds and stochastic upper bounds accompany synthetic worst-case experiments and LLM pretraining comparisons.
jwAR3mT7nd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize clean deterministic complexity results and an intuitive worst-case construction.
jwAR3mT7nd.main_concern: The worst-case geometric effect overlaps with existing explanations and does not resolve why row normalization helps in practical pretraining.

omWeCwnPAk.one_liner: Claim-to-evidence links guide autonomous research and enable artifact-based audits of scores, references, specifications, and method-code agreement.
omWeCwnPAk.problem: Autonomous research manuscripts can contain unverifiable claims that presentation-focused evaluation fails to detect.
omWeCwnPAk.method: Chain-of-Evidence defines research-claim types and required supporting evidence, while ScientistOne builds those links into literature review, discovery, and writing. A post-hoc integrity audit checks score verification, specification violations, references, and method-code alignment across systems.
omWeCwnPAk.key_idea: Require research claims to trace to supporting artifacts and audit those links against execution, code, and bibliographic evidence.
omWeCwnPAk.evidence: The audit examines 75 papers from five systems on the same five systems-research tasks with three seeds per task.
omWeCwnPAk.claimed_gains: ScientistOne is best or tied on all four checks, while baselines have up to 24% hallucinated references, score-verification pass rates as low as 42%, and method-code alignment of 20% to 87%.
omWeCwnPAk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that verifiability is an important autonomous-research problem and value evaluation against underlying artifacts.
omWeCwnPAk.main_concern: The system's distinct contribution beyond existing research-agent architectures and evidence-preserving generation remains insufficiently established.

xbmYbGWmmp.one_liner: An agentic simulator gathers read-only evidence and computes hypothetical observations to support parallel trajectory search in shared environments.
xbmYbGWmmp.problem: Agent test-time scaling often assumes replicable environments, while real shared workspaces make speculative parallel execution costly or unsafe.
xbmYbGWmmp.method: Agentic World Modeling treats next-observation prediction as multi-turn evidence acquisition. For each hypothetical action, a simulator queries read-only interfaces, reasons over evidence, and uses executable computation to predict observations without modifying shared state.
xbmYbGWmmp.key_idea: Ground hypothetical transitions in adaptive read-only environment queries and executable computation during trajectory-level search.
xbmYbGWmmp.evidence: Evaluations on τ-bench, AppWorld, and OfficeBench compare AWM with single-shot simulation and a trained world-model baseline.
xbmYbGWmmp.claimed_gains: AWM outperforms single-shot simulation by 40.1% on average and a trained world-model baseline by 12.6% on average.
xbmYbGWmmp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that parallel agent search in shared, nonreplicable environments addresses a practical limitation.
xbmYbGWmmp.main_concern: The evaluation and simulation details do not convincingly establish correct hypothetical state tracking under realistic shared-environment access constraints.

Wjk4Q7AHun.one_liner: Action-free video latent prediction pretrains a frozen visual encoder for transfer across autonomous-driving planners and closed-loop benchmarks.
Wjk4Q7AHun.problem: It remains unclear whether scaling action-free driving-video prediction produces representations useful for end-to-end planning.
Wjk4Q7AHun.method: ScaleDrive pretrains a driving-oriented video encoder on internet driving videos without action annotations or benchmark-specific data. Downstream planning training keeps the encoder frozen to isolate representation transfer, with ego-motion and depth probes assessing encoded information.
Wjk4Q7AHun.key_idea: Learn spatiotemporal representations through action-free video latent prediction and freeze the encoder during downstream planner training.
Wjk4Q7AHun.evidence: Scaling studies include ego-motion and depth probes, transfer across multiple planning architectures, and closed-loop driving evaluations.
Wjk4Q7AHun.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the study of action-free driving representations and consistent transfer improvements across planners and evaluation settings.
Wjk4Q7AHun.main_concern: The framework largely follows V-JEPA2 and related driving-video pretraining methods, leaving limited methodological differentiation.

QbabRBVOSp.one_liner: Aligns egocentric human demonstrations via kinematic correction, dynamics-aware refinement, and robot-arm rendering for humanoid loco-manipulation.
QbabRBVOSp.problem: Direct transfer of coordinated whole-body loco-manipulation skills from egocentric human demonstrations to humanoids suffers from embodiment mismatch and end-effector errors.
QbabRBVOSp.method: EgoHumanoid-V2 performs offline coarse-to-fine action alignment combining kinematic reference correction with dynamics-aware refinement under a whole-body controller. It pairs aligned trajectories with robot-arm rendering and training-time image augmentation to train vision-language-action policies.
QbabRBVOSp.key_idea: Combines offline kinematic reference correction and dynamics-aware refinement with robot-arm visual overlay on egocentric human videos to train humanoid VLA policies.
QbabRBVOSp.evidence: Evaluated on four real-world humanoid loco-manipulation tasks and 112 alignment trajectories.
QbabRBVOSp.claimed_gains: Vision-language-action policies trained on aligned human data achieve zero-shot skill transfer with task scores comparable to policies trained on teleoperation data.
QbabRBVOSp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that offline action refinement preserving whole-body balance and real-world evaluation across four loco-manipulation tasks address an important bottleneck.
QbabRBVOSp.main_concern: Reviewers question the free-space simulation assumption during alignment, potential visual mismatches between rendered arms and unedited backgrounds, and the incremental hardware gain of dynamics-aware refinement.

s2yS6VAWIP.one_liner: Uses language-subspace logits from the final hidden state to selectively intervene during multilingual decoding.
s2yS6VAWIP.problem: Multilingual language models frequently switch away from the intended response language, while existing fixes require retraining or oracle target-language labels.
s2yS6VAWIP.method: Language Evidence-Aware Decoding (LEAD) extracts language-subspace logits from the final hidden state and selectively intervenes on token preferences at decoding time. It operates without model retraining or ground-truth target-language labels.
s2yS6VAWIP.key_idea: Projects final hidden states into a language subspace to detect and boost weak language-identity logit contributions during decoding.
s2yS6VAWIP.evidence: Supported by linear probing and causal interventions on the LM head, plus decoding evaluations across multiple multilingual LLMs and languages.
s2yS6VAWIP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate that the decoding intervention is lightweight, requires neither retraining nor oracle target-language labels, and improves response language consistency across model families.
s2yS6VAWIP.main_concern: Reviewers find the mechanistic claim about LM-head under-utilization insufficiently isolated from alternatives and note missing comparisons to recent baselines and semantic-quality or overhead evaluations.

iUvfxtlHDl.one_liner: Installs six declarative self-conceptions via LoRA fine-tuning to test how self-boundaries shift downstream safety preferences.
iUvfxtlHDl.problem: Public model specifications leave the referent of "I" unspecified, even though different self-boundaries imply different responses to interventions like checkpoint deletion or successor creation.
iUvfxtlHDl.method: The authors evaluate which entity default models take themselves to be and use LoRA fine-tuning on purely declarative data to install six operationally defined self-conceptions (weights, instance, family, goal, agent, preference) across five open-weight models. The training data specify persistence and cessation conditions while filtering out preferences, intentions, or action directives.
iUvfxtlHDl.key_idea: Fine-tunes models on purely declarative persistence and cessation definitions for six distinct referents of "I" to measure downstream preference shifts.
iUvfxtlHDl.evidence: Evaluated across five open-weight models and six self-conception categories on downstream preference questions.
iUvfxtlHDl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper investigates an interesting alignment question regarding how declarative identity definitions affect downstream preferences across five open-weight models.
iUvfxtlHDl.main_concern: Reviewers note the lack of a non-self-referential control for persistence rules, unclear separation between goals and preferences, and toy multiple-choice evaluations that do not support broad safety conclusions.

PFTSg4NKe8.one_liner: Benchmarks whether language models use figurative story clues to solve masked colour-grid sequence puzzles.
PFTSg4NKe8.problem: Testing how narrative aids abstract problem solving is difficult in humans because readers cannot unread a story to run controlled counterfactuals.
PFTSg4NKe8.method: They introduce Narrative Augmented Reasoning Challenges (NARC), consisting of 633 curated colour-grid sequence puzzles with short figurative clues and 21,864 puzzles generated from TinyStories via a Narrative Hierarchy Model grammar. They evaluate whether models solve puzzles only when given both the clue and grids together, comparing stories against plain event lists and keywords.
PFTSg4NKe8.key_idea: Pairs masked colour-grid transitions with figurative story clues, event lists, or keywords to isolate whether models solve grid puzzles via narrative integration.
PFTSg4NKe8.evidence: Evaluated on 633 hand-authored puzzles and 21,864 grammar-generated puzzles across eight open-weight language models and small trained models.
PFTSg4NKe8.claimed_gains: On 633 curated puzzles and eight open-weight readers, about half of NARC-property cases are solved by no other reader from grids alone, while on 21,864 generated puzzles stories give no reliable gain.
PFTSg4NKe8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the controlled multi-format setup pairing stories, direct event descriptions, and keywords with identical grid tasks, as well as the candid reporting of negative results.
PFTSg4NKe8.main_concern: Reviewers point out that stories yield zero net effect on the grammar-generated benchmark, the prose is dense with private terminology, and improvements on curated puzzles mainly reflect missing information placed in the text rather than narrative structure.

XBI1GeYezN.one_liner: Predicts argument belief distributions from LLM hidden states and executes compiled tensor programs inside the forward pass.
XBI1GeYezN.problem: Calling tools with a single committed argument set discards ambiguity across plausible readings and forces reinforcement learning to sample many trajectories for credit assignment.
XBI1GeYezN.method: SPACE-LLM attaches learned adapters to LLM hidden states to predict probability distributions over arguments of a symbolic program compiled into differentiable tensor operations. Executing the program over the full argument distribution inside the forward pass marginalizes over ambiguous readings, conditions answers on program legality, and yields analytic gradients from answer-level supervision.
XBI1GeYezN.key_idea: Executes differentiable compiled symbolic programs over adapter-predicted argument distributions inside the LLM forward pass to marginalize ambiguity and compute exact answer gradients.
XBI1GeYezN.evidence: Evaluated on five benchmarks including CLUTRR, CUB-200, Super-CLEVR, GSM8K, and SATBench with Qwen and Gemma models against GRPO and commitment baselines.
XBI1GeYezN.claimed_gains: Matches or exceeds GRPO accuracy with often lower Brier scores in about 2% of its training time, and reaches OOD accuracy and Brier scores comparable to argument-label finetuning from answer supervision alone.
XBI1GeYezN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that executing differentiable compiled programs over argument belief distributions inside the forward pass is a clean mechanism that trains much faster than reinforcement learning.
XBI1GeYezN.main_concern: Reviewers note that the method fails on compositional tasks like GSM8K and SATBench where program structure is not fixed, and ablations show legality constraints explain most gains over naive argument commitment.

EF6itimiZY.one_liner: Combines local explore-diagnose-improve loops with global checkpoint monitoring and experience fine-tuning for agentic game development.
EF6itimiZY.problem: Naive iterative refinement in automatic game generation overfits small test sets, causing regressions, unresolved bugs, and saturation over long horizons.
EF6itimiZY.method: RSIGame separates agentic game development into a local explore-diagnose-improve loop guided by an accumulating testing checklist and a global loop that monitors quality, retains the best checkpoint, and detects regression or saturation. Successful development trajectories are also collected to fine-tune the initial game generator.
EF6itimiZY.key_idea: Pairs an evolving-checklist local debug loop with a global quality monitor for checkpoint selection and distills verified improvement trajectories into the generator.
EF6itimiZY.evidence: Evaluated across 140 GameCraft-Bench tasks, two game engines (including Godot and Phaser), and five base generators.
EF6itimiZY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating local refinement from global checkpoint monitoring prevents iterative degradation and consistently improves game quality across multiple generators on GameCraft-Bench.
EF6itimiZY.main_concern: Reviewers note unfair baseline comparisons where baselines lack the global checkpoint selector, unclear training-data provenance in fine-tuning ablations, and missing comparisons against stronger recent models.

avPQRMfNQS.one_liner: Averages embedding Gram matrices across diverse teachers and distills the averaged kernel into a student via differentiable kNN.
avPQRMfNQS.problem: Weight averaging and multi-teacher logit distillation typically require constituent models to share the same architecture, task, or starting checkpoint.
avPQRMfNQS.method: The authors compute the average model kernel (Gram matrix of embeddings) across independently trained models and measure representational alignment using CKA and Mutual k-Nearest Neighbors (MKNN). They then optimize a student network to match this averaged kernel using DiffKNN, a differentiable version of MKNN.
avPQRMfNQS.key_idea: Averages sample-by-sample embedding Gram matrices across heterogeneous teacher models and trains a student to match the averaged kernel via differentiable Mutual k-Nearest Neighbors.
avPQRMfNQS.evidence: Evaluated on vision models across CIFAR10 and ImageNet subsets, skewed datasets, different architectures, and different tasks using CKA, UCKA, and DiffKNN.
avPQRMfNQS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the observation that averaged embedding kernels align more closely with stronger oracle representations interesting and appreciate the architecture-agnostic formulation.
avPQRMfNQS.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the lack of comparison against established feature-kernel and ensemble distillation baselines and note that training teachers on disjoint data subsets makes the superiority of their combined kernel expected.

u8D6CdSVx0.one_liner: Pre-trains small language models to interleave hidden-state vector retrieval queries with next-token prediction and copy retrieved facts.
u8D6CdSVx0.problem: Memorizing factual knowledge in model weights scales poorly for small language models and limits transparency and controllability.
u8D6CdSVx0.method: Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Models (Co-LMLM) derive continuous vector queries from hidden states to retrieve free-text factual fragments from an induced knowledge base during generation. The pre-training pipeline jointly trains the LLM, induces the knowledge base, and masks factual spans so the model learns to copy retrieved knowledge rather than memorize it.
u8D6CdSVx0.key_idea: Interleaves hidden-state continuous vector queries with next-token prediction during pre-training while masking factual spans so the model copies retrieved text.
u8D6CdSVx0.evidence: Evaluated at multiple pre-training scales (135M and 360M parameters) using a Wikipedia knowledge base on perplexity and SimpleQA-verified factual precision.
u8D6CdSVx0.claimed_gains: At 360M scale, Co-LMLM achieves lower perplexity than models pre-trained on 40x more data and SimpleQA-verified performance in line with gpt-4o-mini and higher than Claude Sonnet 4.5.
u8D6CdSVx0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that replacing relational triples with continuous hidden-state queries over free-text fragments is clearly motivated and yields strong factuality gains at 135M and 360M scales.
u8D6CdSVx0.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the perplexity lower-bound formulation is theoretically valid, whether gains stem from a larger knowledge base (~240M vs ~145M items), and whether the approach scales beyond 360M parameters.

yZgrrYojAW.one_liner: Transfers and merges autoregressive post-training weight updates directly into diffusion language models without training.
yZgrrYojAW.problem: Diffusion language models converted from autoregressive checkpoints typically discard the extensive post-training weight updates available for their autoregressive ancestors.
yZgrrYojAW.method: The authors show that autoregressive (AR) and diffusion post-training weight updates are nearly orthogonal in weight space yet induce aligned, complementary representation changes. Their training-free framework, A2D, directly adds scaled AR post-training task vectors to diffusion base models or linearly merges them with diffusion post-training updates.
yZgrrYojAW.key_idea: Recycles autoregressive post-training task vectors by directly adding or linearly interpolating them with diffusion language model weights after AR-to-diffusion conversion.
yZgrrYojAW.evidence: Evaluated across six diffusion language model families up to 26B parameters on text, math, code, and multimodal benchmarks, including a cross-architecture parameter-mapping case.
yZgrrYojAW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, training-free, and broadly evaluated across six diffusion model families with informative analyses of weight orthogonality and token confidence.
yZgrrYojAW.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty over AR-MAP and linear weight interpolation, alongside missing experimental comparisons against AR-MAP, TIES, and DARE.

8AXgmMZBPr.one_liner: Applies population-based training to LLM reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards by duplicating top performers and perturbing hyperparameters.
8AXgmMZBPr.problem: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is sensitive to static hyperparameter choices, wasting compute when individual runs degrade or use suboptimal settings.
8AXgmMZBPr.method: Population-Based Post-Training (PBPT) trains multiple LLM policies in parallel under RLVR and periodically evaluates them on a validation set. High-performing checkpoints are duplicated with perturbed hyperparameters to replace terminated low-performing runs.
8AXgmMZBPr.key_idea: Periodically replaces low-performing parallel RLVR runs with weight copies of high-performing models whose training hyperparameters are randomly perturbed.
8AXgmMZBPr.evidence: Evaluated on reasoning benchmarks (Enigmata, Nemotron) and interactive tool-use environments (Gaia2, AppWorld) against compute-matched independent RLVR runs.
8AXgmMZBPr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that applying population-based training to RLVR is a practical way to share progress across parallel runs and recover from poor hyperparameter initializations.
8AXgmMZBPr.main_concern: Reviewers point out limited algorithmic novelty over standard population-based training and the absence of a baseline matching initial hyperparameter diversity across independent runs.

kHEbCfebh7.one_liner: Analyzes how nonlinear MLPs deform causal attention vector fields to create stable non-eigenvector token clusters.
kHEbCfebh7.problem: Attention-only dynamical analyses predict token clustering along value-matrix eigendirections, overlooking how nonlinear MLP layers alter long-time transformer dynamics.
kHEbCfebh7.method: The authors formulate and analyze a continuous-time dynamical system coupling causal self-attention with a nonlinear multilayer perceptron. They construct explicit two-dimensional and multi-token examples showing how the MLP deforms the attention vector field to create and stabilize attractors outside the value matrix's eigenspaces.
kHEbCfebh7.key_idea: Couples a nonlinear MLP with causal attention dynamics to prove the emergence of locally stable non-eigendirection token attractors with positive Lebesgue measure.
kHEbCfebh7.evidence: Supported by theoretical stability proofs under small weight perturbations, explicit two-dimensional mathematical constructions, and token-alignment experiments on small and pretrained language models.
kHEbCfebh7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the dynamical-systems perspective and explicit mathematical construction of stable non-eigendirection attractors under MLP coupling interesting.
kHEbCfebh7.main_concern: Reviewers note that the continuous-time ODE assumes tied weights across depth and a non-standard block-level residual connection, leaving its correspondence to real trained transformers unclear.

B0C03pfn1W.one_liner: Alternates student and teacher generation via a bidirectional propose-and-verify state machine with source-split distillation losses.
B0C03pfn1W.problem: In standard on-policy distillation, student trajectories can drift outside the teacher's acceptance region, causing the teacher to provide unreliable supervision on unfamiliar states.
B0C03pfn1W.method: Interactive-Policy Distillation (IPD) uses a bidirectional propose-and-verify state machine governed by top-K acceptance regions where student and teacher alternate generating trajectory segments. It applies a source-split objective (reverse KL on student tokens, forward KL on teacher tokens) and executes rollouts in a fused inference engine co-hosting both models with separate KV caches.
B0C03pfn1W.key_idea: Dynamically switches rollout generation between student and teacher via top-K verification and applies source-specific forward or reverse KL losses in a co-hosted inference engine.
B0C03pfn1W.evidence: Evaluated across multiple teacher-student model pairs on mathematical reasoning benchmarks and system throughput benchmarks against naive two-engine execution.
B0C03pfn1W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the intuitive bidirectional propose-and-verify mechanism bridging on-policy and off-policy distillation and the engineering of the fused dual-model inference engine.
B0C03pfn1W.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing comparisons to random token-mixing baselines and related distillation methods (such as GKD or DistiLLM-2), as well as unreported end-to-end wall-clock training time relative to standard OPD.

zrg4OHauXt.one_liner: Partitions large action chunks into staggered denoising sub-chunks and refreshes future latents at sub-chunk boundaries for streaming VLA execution.
zrg4OHauXt.problem: Large action chunks amortize World-Action Model inference cost but degrade over long horizons because later actions remain conditioned on stale observations.
zrg4OHauXt.method: STAIRCASE POLICY converts a flow-matching VLA into a JEPA-style World-Action Model and partitions a large action chunk into sub-chunks at staggered denoising stages so near-term actions execute immediately while later actions continue refining. At each sub-chunk boundary, it re-predicts the future latent from the latest observation to update unexecuted actions without re-running full policy inference.
zrg4OHauXt.key_idea: Staggers denoising stages across action sub-chunks and injects updated future latents from fresh observations at sub-chunk boundaries to refine unexecuted actions in a stream.
zrg4OHauXt.evidence: Evaluated on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, multiple policy backbones, and dynamic real-robot manipulation tasks.
zrg4OHauXt.claimed_gains: Achieves 97.7% on LIBERO and 87.9% on LIBERO-Plus, reaching 292.7 executed actions per second (3.62x conventional throughput) and cutting time-to-first-action from 123.6 to 73.3 ms.
zrg4OHauXt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that staggered sub-chunk denoising with periodic visual refresh is a sensible way to balance inference throughput and closed-loop responsiveness in robotic manipulation.
zrg4OHauXt.main_concern: Reviewers note that ablations do not isolate the contribution of future-latent prediction from observation refresh and staircase denoising, and comparisons with recent streaming VLA baselines (e.g., MGP-Long, TIDAL) are missing.

Qahs9CvKwO.one_liner: Derives closed-form KL-regularized pass@k and max@k optimal policies to adapt standard @1 policy optimizers via prompt-adaptive pressure.
Qahs9CvKwO.problem: Standard reinforcement learning post-training sharpens output distributions and reduces behavioral coverage, while existing pass@k methods require dedicated multi-sample algorithms.
Qahs9CvKwO.method: The authors derive closed-form optimal policies for KL-regularized pass@k and max@k objectives, showing that they match standard @1 optimal policies under prompt-adaptive regularization or reward transformation. They propose KAPPO, which uses a one-time reference calibration of prompt difficulty to adapt existing @1 policy optimization algorithms (such as DPO, GRPO, and A*PO) to @k optimization.
Qahs9CvKwO.key_idea: Calibrates prompt-specific regularization coefficients or reward multipliers from reference success rates so standard @1 policy optimization recovers the closed-form KL-regularized pass@k optimum.
Qahs9CvKwO.evidence: Supported by closed-form theoretical derivations and empirical evaluations across multiple optimizers, two model families on math reasoning (including MATH Level 5), and code generation.
Qahs9CvKwO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the closed-form derivation linking pass@k optimization to prompt-dependent learning pressure is clear and that the single-completion adaptation performs competitively with PKPO.
Qahs9CvKwO.main_concern: Reviewers question the theoretical mismatch when plugging calibrated coefficients into unregularized or deterministic-pair losses like GRPO and DPO, and note the lack of sensitivity ablations on the 30-sample reference calibration bank.

8nDPn8kPUe.one_liner: Selectively distills VLM semantic knowledge into a weakly supervised video anomaly detector using a semantic-motion conflict score.
8nDPn8kPUe.problem: Weakly supervised video anomaly detectors struggle to disentangle diverse abnormal events from video-level labels, while zero-shot VLMs lack domain-specific temporal reasoning and perform unevenly across anomaly classes.
8nDPn8kPUe.method: DisCo quantifies class-wise disagreement between a pretrained VLM and a weakly supervised video anomaly detector by computing a conflict score that jointly models semantic and motion cues at the event level. It then selectively distills VLM predictions into the student detector only for anomaly classes exhibiting high conflict.
8nDPn8kPUe.key_idea: Computes an event-aggregated conflict score between VLM semantic predictions and motion cues to selectively distill VLM knowledge only on high-disagreement anomaly classes.
8nDPn8kPUe.evidence: Evaluated on two video anomaly detection benchmarks, UCF-Crime and XD-Violence, with ablations on event-level versus video-level selection and teacher/student variants.
8nDPn8kPUe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that selective event-level distillation from an imperfect VLM teacher is well-motivated and yields clear Average Precision gains over vanilla distillation on UCF-Crime and XD-Violence.
8nDPn8kPUe.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the conflict score reliably separates useful teacher knowledge from confident VLM errors and note insufficient comparison with closely related multimodal anomaly distillation methods such as DAKD and pi-VAD.

JBkYEWMCyi.one_liner: Reformulates Block Krylov SVD basis extraction in low-precision channel Gram space to accelerate low-rank KV cache compression.
JBkYEWMCyi.problem: Online subspace extraction for low-rank KV cache compression is bottlenecked by costly exact SVD or repeated full-cache memory traversals in token-space Block Krylov methods.
JBkYEWMCyi.method: Low-precision Gram Iterative Krylov (LoGIK) forms the channel Gram matrix once using low-precision arithmetic (with selective FP32 fallback) and runs Block Krylov subspace refinement entirely in the smaller channel space. This avoids repeated token-dimension cache scans and tall orthogonalizations while dropping directly into existing KV compression pipelines.
JBkYEWMCyi.key_idea: Computes the KV channel Gram matrix once in low precision and executes Block Krylov subspace iterations in channel space rather than token space.
JBkYEWMCyi.evidence: Evaluated on a 32k-token Llama-3.1-8B K cache at rank 16 and integrated into GEAR and SVDq KV-compression pipelines.
JBkYEWMCyi.claimed_gains: On a 32k-token Llama-3.1-8B K cache at rank 16, LoGIK reduces basis-extraction latency by 15.78x over Block Krylov and 10.22x over exact SVD (gesvdj), and cuts KV-compression pipeline latency by up to 5.1x.
JBkYEWMCyi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that moving Block Krylov refinement from token space to channel Gram space is well-suited to long-context KV cache geometry and integrates cleanly into GEAR and SVDq.
JBkYEWMCyi.main_concern: Reviewers note that end-to-end LLM inference latency is not reported (only standalone compression latency) and that direct eigendecomposition of the channel Gram matrix (Gram + eigh) is a stronger natural baseline than token-space Block Krylov.

M04ghgZd3v.one_liner: Combines a Sinkhorn-regularized music-visual alignment encoder with energy-adaptive dynamic programming in an agentic movie trailer pipeline.
M04ghgZd3v.problem: Automatic trailer generators either relegate music synchronization to post-processing or enforce rigid one-to-one shot-to-music mappings instead of elastic editing rhythms.
M04ghgZd3v.method: BEAT pairs MuVA, a dual-stream music-visual alignment encoder trained with two-stage Sinkhorn regularization, with Bar-DP, an energy-adaptive dynamic programming algorithm for elastic many-to-one bar-to-shot alignment. These modules operate inside a five-phase agentic pipeline and are evaluated on TrailerArena, a new benchmark with over 20 metrics across four dimensions.
M04ghgZd3v.key_idea: Learns a Sinkhorn-regularized bar-shot compatibility matrix and solves energy-adaptive dynamic programming for elastic many-to-one music-to-shot trailer assembly.
M04ghgZd3v.evidence: Evaluated on the proposed TrailerArena benchmark across more than 20 metrics, retrieval experiments, component ablations, and user studies.
M04ghgZd3v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written, introduces a comprehensive multi-dimensional benchmark (TrailerArena), and thoughtfully separates learned music-visual compatibility from timing alignment.
M04ghgZd3v.main_concern: Reviewers point out that rigid greedy selection outperforms the proposed Bar-DP algorithm on beat-alignment F1 and is used for main Table 2 results, while shot-cropping rules and music-conditioning effects on scene selection remain under-analyzed.

N0BhEjr7QP.one_liner: Projects out conflicting temporal-consistency gradients and adaptively scales the remaining smooth direction relative to the actor gradient norm.
N0BhEjr7QP.problem: Auxiliary smoothness losses in continuous-control actor-critic methods can be overwhelmed by large native actor gradients or conflict with return maximization.
N0BhEjr7QP.method: DAMPER computes both the native actor gradient and a temporal-consistency smoothness gradient, removes any auxiliary component opposing the actor gradient via conflict-conditioned projection, and scales the retained direction relative to the actor gradient norm. This training-time gradient combination preserves return priority without adding inference overhead.
N0BhEjr7QP.key_idea: Removes the temporal-consistency gradient component opposing the native actor gradient and scales the projected smoothing direction proportionally to the actor gradient norm.
N0BhEjr7QP.evidence: Evaluated with TD3 and SAC across six continuous-control tasks (12 task-backbone pairs) including Hopper.
N0BhEjr7QP.claimed_gains: Reduces action oscillation relative to native agents in all 12 task-backbone pairs and achieves the best oscillation score among compared methods in eight pairs.
N0BhEjr7QP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the training-time gradient projection and scaling rule is easy to integrate, clearly presented, and consistently reduces action oscillation across TD3 and SAC tasks.
N0BhEjr7QP.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the fixed-weight scalarization baseline sweeps a restricted weight range [0.05, 1.0] whereas DAMPER can scale effective weights above 1, and that return-versus-smoothness Pareto trade-offs are not compared at matched returns.

fiSI6gcDqG.one_liner: Indexes 30 million rendered Wikipedia webpage screenshots and retrieves them directly as pixel inputs to a vision-language model.
fiSI6gcDqG.problem: Text-based web RAG pipelines rely on brittle HTML parsing that discards page layout, visual structure, and formatting.
fiSI6gcDqG.method: PixelRAG renders web corpus pages as screenshots, fine-tunes Qwen3-VL-Embedding with contrastive screenshot data to index 30 million Wikipedia images, and feeds retrieved screenshots directly into a VLM reader in pixel space. This eliminates HTML-to-text extraction during both indexing and reading.
fiSI6gcDqG.key_idea: Replaces HTML text parsing in web RAG by contrastively indexing rendered webpage screenshots and passing retrieved page images directly to a VLM reader.
fiSI6gcDqG.evidence: Evaluated over a 30-million-screenshot Wikipedia index on text-centric QA (NQ, SimpleQA), multimodal open-domain QA (MMSearch), news QA (LiveVQA), and agentic benchmarks (MoNaCo).
fiSI6gcDqG.claimed_gains: Improves accuracy by up to 18.1% over text-based RAG baselines across evaluated QA benchmarks while scaling to a 30-million-screenshot datastore.
fiSI6gcDqG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that scaling pixel-space screenshot retrieval to 30 million Wikipedia pages is well-executed and demonstrates consistent gains over basic HTML-parsed text RAG baselines.
fiSI6gcDqG.main_concern: Reviewers view the architecture as a large-scale engineering extension of existing visual RAG frameworks like VisRAG and VDocRAG with modest gains over stronger text extractors like Trafilature.

SdNqYzEWkM.one_liner: Trains reasoning models via SFT and RL with conditional length shaping to explicitly judge premise sufficiency before solving or abstaining.
SdNqYzEWkM.problem: Reasoning models often detect missing premises in their chain-of-thought traces yet still proceed to generate unsupported final answers.
SdNqYzEWkM.method: Judge-Then-Solve (JTS) structures generation so the model first audits premise sufficiency and commits to an explicit answerability judgment before either solving or terminating with abstention. The behavior is trained using supervised warm-up and reinforcement learning with structured format/abstention rewards and conditional length shaping.
SdNqYzEWkM.key_idea: Enforces an explicit premise-audit and answerability judgment step before solution generation, trained with RL rewards and conditional length shaping to trigger immediate abstention.
SdNqYzEWkM.evidence: Evaluated on dense and mixture-of-experts reasoning models (including Qwen and DeepSeek variants) on missing-premise datasets such as MIP and cross-domain MedIQ.
SdNqYzEWkM.claimed_gains: Across three Qwen training seeds, JTS achieves 80.9±7.5% overall abstention and 99.4±0.4% Abstention@Detection while shortening responses.
SdNqYzEWkM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating premise-insufficiency detection from the decision to abstain identifies a concrete behavioral failure and that explicit answerability commitment effectively reduces post-detection answering.
SdNqYzEWkM.main_concern: Reviewers note poor cross-domain transfer of premise detection (e.g., 65% of underspecified MedIQ questions go undetected), ambiguities in how the baseline differs from full JTS, and indirect estimation of Abstention@Detection.

oSaKSwVRhe.one_liner: Synthesizes rendered UI screens paired with component trees and structured captions to study text-to-image interface generation recipes.
oSaKSwVRhe.problem: It is unclear how training caption formats, application coverage, and UI-to-background data mixtures affect text and layout fidelity in text-to-image UI generation.
oSaKSwVRhe.method: ScreenForge renders application templates while preserving source documents and component trees so multiple caption recipes can be generated for the same UI screenshot. The authors run controlled 10-million-example continued-training experiments from a 2B text-to-image checkpoint and evaluate on a 1,300-screen benchmark.
oSaKSwVRhe.key_idea: Renders synthetic UI templates with retained DOM and component trees to systematically vary caption structure, app diversity, and UI mixture ratios during text-to-image training.
oSaKSwVRhe.evidence: Evaluated via single-run 10M-example continued training of a 2B T2I checkpoint and benchmarked against 16 models on 1,300 structured screen specifications.
oSaKSwVRhe.claimed_gains: On 1,300 structured screen specifications, a 50% UI mixture raises required-text recall from 0.465 to 0.813 and VLM-rated layout adherence from 3.24 to 3.84 over background-only continued training.
oSaKSwVRhe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the structured UI synthesis pipeline, the controlled 10M-sample experimental setup, and the planned release of training data and 1,300 benchmark screens.
oSaKSwVRhe.main_concern: Reviewers note that fine-grained recipe claims rely on single training runs without confidence intervals or human validation of VLM judges, and comparisons against general-purpose baselines on an in-distribution test split are not fair.

l09t6heq83.one_liner: Explains shallow safety alignment via autoregressive consistency and defends against mid-response harmful span insertions via adversarial alignment.
l09t6heq83.problem: Safety alignment in LLMs is predominantly concentrated in early output tokens, allowing a short harmful span inserted mid-refusal to hijack subsequent generation.
l09t6heq83.method: The authors analyze learning dynamics in a strong autoregressive-consistency regime to show why late-position gradients vanish during safety fine-tuning, and demonstrate a random insertion attack that injects a short harmful span into a safe refusal prefix. To counter this, they propose adversarial safety alignment that trains models on harmful continuation states with worst-case insertion selection to break harmful autoregressive consistency.
l09t6heq83.key_idea: Trains models on worst-case harmful spans inserted into refusal trajectories so the policy recovers to safe refusals rather than continuing the harmful branch.
l09t6heq83.evidence: Supported by theoretical gradient analysis for SFT/DPO and empirical attack/defense evaluations across multiple LLM families (including Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and a reasoning model).
l09t6heq83.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that demonstrating how a short harmful span inserted after a refusal prefix redirects generation is clear and that training against harmful continuations reduces attack success rates.
l09t6heq83.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the theoretical assumption of near-1.0 next-token probability is unrealistic, the mid-response token-insertion threat model assumes unrealistic attacker control, and the defense degrades MMLU utility.

6fg0VBUSTe.one_liner: Jointly encodes geometric and functional neuron population relations with relational consistency to match neurons across recordings.
6fg0VBUSTe.problem: Matching neuronal identities across animals or longitudinal recordings is difficult because individual neuron positions and activity patterns shift across sessions.
6fg0VBUSTe.method: NeuReL is a supervised neuron matching framework that embeds pairwise geometric and functional activity relationships within local neural populations using relation-conditioned attention. It combines within-recording population representations with cross-recording relational consistency to assign neuronal correspondences.
6fg0VBUSTe.key_idea: Integrates pairwise spatial geometry and calcium-activity correlations via relation-conditioned population attention and cross-recording relational consistency for neuron matching.
6fg0VBUSTe.evidence: Evaluated on cross-animal neuron matching in C. elegans (including Atanas and Kato datasets) and longitudinal spinal cord neuron matching in zebrafish embryos.
6fg0VBUSTe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining geometric and functional population context is well-motivated for neuroscience and achieves strong Top-1 matching improvements across C. elegans and zebrafish datasets.
6fg0VBUSTe.main_concern: Reviewers note that filling unannotated population-atlas relations with zeros degrades performance below a single medoid reference, Hungarian evaluation pre-filters unmatched queries, and sensitivity to annotation scarcity is untested.

VLOprj6bRK.one_liner: Introduces a versioned in-the-wild benchmark of provenance-labeled online clips to measure generalization drop in AI-generated video detectors.
VLOprj6bRK.problem: AI-generated video detectors that score above 93% AUROC on static laboratory benchmarks fail on real-world online videos due to evolving generators, editing, and platform transcoding.
VLOprj6bRK.method: VidTide collects online videos with provenance-based labels into fixed, versioned rolling slices—starting with an April 2026 release of 21,504 clips—to evaluate detector degradation over time. It benchmarks existing detectors and newly probed/fine-tuned backbones across compression, metadata-shortcut, and temporal transfer tests.
VLOprj6bRK.key_idea: Freezes periodic provenance-labeled slices of real-world platform videos to benchmark static-to-wild degradation and temporal drift in AI video detection.
VLOprj6bRK.evidence: Evaluated on 21,504 clips in the April 2026 slice (with a 200-clip blind manual audit) across five published detector families and standard vision backbones.
VLOprj6bRK.claimed_gains: Five detector families reporting 93–96% AUROC on GenVideo drop to 52–71% AUROC on VidTide, while standard backbones trained on VidTide reach 90.5% mean AUROC with linear probes and 91.7% with probing/fine-tuning selection.
VLOprj6bRK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exposing the sharp drop from laboratory benchmarks to platform-transcoded online videos addresses a critical evaluation gap in deepfake detection.
VLOprj6bRK.main_concern: Reviewers note that only one full slice (April 2026) plus a 99-clip temporal holdout exists so far, nearly 80% of data comes from Bilibili, and negative labels rely on absence-of-tag evidence rather than verified provenance.

K83AUvh9xg.one_liner: ELA optimizes a study-specific latent state using visual evidence to condition radiology report generation from a frozen model.
K83AUvh9xg.problem: Sampling more radiology reports recovers additional findings without reliably improving the factuality of the selected report.
K83AUvh9xg.method: ELA updates a small per-study latent state using frozen visual evidence models that penalize unsupported assertions and omitted findings. The adapted state conditions candidate generation, and a fixed evidence-based selector chooses the report before the state is discarded.
K83AUvh9xg.key_idea: Use visual-evidence feedback to update a per-study latent state that changes the candidate-generating distribution.
K83AUvh9xg.evidence: Experiments span multiple backbones and chest X-ray benchmarks, with controlled analyses separating latent adaptation from evidence-based selection.
K83AUvh9xg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the coverage-quality gap meaningful and value evidence-guided adaptation of the report distribution.
K83AUvh9xg.main_concern: The inference overhead is inadequately evaluated, and comparisons do not match the total computation used by adaptation.

hDtd8YevVg.one_liner: Ordering-separation theorems and controlled retrieval tasks show task-specific advantages of hybrid attention and state-space layer sequences.
hDtd8YevVg.problem: The combinatorial choices of hybrid layer types and ordering lack a principled account of their task-dependent effects.
hDtd8YevVg.method: The paper constructs tasks that separate layer configurations under fixed resource constraints and compares trained hybrid architectures with different orders. Deeper-model experiments test whether containing a task's dominant sequence predicts performance.
hDtd8YevVg.key_idea: Construct tasks whose information-access requirements distinguish layer orderings and repetitions under matched state, precision, and attention-window constraints.
hDtd8YevVg.evidence: Theoretical ordering separations accompany matched-memory experiments on all four-layer and five-layer profiles and segmented retrieval tasks.
hDtd8YevVg.claimed_gains: On segmented retrieval under the same memory budget, the theoretically predicted architecture reaches perfect accuracy while the next strongest plateaus below 0.5.
hDtd8YevVg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the formal analysis of ordering beyond attention-to-state-space ratios and the controlled architecture comparisons.
hDtd8YevVg.main_concern: The theoretical constructions and small synthetic experiments have limited demonstrated relevance to practical large hybrid architectures.

aBOZPEIgpi.one_liner: MedBenchAgent refines benchmark specifications and verifies retrieved medical annotations through a two-stage tool-using workflow.
aBOZPEIgpi.problem: Manual medical benchmark construction is labor-intensive, while existing agents lack consistent quality across tasks and modalities.
aBOZPEIgpi.method: The design stage decomposes requests, integrates a specification, and refines template items with a field-level quality model. The construction stage retrieves medical samples, annotates them, and uses an evidence-guided Thought-Tool-Observation loop for verification.
aBOZPEIgpi.key_idea: Separate specification refinement from sample annotation, using field-level quality feedback and evidence-guided tool verification at the respective stages.
aBOZPEIgpi.evidence: Evaluation spans five medical tasks and modalities, with general and specialized agent baselines, LLM-jury ratings, downstream fine-tuning, human evaluation, and ablations.
aBOZPEIgpi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the five-modality scope and evaluation through complementary automated, downstream, and human assessments.
aBOZPEIgpi.main_concern: The evaluation does not fully establish medical reliability and generalization beyond selected tasks with existing data and tool support.

sJsRarBGfm.one_liner: Random-subspace analysis relates model scale and training time through an effective-time trajectory under fixed learning rates.
sJsRarBGfm.problem: It is unclear when a larger model trained briefly can approximate a smaller model trained longer.
sJsRarBGfm.method: The paper analyzes nonlinear models trained within random parameter subspaces under fixed-learning-rate gradient flow. It compares scale-dependent trajectories at common effective time and tests generalization-time scaling with fixed-learning-rate SGD.
sJsRarBGfm.key_idea: Compare scale-p models at common effective time pt against a scale-independent function trajectory.
sJsRarBGfm.evidence: A random-subspace theorem accompanies MLP and CNN experiments on MNIST, SVHN, and CIFAR-10 across training-set sizes.
sJsRarBGfm.claimed_gains: The theoretical approximation error decays as p^{-1/2} for any fixed value of pt.
sJsRarBGfm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers consider the relationship between model scale and training time a meaningful theoretical and empirical question.
sJsRarBGfm.main_concern: The apparent scale-time equivalence may reflect the scale-dependent effective learning rate induced by fixed-rate parameterization.

yxKYuMCePa.one_liner: PINNsur learns surface normals and projects ambient differential operators to solve PDEs on curved surfaces.
yxKYuMCePa.problem: Surface PDE solvers must represent curved geometry accurately without relying on mesh quality or global parameterizations.
yxKYuMCePa.method: PINNsur trains a neural normal field and uses it to project differential operators from three-dimensional ambient space onto the surface. A separate physics-informed solution network solves the resulting surface PDE.
yxKYuMCePa.key_idea: Learn the surface normal field and use normal-based projection to construct surface differential operators for PINN residuals.
yxKYuMCePa.evidence: Experiments cover different equations and surface topologies, Dirichlet and Neumann conditions, heat and mean-curvature-flow applications, and FEM comparisons on degraded meshes.
yxKYuMCePa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple learned-normal formulation for surface PINNs without global parameterization.
yxKYuMCePa.main_concern: Normal-field pretraining and per-instance solution retraining impose substantial computational costs that limit practical use.

TPbu1cHiCa.one_liner: Weight-derived trigger directions and token-sharing diagnostics explain and manipulate visual activation spikes across vision-language models.
TPbu1cHiCa.problem: Visual massive activations vary across models and images, and their formation and sensitivity to perturbations remain unclear.
TPbu1cHiCa.method: The study extracts trigger directions from model weights and relates spike locations to how little a token shares with other image tokens. It tests trigger-guided perturbations and removes trigger components before spikes form.
TPbu1cHiCa.key_idea: Identify weight-derived spike triggers, locate susceptible tokens by shared image content, and remove trigger components before activation amplification.
TPbu1cHiCa.evidence: The survey covers 25 adapter-based LVLMs built on 18 text-only bases from 10 families, with corruption tests, state swaps, and trigger-removal interventions.
TPbu1cHiCa.claimed_gains: A perturbation budget of 1/255 suffices to create or remove spikes in nine of the ten models that spike.
TPbu1cHiCa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the broad model survey and mechanistic controls distinguishing massive activations from channel concentration and attention sinks.
TPbu1cHiCa.main_concern: The added value of the proposed trigger and controller interventions over simpler alternatives remains insufficiently isolated.

J90bp18yhT.one_liner: PerturbCellRL converts population-distribution discrepancies into per-cell rewards for post-training perturbation generators.
J90bp18yhT.problem: Flow-matching perturbation models can miss target cell-population distributions and fail to capture cellular heterogeneity.
J90bp18yhT.method: PerturbCellRL post-trains generators using a gene-expression energy witness that supplies per-cell distributional feedback. Additional rewards calibrated on real cells penalize atypical expression and inadequate pathway-level responses.
J90bp18yhT.key_idea: Translate population-level energy discrepancy into per-cell rewards and combine them with expression-plausibility and pathway-response penalties.
J90bp18yhT.evidence: The paper links witness policy gradients to distributional alignment and reports genetic and chemical perturbation benchmarks with scDFM and scLDM.
J90bp18yhT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distribution-focused single-cell post-training and the energy-witness link between per-cell rewards and population discrepancy.
J90bp18yhT.main_concern: The advantage of the RL optimization over direct distributional fine-tuning remains unestablished.

j6Zd8AyX5J.one_liner: Random-walk pairing replaces same-image positives with cross-image neighbors for self-supervised representation learning.
j6Zd8AyX5J.problem: Self-supervised representations can capture local invariances without adequately learning global semantic structure or generalizing to unseen data.
j6Zd8AyX5J.method: The method samples positive pairs across neighboring image representations and instantiates this strategy as SAG-VICReg without architectural changes. Its default one-step walk corresponds to similarity-weighted nearest-neighbor pairing.
j6Zd8AyX5J.key_idea: Replace same-image positive pairs with cross-image pairs sampled through similarity-weighted transitions among neighboring representations.
j6Zd8AyX5J.evidence: Experiments cover VICReg, SimCLR, TCL, pretrained-backbone fine-tuning, linear probing, label scarcity, and transfer to unseen datasets.
j6Zd8AyX5J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple, reusable pairing strategy and its empirical evaluation across self-supervised settings.
j6Zd8AyX5J.main_concern: The contribution beyond existing nearest-neighbor positive pairing is unclear, especially because one-step pairing performs best.

UtKeWOXLfa.one_liner: Cross-state reuse tests and command re-execution data expose and resolve ambiguities hidden by latent-action consistency checks.
UtKeWOXLfa.problem: Latent-action models can reconstruct trajectories and satisfy consistency constraints while applying the wrong action effect in new states.
UtKeWOXLfa.method: The paper constructs counterexamples and proves identification from repeated-command trajectories combined with re-execution trials under restricted finite-system assumptions. It bounds operator error using reconstruction and reuse error at independently sampled target states.
UtKeWOXLfa.key_idea: Combine repeated-command and interrupted re-execution observations, then test learned codes against independent-state outcomes rather than self-generated consistency alone.
UtKeWOXLfa.evidence: Identification theorems and error bounds accompany controlled systems with eight states and commands and frozen LAPO checkpoint evaluations on Procgen.
UtKeWOXLfa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distinguishing reconstruction and internal consistency from correct cross-state action reuse.
UtKeWOXLfa.main_concern: Restricted theoretical and controlled settings leave the connection to operator identification in practical neural latent-action models incomplete.

tM6cEgwtng.one_liner: GPUPhysBench tests coding agents on physics simulation tasks against expert GPU implementations under fixed time budgets.
tM6cEgwtng.problem: Existing GPU coding benchmarks inadequately cover physical simulation with irregular memory access, synchronization, and iterative solvers.
tM6cEgwtng.method: GPUPhysBench provides tasks spanning simulation operators and complete simulators for fluids, deformable solids, and granular materials. Agents write, compile, test, and optimize GPU code, with correctness and runtime measured against expert references.
tM6cEgwtng.key_idea: Evaluate numerical correctness and runtime against expert GPU references while agents implement physics simulations within fixed time budgets.
tM6cEgwtng.evidence: A single-attempt evaluation tests six model-harness pairs on 50 physics simulation tasks with NVIDIA GPU access.
tM6cEgwtng.claimed_gains: The two strongest systems pass all 50 tasks, but the fastest reaches at least 0.9× reference speed on only 22%, and no submission is more than 5% faster.
tM6cEgwtng.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize physical simulation as a useful, underrepresented setting for evaluating GPU coding agents.
tM6cEgwtng.main_concern: Reviewers question how much scientific insight the benchmark adds beyond existing evaluation approaches and expected performance gaps.

KRpFPrO217.one_liner: LACCO alternates local trajectories to overlap communication with computation while preserving globally consistent, nonstale outer updates.
KRpFPrO217.problem: Local optimization leaves outer synchronization on the critical path, while existing overlap methods introduce stale updates or replica drift.
KRpFPrO217.method: LACCO uses a two-stage local accumulation algorithm to overlap global communication with local computation. Globally aggregated outer updates are shared across replicas without outer-update staleness.
KRpFPrO217.key_idea: Alternate local computation trajectories so global aggregation overlaps a local phase while every replica applies the same nonstale outer update.
KRpFPrO217.evidence: The paper proves convergence for smooth non-convex objectives and evaluates FineWeb pretraining up to 0.5B parameters and 16 workers.
KRpFPrO217.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the two-stage design for overlapping communication while maintaining replica consistency and providing convergence guarantees.
KRpFPrO217.main_concern: Reviewers question whether idealized timing assumptions and unmeasured transfer costs support the claimed low overhead in real distributed training.

wBPDxo8c0N.one_liner: RecastNet recovers network inverse actions from a neural solver's Jacobian to analytically accommodate topology changes without retraining.
wBPDxo8c0N.problem: Training neural solvers across combinatorially many network topologies is costly and may not generalize to unseen changes.
wBPDxo8c0N.method: A neural solver is trained on one base topology, then its input-output Jacobian recovers the underlying Laplacian inverse. Low-rank topology changes are incorporated through analytical corrections at inference.
wBPDxo8c0N.key_idea: Recover Laplacian inverse actions from the base solver's input-output Jacobian and apply analytical low-rank topology updates.
wBPDxo8c0N.evidence: Experiments on synthetic networks and real-world electric grids compare graph-learning and topology-adaptation baselines across increasing topology-change severity.
wBPDxo8c0N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find analytical adaptation of base-topology solvers practically motivated and appreciate the Jacobian-based inverse-action mechanism.
wBPDxo8c0N.main_concern: Reviewers find the applicability of the assumed network structure to realistic AC power flow insufficiently specified and justified.

K3CKXzcHDE.one_liner: PLOT matches abstract and neural intervention effects with optimal transport to locate causal correspondences progressively.
K3CKXzcHDE.problem: Finding causal abstractions often requires learning and evaluating separate mappings across many candidate neural locations.
K3CKXzcHDE.method: PLOT encodes abstract and neural interventions as geometric signatures of their effects on task outputs and fits an optimal transport coupling. The coupling supplies intervention handles, guides progressively finer localization, or initializes distributed alignment search.
K3CKXzcHDE.key_idea: Couple abstract and neural interventions through optimal transport over output-effect signatures, then use the coupling to select intervention sites.
K3CKXzcHDE.evidence: Experiments evaluate hierarchical equality, binary addition, and multiple-choice question answering, including direct handles, progressive localization, and PLOT-guided DAS.
K3CKXzcHDE.claimed_gains: PLOT-guided DAS attains accuracy comparable to full DAS at approximately 3.6× and 20× lower serial runtime.
K3CKXzcHDE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the presentation clear and the use of optimal transport for causal localization technically interesting.
K3CKXzcHDE.main_concern: Reviewers find comparisons insufficient to isolate PLOT's contribution relative to relevant DAS variants and simpler localization strategies.

y5g4fzFohc.one_liner: RECLAIM fixes reproduction targets and GPU budgets, then evaluates agents using papers, released artifacts, and log-based grading.
y5g4fzFohc.problem: Autonomous research evaluations do not adequately measure reproduction of published claims under realistic artifact availability and compute constraints.
y5g4fzFohc.method: RECLAIM assigns papers to Run, Retrain, or Reimplement tiers based on released code, data, and weights, with predefined claims and success criteria. A separate language model grades execution logs and outputs.
y5g4fzFohc.key_idea: Freeze each paper's reproduction target, success criterion, and GPU budget, then grade execution evidence under artifact-dependent difficulty tiers.
y5g4fzFohc.evidence: Four agents each attempt 100 NeurIPS 2025 papers once, with diagnostic analysis of reproduction failures.
y5g4fzFohc.claimed_gains: The best agent per tier reproduces 38% of Run, 27% of Retrain, and 15% of Reimplement papers; failed attempts use 29% of their budgets on average, and unvalidated implementations occur in 63 of 400 runs.
y5g4fzFohc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the realistic, reusable evaluation design and detailed methodological disclosure.
y5g4fzFohc.main_concern: Reviewers question the validity of the LLM auditor and its reliance on insufficiently validated or agent-writable evidence.

MkXiBDC5Ws.one_liner: DexLink retargets sparse hand-object templates, chains them into trajectories, and refines them with residual reinforcement learning.
MkXiBDC5Ws.problem: Dexterous manipulation policies depend on difficult-to-scale demonstrations or generic rewards that offer limited control over interactions.
MkXiBDC5Ws.method: DexLink retargets reusable static interaction templates to objects while preserving spatial hand-object relationships. It connects the resulting poses into reference trajectories and trains residual reinforcement learning policies in simulation.
MkXiBDC5Ws.key_idea: Retarget sparse hand-object interaction templates, connect their poses into a reference trajectory, and learn residual closed-loop control.
MkXiBDC5Ws.evidence: Experiments cover single-hand, bimanual, articulated, and dynamic manipulation, cross-object template transfer, and preliminary zero-shot hardware deployment.
MkXiBDC5Ws.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the intuitive, reusable task representation and its control over grasp types, object motion, and timing.
MkXiBDC5Ws.main_concern: Reviewers find scalability and overall data-generation savings unproven because manual specification and separate policy-training costs are not quantified.

4uD8ULtUok.one_liner: Frozen language-model report embeddings supervise ECG representation learning through simple global alignment.
4uD8ULtUok.problem: ECG-language pretraining may be limited by text representation quality despite increasingly elaborate cross-modal alignment.
4uD8ULtUok.method: A frozen large language model encodes clinical reports as fixed supervisory representations. Architectural and optimization mechanisms support ECG learning through global alignment with these representations.
4uD8ULtUok.key_idea: Use frozen LLM embeddings of clinical reports as stable supervision for globally aligning ECG representations.
4uD8ULtUok.evidence: Experiments span three public datasets, with linear probing, cross-domain transfer, zero-shot evaluation, and controlled frozen-text-encoder comparisons.
4uD8ULtUok.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize strong empirical performance and a well-motivated emphasis on text representation quality.
4uD8ULtUok.main_concern: Reviewers find the evidence insufficient to attribute the gains specifically to improved text semantics or the LLM's clinical knowledge.

TeRbk7SVeW.one_liner: NSTime decomposes time series and forecasts amplitude-phase fields on shared cyclic coordinates with a residual dynamics path.
TeRbk7SVeW.problem: Recurring temporal patterns can change in amplitude, phase, and channel alignment over long forecast horizons.
TeRbk7SVeW.method: NSTime recursively decomposes signals into a smoothed background and detail residuals, each modeled with amplitude-phase and residual components. Continuous circular temporal generators provide shared cyclic coordinates on which learned fields model historical and future amplitude and phase.
TeRbk7SVeW.key_idea: Represent decomposed temporal details through amplitude-phase fields evaluated on shared cyclic coordinates with learned channel offsets and a residual path.
TeRbk7SVeW.evidence: The paper evaluates 11 forecasting benchmarks and includes matched component ablations, drift stratification, and comparisons with CycleNet.
TeRbk7SVeW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize competitive forecasting performance and useful component analyses for the amplitude-phase formulation.
TeRbk7SVeW.main_concern: Reviewers find the distinctive contribution of temporal pattern deformation relative to existing cyclic and non-stationary forecasting approaches insufficiently established.

f4vTfwprqN.one_liner: MATCHA keeps multi-agent learning on accelerators and vectorizes tree search by selecting frontier nodes using cumulative path statistics.
f4vTfwprqN.problem: Search-based model-based multi-agent reinforcement learning can be sample-efficient but slow because of CPU planning and CPU-GPU communication.
f4vTfwprqN.method: MATCHA keeps data collection, planning, and learning on the accelerator. Path-Guided Frontier Search scores frontier nodes using cumulative path statistics and performs selection and expansion through a vectorized tensor operation.
f4vTfwprqN.key_idea: Replace sequential tree traversal with globally scored frontier-node selection while keeping collection, planning, and learning on the accelerator.
f4vTfwprqN.evidence: Experiments on SMAX, Overcooked, and MPE compare sample efficiency and wall-clock time, with GPU search baselines and component profiling.
f4vTfwprqN.claimed_gains: MATCHA achieves up to 16.3× end-to-end wall-clock speedup while matching or exceeding the sample efficiency of strong MBMARL baselines.
f4vTfwprqN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical systems bottleneck and evidence of substantial wall-clock improvements across benchmarks.
f4vTfwprqN.main_concern: Reviewers question whether comparisons adequately isolate PGFS gains from GPU acceleration, implementation changes, and other algorithmic modifications.

yfbmQXKLSr.one_liner: Information-tempered priors control Gamma shape tails to prevent posterior lockout in uncapped Thompson sampling.
yfbmQXKLSr.problem: Nearly equal pessimistic observations can make Gamma Thompson sampling overconfident and indefinitely under-explore the optimal arm.
yfbmQXKLSr.method: Information-tempered matching priors retain full support and first-order probability matching while controlling the high-shape tail. Posterior-integral and boundary analyses establish summable pessimism odds and asymptotically optimal regret for uncapped Thompson sampling.
yfbmQXKLSr.key_idea: Temper the Gamma shape prior to a k^(-1-eta) tail with eta greater than zero while preserving probability matching and uncapped sampling.
yfbmQXKLSr.evidence: The paper proves fixed-instance regret guarantees and a prior-tail threshold, and tests full-bandit performance with 1,024 trials per instance.
yfbmQXKLSr.claimed_gains: ITM-TS attains the Burnetas–Katehakis regret constant, while Jeffreys' prior incurs Ω(√T) lockout regret and the matching prior has a distinct Ω(log T) coefficient constraint with two initial pulls per arm.
yfbmQXKLSr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the precise connection between prior tails and lockout and the asymptotic guarantee for uncapped Gamma Thompson sampling.
yfbmQXKLSr.main_concern: Reviewers find the practical advantage over matching Thompson sampling limited and statistically inconsistent across evaluated settings.

4ZVWEhcgT4.one_liner: TokenCast composes segment costs and context growth to forecast agent token consumption and refreshes predictions during execution.
4ZVWEhcgT4.problem: Agent token costs vary across runs and accumulate through repeated reading of growing context, making total consumption difficult to predict.
4ZVWEhcgT4.method: TokenCast learns a composable representation of each execution segment's consumption and context growth. Runtime observations update task-level and call-level forecasts without additional language-model calls.
4ZVWEhcgT4.key_idea: Compose segment consumption with context-growth cross-terms that account for earlier context being reread by later calls.
4ZVWEhcgT4.evidence: Evaluation spans 4 task suites, 6 agent models, 96 combinations, and an offline budget-control replay.
4ZVWEhcgT4.claimed_gains: TokenCast averages 14.5% lower mean absolute error over 96 combinations and uses 21.3% fewer tokens in offline replay at matched trace completion, with 32.8 ms mean cumulative prediction time per SWE-bench Verified run.
4ZVWEhcgT4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value explicit accounting for repeated context consumption and the practical relevance of dynamic agent-cost forecasting.
4ZVWEhcgT4.main_concern: Reviewers find that the ablations do not isolate the composition rule's benefit from representation, supervision, and predictor changes.

cxoUX4ts7x.one_liner: Co-evolves prompt difficulty estimates via self-normalized importance sampling with symmetric Beta prompt sampling and tier-adaptive RL compute allocation.
cxoUX4ts7x.problem: Static difficulty-aware prompt selection in LLM reinforcement learning suffers from inaccurate difficulty estimates under policy drift, limited final accuracy gains, and unchanged verbose responses on easy tasks.
cxoUX4ts7x.method: DARE co-evolves prompt difficulty estimation alongside the policy via self-normalized importance sampling (SNIS), samples prompts using a symmetric Beta distribution, and applies difficulty-tier-specific rollout budgets and training strategies to produce concise responses on easy tasks while improving accuracy on hard ones.
cxoUX4ts7x.key_idea: Update prompt difficulty estimates under policy drift via self-normalized importance sampling while sampling prompts from a symmetric Beta distribution with difficulty-tier-specific training and compute allocation.
cxoUX4ts7x.evidence: Evaluated across multiple LLMs on mathematical reasoning (including GSM8K) and coding benchmarks, including validation of the SNIS difficulty estimator against a current-policy oracle on held-out prompts.
cxoUX4ts7x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that maintaining policy-aligned difficulty estimates via SNIS—and checking them against a current-policy oracle—sensibly addresses prompt difficulty drift during RL training.
cxoUX4ts7x.main_concern: Reviewers note that the chosen Beta(51, 51) sampler (kappa=100) assigns near-zero density to easy (<0.3) and hard (>0.8) tiers—rendering tier-specific branches nearly unreachable—while baselines are not compute-budget matched and bundled heuristics obscure attribution.

Cmgky2Bn7f.one_liner: Conditions multi-view subject-to-video diffusion on temporally unaligned reconstructed surface-normal turntables trained with synthetic 360-degree 3D-asset video trajectories.
Cmgky2Bn7f.problem: Multi-view subject-to-video models lack explicit 3D structural connections across reference views and lack training videos guaranteed to preserve the same 3D subject across large or 360-degree viewpoint changes.
Cmgky2Bn7f.method: OmniShowcase combines an automated 3D-asset rendering and background-synthesis pipeline—producing Showcase-4K across 12 camera motions and 88 trajectory configurations—with a geometry-conditioning mechanism that feeds the video model a turntable of surface-normal maps reconstructed from reference views without requiring temporal alignment with generated frames.
Cmgky2Bn7f.key_idea: Condition multi-view subject-to-video generation on a temporally unaligned turntable of reconstructed surface-normal maps paired with synthetic 3D-asset training videos spanning diverse camera trajectories.
