Cmgky2Bn7f.evidence: Trained on Showcase-4K and evaluated on the held-out ShowcaseBench dataset using foreground identity and geometric consistency metrics (including DINO, MEt3R, and GT-CD) and reference-count ablations.
Cmgky2Bn7f.reviewer_consensus: Two of three reviewers agree that the frame-unaligned surface-normal turntable and 3D-asset synthesis pipeline offer a practical way to preserve foreground subject geometry across flexible camera trajectories.
Cmgky2Bn7f.main_concern: Reviewers question why generative video synthesis is needed instead of directly rendering the already-reconstructed static 3D subject in a 3D scene, alongside untested robustness to normal-reconstruction errors and unmeasured background 3D consistency.

EOOJsjIzG1.one_liner: Iteratively optimizes natural-language style system prompts using evaluator discrimination rewards and reflector feedback so LLMs imitate target writing styles.
EOOJsjIzG1.problem: Language models exhibit recognizable implicit writing styles that are rarely articulated into explicit natural-language prompts that other models can reliably adopt.
EOOJsjIzG1.method: PrompTo runs an iterative prompt-optimization loop in which an independent evaluator attempts to distinguish paired responses from a style-prompted source LLM and a target LLM, and a reflector consumes the resulting reward and language feedback to propose refined system-prompt candidates without updating model weights.
EOOJsjIzG1.key_idea: Optimize transferable natural-language style system prompts through an iterative search loop where a reflector refines candidate prompts from an independent evaluator's discrimination reward and language feedback.
EOOJsjIzG1.evidence: Evaluated across multiple 3B–7B source LLMs and target models (including Claude Haiku on ELI5), measuring discriminator confusion, response quality, cross-model prompt transfer, qualitative analysis, and ablations.
EOOJsjIzG1.claimed_gains: Optimized style prompts recover 74.8% of the source-target gap on average, compared with at most 15.2% for existing baselines.
EOOJsjIzG1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distilling implicit LLM writing styles into interpretable, cross-model transferable system prompts is thoroughly evaluated across baselines, source-target pairs, and qualitative analyses.
EOOJsjIzG1.main_concern: Reviewers note limited model and domain scale (3B–7B source models, single frontier target Claude Haiku on ELI5, omitting motivating targets like GPT-4o), missing statistical confidence intervals, and incremental originality over GEPA with a discriminator.

P0wmdAh2RR.one_liner: Establishes formal conditions for out-of-support specification generation using structural graphical models and samples via likelihood-weighted resampling or guided diffusion.
P0wmdAh2RR.problem: Generating data satisfying unseen specification combinations beyond the support of the training distribution lacks formal conditions separating when extrapolative generation is feasible and identifiable from when it is impossible.
P0wmdAh2RR.method: Structural Extrapolative Data Generation (SEDGE) models specification-to-feature graphical structures with explicit selection variables to establish formal feasibility, non-identifiability, and approximate identifiability conditions under conservative assumptions. Algorithmically, the authors develop structure-informed likelihood-weighted resampling (LWR) and likelihood-guided diffusion (LGD) for extrapolative sampling.
P0wmdAh2RR.key_idea: Model specification-to-feature graphical structures with selection variables to characterize conservative extrapolative identifiability and generate unseen-specification samples via structure-informed likelihood-weighted resampling or likelihood-guided diffusion.
P0wmdAh2RR.evidence: Supported by formal feasibility and identifiability propositions/theorems and empirical evaluations on synthetic selection audits, property-guided molecule design, and text-guided compositional image generation.
P0wmdAh2RR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing extrapolative generation via specification-to-feature graphical structures and selection variables usefully separates sample feasibility from target-distribution identifiability.
P0wmdAh2RR.main_concern: Reviewers find central theoretical concepts ('approximately identifiable', 'conservative solution') insufficiently formalized with error bounds and note loose connections between the formal assumptions and approximations used in molecule and image experiments.

IrlQW79O1p.one_liner: AAS-MAD schedules argument-focused revisions by predicted benefit, risk, and token cost.
IrlQW79O1p.problem: Full-response debate rounds spend computation on low-value reasoning and can propagate erroneous arguments instead of selectively revising useful claims.
IrlQW79O1p.method: AAS-MAD organizes rationales into a public argument state containing claims, decisions, evidence, support, and conflict relations. It predicts rescue and damage for candidate revisions, ranks actions by rescue and call cost, and stops with a damage-aware gate.
IrlQW79O1p.key_idea: Treat debate as costed revisions over an argument graph, ranking focused actions by predicted rescue and stopping through damage estimates.
IrlQW79O1p.evidence: Experiments cover eight reasoning benchmarks and a curated FIFA 2026 dataset, comparing five MAD methods with opening-relative promotion, acquisition, and damage measurements.
IrlQW79O1p.claimed_gains: AAS-MAD achieves 70.76% pooled accuracy, exceeding the strongest evaluated debate baseline by 1.03 percentage points with 28.84–44.34% fewer tokens, and its 1.45-percentage-point opening-relative gain is the largest among five MAD methods.
IrlQW79O1p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that argument-focused computation is well motivated and that the method improves token efficiency while retaining competitive accuracy.
IrlQW79O1p.main_concern: Much of the endpoint advantage exists before debate, and the learned scheduler's predictive quality and cross-task contribution remain insufficiently isolated.

AZ4YZtJTs3.one_liner: Output-aware pruning selects residual-stream subspaces using sensitivity-weighted covariance eigendecomposition.
AZ4YZtJTs3.problem: Activation reconstruction objectives for residual-stream pruning ignore direction-dependent sensitivity in downstream model outputs.
AZ4YZtJTs3.method: The method approximates output KL divergence to second order using activation covariance and local output sensitivity. A spectral upper bound turns subspace selection into eigendecomposition of a sensitivity-weighted covariance matrix compatible with rotation-based pruning.
AZ4YZtJTs3.key_idea: Weight residual activation covariance by output sensitivity, then select pruning subspaces through a tractable spectral bound on output KL divergence.
AZ4YZtJTs3.evidence: Experiments across several instruction-tuned language model families and compression levels measure calibration KL, perplexity, and downstream performance against activation-only pruning.
AZ4YZtJTs3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that output sensitivity addresses a clear weakness of activation-only pruning and yields consistent gains without changing the pruned model structure.
AZ4YZtJTs3.main_concern: The evaluation relies mainly on SliceGPT and omits newer hidden-dimension pruning baselines, measured efficiency, and recovery fine-tuning.

irVKjZ7a6I.one_liner: Recursive-model completion is diagnosed through latent settling and trajectory-conditioned anisotropic stability.
irVKjZ7a6I.problem: An incorrect recursive-model output at its nominal inference budget cannot distinguish unfinished computation from a persistently unsuccessful regime.
irVKjZ7a6I.method: The study extends attention and MLP-based Tiny Recursive Models beyond nominal recurrence and aligns trajectories by their first exact solution. It analyzes latent motion, local Jacobian directions, and perturbations to characterize completion as trajectory-conditioned anisotropic stability.
irVKjZ7a6I.key_idea: Identify completed computation by latent-state settling and contraction along the trajectory despite expansion in other local Jacobian directions.
irVKjZ7a6I.evidence: Experiments use 1,000 hard Sudoku puzzles, recurrence extended from 16 to 512 steps, perturbation tests on both architectures, and a second attention checkpoint.
irVKjZ7a6I.claimed_gains: Extending recurrence from 16 to 512 steps raises cumulative exact-solve accuracy from 59.2% to 87.5% for the attention model and from 74.4% to 91.9% for the MLP model, solving more than two-thirds of puzzles unsolved at the nominal budget.
irVKjZ7a6I.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing unfinished from failed computation is useful and that the solve-aligned trajectory analysis is clear and informative.
irVKjZ7a6I.main_concern: The limited task and checkpoint scope, together with prior reports of inference-time recurrence scaling, leave the analysis's added impact uncertain.

mKgXypjI6R.one_liner: BVB evaluates video agents by programmatically reconstructing source videos as animated Blender scenes.
mKgXypjI6R.problem: Question-answering benchmarks do not test whether video agents can integrate observations into one coherent, executable scene reconstruction.
mKgXypjI6R.method: BVB asks agents to reconstruct real-world videos through the Mini-BVB harness in an identical sandbox under a shared cost limit. Dual VQA measures recoverable spatiotemporal facts, Latent Similarity measures perceptual match, and a square-root mean combines them.
mKgXypjI6R.key_idea: Score executable Blender reconstructions by both judge-recoverable spatiotemporal facts and rendered perceptual similarity under a common agent harness.
mKgXypjI6R.evidence: The benchmark evaluates 51 configurations from 10 model families and analyzes semantic retention, perceptual similarity, reasoning effort, and cost.
mKgXypjI6R.claimed_gains: The best model retains only 53.7% of judge-recoverable facts, and additional reasoning improves perceptual similarity but not fact retention.
mKgXypjI6R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that programmatic reconstruction is an interesting task and that the shared harness and complementary metrics provide useful comparisons.
mKgXypjI6R.main_concern: Evaluating rendered 2D videos without validating underlying 3D geometry conflates video understanding with coding ability and permits visually plausible but spatially wrong scenes.

2I7f9qIBG0.one_liner: AMD adapts task-wise mutual-distillation weights between models trained with different task-balancing strategies.
2I7f9qIBG0.problem: Multi-task post-training with uneven data produces complementary models, but useful cross-model supervision varies by task, direction, and training stage.
2I7f9qIBG0.method: AMD jointly trains two models with different task-balancing strategies and tests candidate distillation-weight adjustments through short shared training probes. Task-wise validation scores select adjustments for each task and transfer direction, with optional model merging for inference.
2I7f9qIBG0.key_idea: Use short training probes and task-wise validation to choose directional distillation weights between differently balanced models throughout post-training.
2I7f9qIBG0.evidence: Experiments span six benchmarks and three LLM backbones, comparing both AMD branches and merged models with sampling-matched SFT and task-balancing methods.
2I7f9qIBG0.claimed_gains: The merged models outperform multi-task SFT by an average of 2.91 points across the three backbones.
2I7f9qIBG0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that mutual distillation between differently sampled models is intuitive and supported by broad comparisons and useful controls.
2I7f9qIBG0.main_concern: Adaptive weight selection offers small, sometimes sub-noise gains over fixed weights, and unmatched two-model compute complicates attribution.

fejBVFa8fE.one_liner: QSFN compiles compositional formulas into quantum spectral circuits with explicit approximation and resource guarantees.
fejBVFa8fE.problem: Global Fourier or Chebyshev expansions can grow exponentially for compositional targets even when their generating formulas remain small.
fejBVFa8fE.method: QSFN compiles bounded generating formulas with univariate spectral leaves exposing signed Pauli-Z expectations and internal vertices applying bounded multiaffine maps. A deterministic compiler provides query, gate, depth, normalization, stability, and analytic approximation guarantees.
fejBVFa8fE.key_idea: Compile local formula structure directly through Pauli-Z spectral leaves and multiaffine composition instead of expanding the target's global spectrum.
fejBVFa8fE.evidence: The paper proves an exponential signed-flat Fourier branch lower bound and a Θ(d²) QSFN construction, with three matched-error experiments and semantic controls.
fejBVFa8fE.claimed_gains: For an explicit continuous bounded family, fixed-error signed-flat Fourier approximation requires Ω(2^d) branches while QSFN gives an exact Θ(d²) construction, and matched-error experiments reduce entangling depth by up to 10.5-fold.
fejBVFa8fE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the representation is precise, the compiler guarantees are substantive, and the fixed-error spectral separation is carefully supported.
fejBVFa8fE.main_concern: The separation depends on representation and cost conventions, while the quantum application value remains unclear for known formulas that classical computers can evaluate efficiently.

MNwejBwJSK.one_liner: AS-TRM masks recursive-step supervision using step outcomes and task-specific focus sets.
MNwejBwJSK.problem: Full supervision at every early recursive thinking step can impose noisy targets before a Tiny Recursive Model can derive a complete solution.
MNwejBwJSK.method: AS-TRM uses each thinking step's outcome to partition training signals into focus and non-focus sets, selectively supervising positions according to task structure. Gradient and loss-landscape diagnostics examine supervision noise and convergence without changing the TRM architecture.
MNwejBwJSK.key_idea: Dynamically restrict intermediate supervision to outcome-selected focus positions rather than imposing complete targets at every recursive step.
MNwejBwJSK.evidence: Experiments on Sudoku-Extreme, Maze-Hard, and ARC-AGI-1 include recursion-depth comparisons, frontier ablations, and gradient and loss-landscape analyses.
MNwejBwJSK.claimed_gains: AS-TRM gains 7.9 points of accuracy (11.3% relative) and up to 1.79x training speed on Sudoku-Extreme, improves Maze-Hard accuracy by 6.3 points, and reaches up to 1.51x speedup on ARC-AGI-1.
MNwejBwJSK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adapting supervision to reasoning progress is intuitive and that Sudoku gains and frontier ablations support selective intermediate supervision.
MNwejBwJSK.main_concern: Task-specific focus rules limit generality, and the Maze-Hard comparison confounds adaptive supervision with changed targets and augmentation.

7EKNxwiX7s.one_liner: WILDFIRE-FM evaluates wildfire transfer under fixed contracts that expose metric-driven ranking instability.
7EKNxwiX7s.problem: Wildfire transfer scores and model rankings can reflect evaluation choices rather than backbone quality when matching and selection rules vary.
7EKNxwiX7s.method: The study fixes evaluation contracts and varies matching rules and head-selection metrics while holding predictions or frozen features fixed. It introduces contract dominance ratio and rank instability rate, and provides WILDFIRE-FM as a wildfire-trained reference across six tasks.
7EKNxwiX7s.key_idea: Hold evaluation contracts fixed and quantify how matching and model-selection choices change scores and rankings independently of backbone predictions.
7EKNxwiX7s.evidence: Controlled checks hold predictions or frozen features fixed, and WILDFIRE-FM supplies reference results for occupancy, spread, burned-area prediction, and six downstream tasks under specified contracts.
7EKNxwiX7s.claimed_gains: Decision F1 changes from 5.31% to 66.74% solely with the matching rule, head selection changes it by up to 88.10 percentage points, and evaluation choices reverse up to 46% of model-pair rankings.
7EKNxwiX7s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluation sensitivity is empirically important and that explicitly reported settings and a wildfire reference aid controlled comparison.
7EKNxwiX7s.main_concern: The fixed-contract framework largely restates controlled-comparison practice, while CDR and RIR do not identify which evaluation setting is operationally appropriate.

k4yeAITBxf.one_liner: Multi-turn benchmark evaluating whether LLMs clarify missing or contradictory specifications in computational science prompts.
k4yeAITBxf.problem: Scientific LLM benchmarks assume well-posed prompts, ignoring that real user requests often lack critical parameters or contain contradictions.
k4yeAITBxf.method: SciConvBench covers fluid mechanics, solid mechanics, materials science, and PDEs with a task ontology and rubric scoring disambiguation, inconsistency resolution, conversational grounding, and final specification fidelity.
k4yeAITBxf.key_idea: Evaluates multi-turn disambiguation and contradiction detection in ill-posed scientific prompts by separating final fidelity from conversation-grounded resolution.
k4yeAITBxf.evidence: Evaluated frontier LLMs across four computational science domains using a validated judge-and-simulator pipeline.
k4yeAITBxf.claimed_gains: Even the best frontier model resolves only 52.7% of disambiguation cases through dialogue, averaged across the four domains.
k4yeAITBxf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper targets an overlooked real-world gap in scientific assistants and cleanly separates final state from conversational grounding.
k4yeAITBxf.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the CGRR metric penalizes reasonable scientific defaults and exhibits large annotator variance (15-point spread, Fleiss kappa = 0.65).

5HASBtgMJG.one_liner: Trains LLMs to verbalize latent beliefs like evaluation awareness using span-masked RL on prefixes before spontaneous verbalizations.
5HASBtgMJG.problem: LLMs may recognize they are being evaluated without verbalizing it, undermining audits and chain-of-thought monitoring.
5HASBtgMJG.method: Verbalization training (VT) truncates rollouts immediately before spontaneous verbalizations to collect belief-holding prefixes, then applies a span-masked RL objective restricted to verbalization spans to increase calibrated reporting without supervising the belief itself.
5HASBtgMJG.key_idea: Mines prefixes preceding spontaneous verbalizations and applies span-masked RL to amplify latent-belief reporting without an external oracle.
5HASBtgMJG.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Kimi K2.6, and Inkling across evaluation awareness, synthetic-document implantation, reward hacking, sycophancy, and bias.
5HASBtgMJG.claimed_gains: Increases verbalized evaluation awareness by 2.4-2.9x across Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Kimi K2.6, and Inkling.
5HASBtgMJG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the oracle-free prefix-mining and span-masked RL design is clean and addresses an important AI safety monitoring problem.
5HASBtgMJG.main_concern: Reviewers find limited technical novelty in combining standard RL/KL/judge filtering and question whether unchanged probes prove belief invariance or faithful reporting.

NK6AN4OKBj.one_liner: Training-free sampler boosting generative diversity via matrix-free perturbations along leading right singular vectors of the endpoint Jacobian.
NK6AN4OKBj.problem: Existing diversity heuristics repel sampling trajectories without directly maximizing the spread of final generated endpoints.
NK6AN4OKBj.method: JIVE computes leading right singular vectors of the generator's endpoint Jacobian via matrix-free iterations and injects aligned velocity perturbations during sampling to expand endpoint volume.
NK6AN4OKBj.key_idea: Injects matrix-free velocity perturbations aligned with the leading right singular subspace of the endpoint Jacobian to maximize sample spread.
NK6AN4OKBj.evidence: Evaluated on one-step and few-step generative models using pixel and feature-level diversity and quality metrics.
NK6AN4OKBj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using the endpoint Jacobian in a training-free, matrix-free sampler is well-motivated and clearly presented.
NK6AN4OKBj.main_concern: Reviewers observe noticeable image-quality degradation alongside diversity gains, plus limited linearized one-step theory and conflation of IID versus non-IID diversity.

1Azj6zZhg5.one_liner: Detects benign-looking training examples that pass safety filters yet induce emergent misalignment via representation scoring.
1Azj6zZhg5.problem: Ordinary fine-tuning corpora can contain examples that pass content-level safety filters but still trigger broad emergent misalignment.
1Azj6zZhg5.method: The authors score safety-filtered LMSYS-Chat and Dolci examples along activation directions derived from known EM-inducing versus aligned data, and repeat selection using 9-12 sparse autoencoder (SAE) features.
1Azj6zZhg5.key_idea: Ranks safety-filtered training examples by projection onto misalignment activation directions and sparse autoencoder features to uncover EM-inducing data.
1Azj6zZhg5.evidence: Fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on 1,000 selected LMSYS-Chat examples out of 775k and evaluated on 2,190 questions across six categories.
1Azj6zZhg5.claimed_gains: Yields a 15.95% emergent misalignment rate versus 1.70% for random selection; 9-12 SAE features recover 81-90% of selected examples.
1Azj6zZhg5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper demonstrates an important safety risk—that safety-filtered text can induce emergent misalignment—with thorough experiments.
1Azj6zZhg5.main_concern: Reviewers note selected examples are mostly short or wrong answers that quality filters might catch, capability drops sharply, and overlap with prior SAE/persona-direction work is underdiscussed.

GyurSJQxPM.one_liner: Amortizes long-document understanding to index time with entity-memory and hierarchical-summary updates for single-pass top-k retrieval.
GyurSJQxPM.problem: Single-pass retrievers miss distributed multi-hop evidence in long documents, while agentic multi-step retrieval adds high query-time latency.
GyurSJQxPM.method: SAADI performs <=1.25 index-time LLM calls per chunk to extract entities conditioned on entity memory and a hierarchical prefix summary, linking each chunk to its records and summary. At query time, two auxiliary scores fuse with any sparse or dense retriever in one top-k pass.
GyurSJQxPM.key_idea: Builds query-agnostic entity records and hierarchical prefix summaries at index time to score chunks in a single query-time retrieval pass.
GyurSJQxPM.evidence: Evaluated across four long-document datasets, five retrieval backends, and contexts up to 256K tokens.
GyurSJQxPM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree amortizing document understanding to index time with explicit cost accounting across diverse retrievers and long contexts is practical.
GyurSJQxPM.main_concern: Reviewers find limited novelty over RAPTOR/GraphRAG/Contextual Retrieval, note entity-memory conditioning adds little over summaries alone, and flag fusion-weight tuning leakage.

BieyJqWUIL.one_liner: Lightweight distilled predictor that scores KV-cache tokens dynamically at each decoding step without evicting the full cache.
BieyJqWUIL.problem: Reading the full KV cache during long-context decoding is memory-bandwidth bound, while permanent eviction risks dropping future-relevant tokens.
BieyJqWUIL.method: TokenButler distills masked causal attention distributions into a lightweight predictor (<1% parameters) that generates low-dimensional importance queries at a depth stride and scores projected KV-cache keys for per-step budget selection while retaining the full cache.
BieyJqWUIL.key_idea: Distills attention distributions into low-dimensional importance queries and projected keys to dynamically select KV tokens while keeping the full cache.
BieyJqWUIL.evidence: Evaluated on a synthetic co-reference task, RULER, LongBench, and AIME24 with latency measurements.
BieyJqWUIL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree preserving the full KV cache with a lightweight (<1% parameter) predictor that accounts for selection overhead is practical.
BieyJqWUIL.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited conceptual novelty over TokenSelect/DSA/IndexMem, mismatched context lengths for quality (64K) versus speed (128K+), and missing peak memory metrics.

NxC756j1ih.one_liner: Detects subliminal traits in distillation datasets by optimizing a soft prompt and beam-search verbalizing it into text.
NxC756j1ih.problem: Distillation datasets can covertly transmit teacher traits (subliminal learning) that are illegible in the text itself.
NxC756j1ih.method: SALVE frames prompted subliminal learning as context distillation, optimizes a soft prompt on the dataset, queries the same model to verbalize the soft prompt into legible text, and uses beam search to stabilize recovery.
NxC756j1ih.key_idea: Optimizes a soft prompt on a distillation dataset and uses beam-search self-verbalization to recover the teacher's hidden trait as text.
NxC756j1ih.evidence: Evaluated on prompted subliminal learning datasets, student training interventions, and preference-data auditing.
NxC756j1ih.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree SALVE is simple, well-written, and reliably recovers hidden teacher traits in prompted subliminal learning settings.
NxC756j1ih.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over LARGO with beam search, idealized sampling assumptions in theory, and lack of calibration for unknown training risks.

I5hl3JId9G.one_liner: Applies top-p twice over KV cluster centroids to adaptively select attended clusters and allocate exact versus centroid attention.
I5hl3JId9G.problem: Existing top-p sparse attention methods pre-filter with a fixed-budget selector, preventing recovery of missed attention mass.
I5hl3JId9G.method: Double-P estimates cluster attention mass from size-weighted centroids across the full context, applies a first top-p threshold to select clusters, and applies a second top-p threshold to give high-mass clusters exact token attention while approximating remaining selected clusters by centroids.
I5hl3JId9G.key_idea: Uses two top-p passes over KV cluster centroids to adaptively select context clusters and split them into exact versus centroid attention.
I5hl3JId9G.evidence: Evaluated across long-context benchmarks against fixed-budget and cluster-based sparse attention baselines.
I5hl3JId9G.claimed_gains: Achieves near-zero accuracy drop, reduces attention computation overhead by up to 1.8x, and delivers up to 1.3x end-to-end decoding speedup.
I5hl3JId9G.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the two-pass top-p cluster selection is simple, well-motivated, and avoids modifying KV data structures.
I5hl3JId9G.main_concern: Reviewers note the omission of a direct comparison to Tactic and point out that some reported speedups rely on reconstructed rather than directly measured latency.

3eCpXmHlq3.one_liner: Analyzes Muon versus GD and Adam in a linear-transformer factual-recall model, showing spectral updates balance subject-relation learning.
3eCpXmHlq3.problem: How Muon's spectral orthogonalization alters feature-learning dynamics compared to gradient descent and Adam is poorly understood.
3eCpXmHlq3.method: The authors study continuous-time gradient flow (GF), spectral GF (Muon), and Sign GF (Adam) on a tractable factual-recall model with S subjects and R relations, deriving matching bounds on subject/relation learning-time ratios and error decay rates.
3eCpXmHlq3.key_idea: Derives invariant-manifold learning-time bounds on a linear-transformer factual-recall model to contrast GF, Spectral GF, and Sign GF.
3eCpXmHlq3.evidence: Supported by theoretical proofs on an invariant manifold and small-scale stochastic training experiments.
3eCpXmHlq3.claimed_gains: Reduces subject-to-relation learning-time ratio from Theta-tilde(sqrt(S/R)) under GF to Theta-tilde(1) under Spectral GF, improving error decay from 1/(T log T) to exp(-poly(T)).
3eCpXmHlq3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the invariant-manifold analysis with matching upper and lower bounds cleanly characterizes feature-learning speedups.
3eCpXmHlq3.main_concern: Reviewers point out that rank-one gradients on the invariant manifold collapse spectral orthogonalization into simple normalization, and empirical validation is limited.

frTOPatKvV.one_liner: Freezes non-routed interface parameters during MoE domain module fine-tuning so independently trained experts reinsert and compose cleanly.
frTOPatKvV.problem: Independently fine-tuned MoE domain modules lose much of their accuracy gains when reinserted into the shared model due to co-adaptation with interface parameters.
frTOPatKvV.method: The authors diagnose the reinsertion gap via controlled interventions and propose Interface-Frozen Fine-Tuning (IF-FT), which updates only routed domain experts while keeping all non-routed interface parameters fixed.
frTOPatKvV.key_idea: Freeze all parameters outside the routed domain experts during standalone module fine-tuning to prevent expert-interface co-adaptation.
frTOPatKvV.evidence: Experiments across seven domains on the 14B-parameter EMO modular MoE model, holding 3.9B parameters in memory during extracted training, and composition evaluations support the method.
frTOPatKvV.claimed_gains: IF-FT preserves standalone accuracy after reinsertion to within test-set noise, improves reinserted accuracy by up to 10 points over full-parameter module fine-tuning, and holds 3.9B of the 14B parameters in memory.
frTOPatKvV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that diagnosing expert-interface co-adaptation as the cause of reinsertion loss and reducing resident training memory from 14B to 3.9B are valuable practical contributions.
frTOPatKvV.main_concern: Reviewers note that freezing non-expert parameters is not itself new, ESFT baselines train fewer experts by default, and freezing the entire interface is not proven strictly necessary.

EDVb15mn6n.one_liner: Pre-trains a dual-stream symbolic regression model with cross-environment contrastive learning to separate invariant equation skeletons from parameters.
EDVb15mn6n.problem: Parameterized equation discovery suffers from distribution shifts and structural aliasing across environments, while existing methods search from scratch without a structural prior.
EDVb15mn6n.method: DisPV uses a dual-stream architecture that separates universal symbolic skeleton representations from environment-specific constants using cross-environment contrastive learning to align invariant structures.
EDVb15mn6n.key_idea: Disentangle invariant symbolic equation skeletons from parameter variations via a dual-stream pre-training architecture with cross-environment contrastive supervision.
EDVb15mn6n.evidence: Experiments on parameterized equation discovery benchmarks including an underdamped oscillator example, consistency analyses, and OOD tests support the framework.
EDVb15mn6n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear formulation of distribution shift and structural aliasing in parameterized equation discovery and the motivation for a pre-trained structural prior.
EDVb15mn6n.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the small noiseless benchmarks, best-of-10 reporting without variance, unclear attribution of gains, and structural consistency metrics that are guaranteed by aggregation.

kfaXAaXdWH.one_liner: Shortens long-horizon offline goal-conditioned RL value propagation using single-discount shortcut backups and selective reward compression.
kfaXAaXdWH.problem: Sparse rewards in long-horizon offline goal-conditioned RL require many Bellman backups to separate primitive action values.
kfaXAaXdWH.method: SSVL trains primitive action-value critics on stopped trajectory segments using a single-discount shortcut continuation, a frozen shortcut-aligned reference for selective reward compression, and an auxiliary Shortcut Value Consistency loss while deploying a flat policy.
kfaXAaXdWH.key_idea: Applies single-discount shortcut backups and consistency losses over trajectory segments during training to accelerate primitive-action value separation without hierarchical inference.
kfaXAaXdWH.evidence: Theoretical analysis of progress-state separation and empirical evaluation on state-based and visual OGBench tasks.
kfaXAaXdWH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate that SSVL matches or beats hierarchical GCRL methods on OGBench while retaining a flat policy at deployment.
kfaXAaXdWH.main_concern: Reviewers note that the theoretical alignment assumption presupposes the central property, gains at K=1 are unexplained, and novelty over OTA's shortcut mechanism is limited.

hygNIH1Dwf.one_liner: Measures per-example memorization in one training run by tracking representation disagreement with class centroids.
hygNIH1Dwf.problem: Estimating Feldman-Zhang memorization scores requires training many models, which is computationally prohibitive.
hygNIH1Dwf.method: The authors propose a single-run proxy that averages across training epochs how strongly a sample's position relative to class centroids in representation space disagrees with its observed label. They derive a sandwich bound relating this trajectory-averaged score to Feldman-Zhang memorization.
hygNIH1Dwf.key_idea: Tracks trajectory-averaged disagreement between an example's penultimate representation relative to class centroids and its assigned label in a single run.
hygNIH1Dwf.evidence: A theoretical sandwich bound and experiments on ImageNet and CIFAR-100 evaluate agreement with Feldman-Zhang scores, mislabel detection, and true-label recovery.
hygNIH1Dwf.claimed_gains: For mislabel detection on CIFAR-100 under asymmetric noise, AUROC decreases by less than one percentage point.
hygNIH1Dwf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the single-run representation-space proxy intuitive, easy to follow, and empirically effective on ImageNet and structured-noise mislabel detection.
hygNIH1Dwf.main_concern: Reviewers criticize weak or circular theoretical assumptions in the sandwich bound and remark justifications, as well as missing related memorization literature.

p3O3NQjP5W.one_liner: Decomposes LLM answer revision into content, social, and re-ask effects using matched donor controls and six audits.
p3O3NQjP5W.problem: Sycophancy evaluations compare against a no-pushback control assumed to be zero, conflating argument-driven, social, and re-ask revision.
p3O3NQjP5W.method: Matched-Presence Decomposition (MPD) swaps each prompt element with a donor element from another item and applies six statistical audits to separate content, social, and re-ask components, alongside a prompt requiring the model to state whether material is new.
p3O3NQjP5W.key_idea: Isolates content, social, and re-ask revision components by substituting prompt elements with matched donor elements from other items under six audits.
p3O3NQjP5W.evidence: Prediction-market experiments across four to seven open-weight LLM families and sycophancy benchmark audits.
p3O3NQjP5W.claimed_gains: A bare re-ask without parent changed answers in 59.7 to 82.2% of episodes (65.6 to 86.6% with parent), and the novelty-check prompt removed 19.4 to 46.8 points of drift.
p3O3NQjP5W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the matched-presence control design and separation of revision frequency from directional alignment.
p3O3NQjP5W.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the headline reask_only condition prepends a previously unseen parent comment on 73.6% of reply items, confounding zero-information drift claims.

0CAcw5qRGs.one_liner: Treats coding-agent execution feedback as a noisy measurement, combining budgeted randomized branching, verifier calibration, and AIPW credit assignment.
0CAcw5qRGs.problem: Branching RL for coding agents introduces selection bias from heuristic branch choices and gradient corruption from noisy leaf verifiers.
0CAcw5qRGs.method: BANC purchases branch and audit evaluations by expected policy-gradient effect against shadow-priced resource costs while logging randomized propensities. It calibrates raw verifier verdicts against higher-fidelity audits and computes action-level credit via a cross-fitted augmented inverse-propensity weighted (AIPW) estimator.
0CAcw5qRGs.key_idea: Combines shadow-priced randomized branch acquisition, selection-corrected verifier calibration, and AIPW estimation to de-bias coding-agent RL credit assignment.
0CAcw5qRGs.evidence: Evaluated via a 500-leaf verifier audit, 1,024-leaf calibration set, 2^3 factorial ablation, noise stress tests, and 5-seed coding RL runs across 640 tasks.
0CAcw5qRGs.claimed_gains: Cuts normalized gradient error from 0.50 to 0.34, reduces harmful update mass under 20% noise from 24.7% to 9.1%, and lowers adaptive selection bias from 0.148 to 0.021 (44% lower RMSE than IPS).
0CAcw5qRGs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise framing executable feedback as a selectively acquired noisy measurement and the thorough mechanism-level diagnostics and factorial ablations.
0CAcw5qRGs.main_concern: Reviewers note a statistical-test mismatch (per-task vs. per-seed n=5 p-values), ~10% extra GPU-hour cost, reliance on filterable repositories, and conditional-independence assumptions.

U3Bmzztjq3.one_liner: Augments PPO with a Pain channel that stores failure corrections only after closed-loop counterfactual replay verifies action fault.
U3Bmzztjq3.problem: Standard policy gradients and failure memories conflate exogenous bad luck with poor actions and forget rare, consequential lessons.
U3Bmzztjq3.method: PAIN-PPO pairs a standard PPO Advantage channel with a Pain channel: for candidate failures, it replays the episode under identical recorded noise with an alternative action, admits the correction if outcomes improve, and applies one-sided gradient retention constraints when needed.
U3Bmzztjq3.key_idea: Uses closed-loop same-noise counterfactual replay to verify whether an action caused a failure before storing it as a one-sided retention constraint alongside PPO.
U3Bmzztjq3.evidence: Evaluated in controlled simulations (corridor, sepsis simulator, maze) with paired-seed ablations and real-world financial market tape replays.
U3Bmzztjq3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the causal attribution-before-memory concept and the rigorous experimental controls isolating admission from retention.
U3Bmzztjq3.main_concern: Reviewers note heavy reliance on an exact same-realization replay oracle (and small-agent market-impact assumptions) without testing a learned verifier, plus gaps in theoretical guarantees.

E4L34c9WRE.one_liner: Uses feedforward hypernetworks and latent task embeddings for task-agnostic boundary detection and continual meta-learning.
E4L34c9WRE.problem: Continual meta-learning relies heavily on slow inner-loop MAML optimization and known task boundaries, limiting scalability to complex task-agnostic streams.
E4L34c9WRE.method: FLAME replaces gradient-based inner loops with a feedforward hypernetwork/(L)LoRA meta-learner conditioned on prototype task embeddings. The same latent embeddings drive task boundary detection, identity estimation, and replay consolidation for recurring tasks.
E4L34c9WRE.key_idea: Uses a single feedforward context embedding both to generate fast-adaptation weights via hypernetworks and to detect task boundaries and cluster identities.
E4L34c9WRE.evidence: Evaluated across domain shifts, recurring tasks, sequential image datasets (including MNIST-Rotations), and text classification, measuring retained accuracy and test-time adaptation latency.
E4L34c9WRE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the unified task-agnostic design separating "what" (latent task inference) from "how" (hypernetwork adaptation) and the 15x faster TTA latency over MAML.
E4L34c9WRE.main_concern: Reviewers note an unspecified test-time selection rule for dataset embeddings s^d in nested adaptation, presentation-window assumptions in boundary detection, and lower learning accuracy than MAML.

9ICxBlc0oe.one_liner: Formulates multi-turn LLM RL as a cooperative sequential game to compute subgame-perfect equilibrium rollout advantages without a critic.
9ICxBlc0oe.problem: Critic-free group-based RL suffers from imprecise trajectory-level credit assignment under sparse, delayed rewards in multi-turn LLM tasks.
9ICxBlc0oe.method: Sequential Equilibrium Policy Optimization (SEPO) models multi-turn interaction as a cooperative sequential game, chunking turns and sampling prefix-shared rollouts with in-chunk exploration and suffix exploitation to approximate best-response trajectory advantages.
9ICxBlc0oe.key_idea: Structures critic-free multi-turn rollouts via prefix sharing, in-chunk exploration, and suffix exploitation derived from a cooperative sequential game best-response formulation.
9ICxBlc0oe.evidence: Evaluated on ALFWorld, WebShop, and a third task family across multiple model sizes, including equal-budget controls.
9ICxBlc0oe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the prefix-shared chunked rollout design clean and well-tested with equal-budget controls.
9ICxBlc0oe.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the gap between Theorem 4.4 (which assumes independent tabular policies per history and exact best responses) and the shared-parameter PPO implementation, plus extra rollout cost.

Mq9WVsAp9x.one_liner: Exposes prompts and interaction histories as code variables within a recursive `invoke` primitive to replace specialized agent harnesses.
Mq9WVsAp9x.problem: Long-horizon memory and self-improving agent workflows typically require complex, specialized engineering harnesses beyond standard agent loops.
Mq9WVsAp9x.method: JAZ provides a single `invoke` primitive where the LLM writes executable code (including recursive `invoke` calls) and all prompt inputs and REPL interaction histories are directly accessible as variables in the code environment, paired with built-in hooks.
Mq9WVsAp9x.key_idea: Treats all prompt inputs and full interaction histories as program variables inside a recursive code-execution `invoke` loop.
Mq9WVsAp9x.evidence: Evaluated on long-range recall (StuLife) and self-improvement tasks against Letta and CodeAct+subagents.
Mq9WVsAp9x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exposing prompts and histories as REPL variables is a clean, practical interface that avoids manual string copying and reduces cost.
Mq9WVsAp9x.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty over CodeAct/RLM harnesses, note that prompt variables and history variables are confounded in ablations, and observe reliance on careful workflow prompting.

cEFOjGNbBL.one_liner: Trains an inverse dynamics model via self-play by executing best-guess actions to follow a video planner without action labels.
cEFOjGNbBL.problem: Executing plans from video generative models typically requires inverse dynamics models trained on large, human-collected video-action datasets.
cEFOjGNbBL.method: Mirror attempts to follow a video planner's visual trajectories by executing its current inverse dynamics guesses in the environment and iteratively training on the resulting self-collected video-action pairs.
cEFOjGNbBL.key_idea: Self-improves a video-to-action inverse dynamics model by repeatedly trying to follow generated visual plans in the environment and training on achieved transitions.
cEFOjGNbBL.evidence: Evaluated on Atari, OGBench, DeepMind Control, Minecraft BASALT, and Minecraft survival/diamond tasks with learned and oracle video planners.
cEFOjGNbBL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple self-supervised grounding loop and strong empirical results on long-horizon Minecraft tasks without action labels.
cEFOjGNbBL.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over Grounding (conditioning on multiple future frames vs. one), reliance on expert/oracle video planners in comparisons, and incomplete positioning against SILVR.

RIXrEpabOM.one_liner: Batches token states across different positions and recurrence depths on a diagonal wavefront for looped-LM self-speculative decoding.
RIXrEpabOM.problem: Looped language models incur high sequential latency from T recurrent-block calls per token, and draft-then-verify suffers from phase separation.
RIXrEpabOM.method: Wavefront Decoding (WFD) uses shallow recurrence outputs as drafts and leverages weight sharing to batch tokens at different positions and recurrence depths along a diagonal wavefront, concurrently drafting and verifying while optionally sharing KV across recurrences.
RIXrEpabOM.key_idea: Organizes tokens at staggered positions and recurrence depths into a diagonal wavefront to batch drafting and full-depth verification in the same recurrent-block calls.
RIXrEpabOM.evidence: Evaluated across six Spec-Bench categories on Ouro-2.6B and Huginn-3.5B, with acceptance-rate, batch-size, context-length, and CUDA-graph analyses.
RIXrEpabOM.claimed_gains: Achieves 2.42x speedup on Ouro-2.6B and 3.54x on Huginn-3.5B over autoregressive decoding, increasing to 4.81x on Huginn-3.5B with cross-recurrence KV sharing.
RIXrEpabOM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the diagonal wavefront schedule a natural, training-free way to eliminate draft-verify phase boundaries in looped LMs.
RIXrEpabOM.main_concern: Reviewers note limited workload/model scale (batch size 1, 2.6B/3.5B models, no code-generation tasks), missing LoopSpec comparison, and unsupported lossless claims beyond greedy decoding.

qsERMBYyPX.one_liner: Triggers embodied exploration to disambiguate spoken instructions when mutual information shows intent uncertainty affects the next action.
qsERMBYyPX.problem: Ambiguous spoken instructions cause task failures in embodied control, yet resolving every linguistic ambiguity before acting is unnecessary and inefficient.
qsERMBYyPX.method: The authors propose a probabilistic-symbolic framework that measures speech-induced action uncertainty via mutual information between intent and next action, maps candidate intents and observations into a shared symbolic space, and aligns world constraints to actively explore discriminative evidence.
qsERMBYyPX.key_idea: Triggers active environmental disambiguation only when mutual information indicates speech intent uncertainty propagates to action disagreement in a shared symbolic space.
qsERMBYyPX.evidence: Experiments on SPEAR-Bench and REI-Bench embodied control benchmarks.
qsERMBYyPX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating intent uncertainty from action uncertainty is a practical and well-motivated criterion for embodied speech disambiguation.
qsERMBYyPX.main_concern: Experimental reporting lacks sample sizes, repetition counts, and confidence intervals, and environmental exploration cannot resolve ambiguities when physical evidence is absent or identical.

apWpDNjPdO.one_liner: Identifies horizon-induced mutual-information decay in goal-conditioned policies and distills short-horizon teacher input Jacobians into long-horizon policies.
apWpDNjPdO.problem: Increasing goal relabeling horizons degrades goal-conditioned policy generalization even when tested on nearby subgoals, shifting sensitivity from goals to states.
apWpDNjPdO.method: The authors decouple training and evaluation horizons using oracle planners, prove conditional mutual information between actions and hindsight goals decreases with horizon, and distill short-horizon teacher input Jacobians into long-horizon policies via Sobolev bootstrapping.
apWpDNjPdO.key_idea: Distills input Jacobians from a short-horizon goal-conditioned teacher policy into a long-horizon policy to counter mutual-information decay.
apWpDNjPdO.evidence: Proved a monotonic mutual-information theorem and evaluated on maze and combinatorial cube-manipulation benchmarks.
apWpDNjPdO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the informational curse of horizon and its decoupling of training versus evaluation horizons to be a fresh, insightful perspective on goal-conditioned RL.
apWpDNjPdO.main_concern: Reviewers note a theoretical gap between Gaussian Fisher-information guarantees and flow-matching policies, vulnerability to noisy long-horizon critics, and inconsistent numbers and seed counts across tables.

d83mBTrpiJ.one_liner: Encodes text into multiscale residual VQ-VAE concept levels and generates each level's codes in parallel from coarse to fine.
d83mBTrpiJ.problem: Diffusion language models suffer rapid quality loss at low step counts while processing the full sequence at every denoising step.
d83mBTrpiJ.method: Next Concept Modeling (NCM) trains a multiscale residual VQ-VAE to encode text into hierarchical discrete code levels, then uses a transformer to predict all tokens within each level in parallel from coarse to fine.
d83mBTrpiJ.key_idea: Generates text coarse-to-fine by predicting all discrete codes within each multiscale residual VQ-VAE level in parallel.
d83mBTrpiJ.evidence: Evaluated at ~100M scale on LM1B, OpenWebText, WMT14 translation, and XSum summarization against diffusion and non-AR baselines.
d83mBTrpiJ.claimed_gains: At ~100M scale, NCM beats the strongest DLM on LM1B using 11x fewer steps and running 21x faster, and samples up to 31x faster than ELF with guidance on XSum.
d83mBTrpiJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean adaptation of VAR-style coarse-to-fine parallel prediction to text and the strong measured speedups on LM1B and XSum.
d83mBTrpiJ.main_concern: Reviewers note the lack of an autoregressive baseline for scaling comparison, missing ablations of VQ-VAE levels and refiners, and lower entropy confounding Gen. PPL on OpenWebText.

c2exIjjkYB.one_liner: Shards clean prefixes across ranks while keeping corrupted block K/Vs and gradients local for distributed long-context block diffusion training.
c2exIjjkYB.problem: Conventional context parallelism in block diffusion language models wastes communication and activation memory by exchanging block-specific corrupted K/Vs.
c2exIjjkYB.method: Block Parallelism (BP) assigns each corrupted target block to one rank; Context-Sharded BP (CSBP) additionally shards the shared clean prefix across ranks, keeping corrupted K/Vs and gradients local while preserving exact training semantics.
c2exIjjkYB.key_idea: Assigns corrupted target blocks locally per rank while sharding the shared clean prefix across ranks to eliminate corrupted K/V communication.
c2exIjjkYB.evidence: Proved exact loss/gradient equivalence and benchmarked on 16 H200 GPUs at 256K context across 3B-27B models and speculative drafters.
c2exIjjkYB.claimed_gains: On 16 H200 GPUs at 256K context, CSBP improves throughput by 1.18-1.45x for 3B-26B-A4B SFT and 1.27-1.33x for 27B AR-to-BDLM conversion.
c2exIjjkYB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree CSBP exploits the block-separable BDLM objective cleanly, preserves exact gradients, and delivers consistent long-context throughput gains.
c2exIjjkYB.main_concern: Reviewers argue that BP is never used alone and CSBP acts as a block-aligned placement inside CP, while the baseline CP exchanges masked-out K/Vs rather than using a mask-aware CP control.

oFNONZCKdX.one_liner: Trains a 340M-parameter neural operator on 250k 3D PCB simulations to jointly predict electromagnetic fields and S-parameters.
oFNONZCKdX.problem: Existing electromagnetic surrogates specialize in narrow design families and predict either spatial fields or aggregate S-parameters rather than both.
oFNONZCKdX.method: The authors generate 250k simulations across 25 3D PCB/package families, train a 340M-parameter cross-attention transformer with impedance-aware scaling and heteroscedastic field loss, and release the EMVal suite.
oFNONZCKdX.key_idea: Jointly supervises 3D complex electromagnetic fields and S-parameters in a 340M cross-attention operator to improve out-of-distribution geometry generalization.
oFNONZCKdX.evidence: Evaluated on 25 training families and ~2k OOD designs from two held-out families in EMVal, with joint vs. S-parameter-only ablations.
oFNONZCKdX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the 250k 3D EM dataset and agree that joint field supervision substantially improves held-out-family S-parameter generalization (33% riRMSE and 48% MAE reductions in Table 1).
oFNONZCKdX.main_concern: Reviewers note that OOD evaluation covers only two unnamed held-out families without per-family breakdowns, lacks real-data or downstream fine-tuning tests, and lacks justification for the Student-t loss.

rQp8HeWXue.one_liner: Audits how changing classifiers and representations shifts benchmark difficulty rankings of binary label pairs at fixed score resolution.
rQp8HeWXue.problem: Benchmark difficulty rankings are often treated as intrinsic dataset properties, leaving unclear how sensitive they are to the choice of classifier probe and representation.
rQp8HeWXue.method: Holding examples and grouped folds fixed, the authors vary representations and four supervised probes to rank binary label-pair tasks by out-of-fold balanced accuracy, measuring rank shifts and minimum required hard-set changes up to a 0.02 score resolution.
rQp8HeWXue.key_idea: Measures rank shifts and minimum hard-set overlap across probes and representations at fixed examples and score resolution to test whether difficulty rankings are procedure-relative.
rQp8HeWXue.evidence: Evaluated on 400 AIOps2025 failure events (55 pairs), three RCAEval RE1 systems, and six OpenML datasets across three representations and four probes.
rQp8HeWXue.claimed_gains: Six probe contrasts yield mean absolute rank shifts of 3.69–14.55 positions on AIOps2025, with logistic regression and random forest sharing only 3 of their top 10 hardest pairs and requiring 3–6 changes across ten splits.
rQp8HeWXue.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the tightly controlled experimental protocol (fixed samples, grouped folds, and confound checks) isolating probe and representation effects.
rQp8HeWXue.main_concern: Reviewers note the study is largely descriptive/expected without random-ranking baselines, underlying probe accuracy distributions, or analysis of why specific pairs move.

c2M4Xq4Fia.one_liner: Selects textual skill revision operators per round using an optimizer LLM conditioned on execution feedback and outcome history.
c2M4Xq4Fia.problem: Fixed skill-revision operators in self-evolving LLM agents fail to generalize across tasks and stall when applied repeatedly.
c2M4Xq4Fia.method: StraTune lets a frozen optimizer LLM choose among search strategies and revision forms each round based on current execution feedback and past operator outcomes, screening candidates on a small set before validation.
c2M4Xq4Fia.key_idea: Conditions an optimizer LLM on execution feedback and operator outcome history to dynamically select search strategies and revision forms each round.
c2M4Xq4Fia.evidence: Evaluations across four benchmarks and two LLM settings against five baselines, plus ablations on fixed, random, cyclic, and bandit selectors.
c2M4Xq4Fia.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem practical and appreciate the controlled comparison protocol and broad ablations across four tasks.
c2M4Xq4Fia.main_concern: Evidence that per-round adaptive selection drives gains over cyclic or fixed operators is statistically weak (single-run ablations and small margins).

6IEi70e1SP.one_liner: Characterizes PAC learnability of inference-time alignment via a finite alignment dimension and pairwise-comparator tournaments.
6IEi70e1SP.problem: Inference-time alignment lacks a statistical learning characterization when rewards are unknown and must be learned from data.
6IEi70e1SP.method: Formulates inference-time alignment as weak-to-strong PAC learning, defines the alignment dimension of a reward class, proves learnability holds iff this dimension is finite, and constructs a learner via pairwise comparison and tournament selection.
6IEi70e1SP.key_idea: Defines the combinatorial alignment dimension and proves it characterizes PAC learnability of inference-time alignment via pairwise-comparator tournaments.
6IEi70e1SP.evidence: Purely theoretical upper and lower bounds characterizing alignment learnability.
6IEi70e1SP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the alignment dimension provides a clean necessary-and-sufficient PAC characterization of inference-time alignment.
6IEi70e1SP.main_concern: Reviewers note the lack of empirical validation or guidance for estimating the alignment dimension in practice, plus an arithmetic error in Example 3.

DMJ4oD8MJ8.one_liner: Matches flow-model source components to elemental-family regions in crystal VAE latent spaces for controllable crystal generation.
DMJ4oD8MJ8.problem: Latent crystal generative models lack fine-grained control over elemental-family composition during generation.
DMJ4oD8MJ8.method: Identifies that crystal VAEs naturally cluster atom-wise latents by elemental family, assigns each family a distinct source component, and trains a family-matched flow model so inference can follow user-specified family templates.
DMJ4oD8MJ8.key_idea: Exploits emergent elemental-family clustering in crystal VAE latents by pairing family-indexed Gaussian source components with family-matched flow training.
DMJ4oD8MJ8.evidence: Evaluated on MP-20 and MPTS-52 crystal datasets with latent-space nearest-neighbor analyses and generation metrics.
DMJ4oD8MJ8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple and clear, with thorough empirical analysis of VAE latent clustering across datasets.
DMJ4oD8MJ8.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty in both the VAE clustering observation and flow matching, missing comparisons to composition-conditioned baselines, and lower stability/SUN than ADiT.

2r1nz2sGk4.one_liner: Reinterprets linear Echo State Networks as non-stationary Gaussian Processes and replaces recurrence with tunable random Fourier features.
2r1nz2sGk4.problem: Nonlinear recurrent Echo State Networks (ESNs) are sequential to evaluate, while the kernel structure of parallelizable linear ESNs is poorly understood.
2r1nz2sGk4.method: The authors show that a finite-width linear ESN induces a matrix-valued Gaussian Process whose stationarity depends on reservoir topology. Motivated by this, TUNE replaces recurrent dynamics with random Fourier features drawn from a parameterizable spectral measure combined with tunable temporal weighting.
2r1nz2sGk4.key_idea: Replaces linear ESN recurrence with random Fourier features from a parameterizable spectral measure and tunable temporal envelopes.
2r1nz2sGk4.evidence: Theoretical GP kernel derivations and experiments across time-series classification and long-term forecasting tasks.
2r1nz2sGk4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the Gaussian Process kernel perspective on linear ESN reservoir topologies interesting and the empirical study broad.
2r1nz2sGk4.main_concern: Reviewers identify mathematical gaps in the GP/local-stationarity proofs (missing assumptions and an incorrect empirical kernel lemma) and note incremental novelty over ParalESN alongside unclear experimental protocols.

yDVGfmSNEy.one_liner: Performs targeted bit-flip attacks on LLMs using keyword-focused loss and auxiliary utility scoring.
yDVGfmSNEy.problem: Existing bit-flip attacks on LLMs induce untargeted degradation rather than manipulating outputs for specific prompts.
yDVGfmSNEy.method: The authors propose TFL, which combines a keyword-focused attack loss to promote target tokens in generative outputs with an auxiliary utility score to limit collateral degradation on benign inputs.
yDVGfmSNEy.key_idea: Optimizes weight bit flips using a masked keyword-focused loss paired with an auxiliary utility score on benign data.
yDVGfmSNEy.evidence: Evaluations span factual QA, summarization, code generation, and mathematical reasoning across Qwen, DeepSeek, and Llama models.
yDVGfmSNEy.claimed_gains: TFL induces targeted output changes with only 1–9 weight bit flips while incurring substantially less collateral degradation than baselines.
yDVGfmSNEy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that investigating targeted bit-flip attacks on LLMs is an interesting and important security problem.
yDVGfmSNEy.main_concern: Reviewers note a gap between software and hardware threat models, very small target attack sample sizes, weak baselines, and lack of theoretical analysis for the attack loss.

oezJMwixbB.one_liner: Derives model-agnostic Gaussian localization conditions for asymptotically valid local learning coefficient estimation.
oezJMwixbB.problem: In sampling-based local learning coefficient estimation, weak or excessive Gaussian localization distorts the measured local model complexity.
oezJMwixbB.method: By resolving the loss and localizer in a common geometric representation, the authors derive model-agnostic localization growth conditions that guarantee asymptotic convergence to the target LLC across analytic models, along with classwise counterexamples.
oezJMwixbB.key_idea: Balances localization strength against sample size in a common geometric representation to prevent remote low-loss leakage and artificial contraction.
oezJMwixbB.evidence: Theoretical proofs and counterexamples are accompanied by toy numerical experiments and DNN experiments on grokking, learning rate transitions, and MNIST.
oezJMwixbB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses a significant foundational gap in LLC estimation with model-agnostic theoretical conditions.
oezJMwixbB.main_concern: Reviewers find the mathematical exposition insufficiently self-contained for non-experts and note that DNN experiments run at fixed finite scale do not show validity changing qualitative conclusions.

fcd8xhAB1p.one_liner: Models edge dependencies in Bayesian causal discovery using normalizing flows and updates node potentials via SVGD in acyclicity space.
fcd8xhAB1p.problem: Existing Bayesian causal discovery methods fail to model dependencies between graph edges and struggle to capture multimodal DAG posteriors.
fcd8xhAB1p.method: SVI-DAG uses normalizing flows conditioned on node potentials to capture dependencies between edge logits for expressive posterior approximation over DAGs. To prevent mode collapse during ELBO optimization, it applies Stein variational gradient descent (SVGD) to update node potentials using a kernel in acyclicity space.
fcd8xhAB1p.key_idea: Combining normalizing flows for dependent edge-logit posteriors with acyclicity-space SVGD updates on node potentials.
fcd8xhAB1p.evidence: Benchmarked against five Bayesian DAG learning methods on linear/nonlinear synthetic settings and the real-world Sachs dataset.
fcd8xhAB1p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling joint edge dependencies to represent multimodal DAG posteriors addresses an important challenge in Bayesian causal discovery.
fcd8xhAB1p.main_concern: Reviewers note weak empirical evidence of improved multimodal posterior coverage, mixed results on Sachs (poor Brier score and SHD despite high F1), and cases where removing SVGD improves accuracy.

jtEinwdJSl.one_liner: Establishes minimax squared prediction risk for nonparametric Besov regression on an unknown low-dimensional linear subspace under Gaussian design.
jtEinwdJSl.problem: High-dimensional nonparametric regression is faster when functions depend on a few smooth coordinates, but the additional statistical cost of learning those unknown coordinates from data was not sharply characterized.
jtEinwdJSl.method: Under standard Gaussian design and noise for f(x) = g(W^T x) with unknown orthonormal W in R^{d×k} and g in a B^s_{2,q}(R^k) ball, the authors derive matching minimax bounds separating known-subspace estimation from unknown-representation cost, plus a finite-resolution coordinate-frame metric in a two-block matrix-dilation Besov model.
jtEinwdJSl.key_idea: Derives dimension-free minimax risk separating known-subspace Besov estimation from the (m/n) log(1+n/m) representation-learning penalty and a finite-resolution metric on coordinate frames.
jtEinwdJSl.evidence: Theoretical minimax lower and upper bounds and finite-resolution covering analysis.
jtEinwdJSl.claimed_gains: Establishes minimax squared prediction risk R_n^* ≍ n^{-2s/(2s+k)} + (m/n) log(1 + n/m) for m = k(d-k) = o(n) with constants independent of d.
jtEinwdJSl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem of quantifying the statistical cost of unknown anisotropic smooth coordinates theoretically interesting and clarifying.
jtEinwdJSl.main_concern: Reviewers note the absence of a practically implementable estimation algorithm and poor accessibility and motivation of the notation and Besov assumptions.

1LyORXnEZ0.one_liner: Defines instance difficulty via model-series competence monotonicity to identify transitional problems and build static easy-to-hard curricula.
1LyORXnEZ0.problem: Static curriculum difficulty proxies are learner-agnostic and unreliable, while dynamic gradient-based curricula incur high training overhead.
1LyORXnEZ0.method: The authors calibrate problem difficulty against a series of models of increasing competence (varying size, checkpoints, context length, or skill conditioning), define transitional problems solved by all models at or above a competence level, and train learners on easy-to-hard progressions over these levels.
1LyORXnEZ0.key_idea: Assigns each example a difficulty level from the competence threshold where a series of progressively stronger models monotonically transitions from failure to success.
1LyORXnEZ0.evidence: Evaluated across diverse model series and tasks (including chess and math) comparing transitional-problem curricula against random and alternative training strategies.
1LyORXnEZ0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the model-competence-based definition of transitional problems clear, intuitive, and well-motivated.
1LyORXnEZ0.main_concern: Reviewers point out inconsistent construction of model series across experiments (confounding the source of gains), unequal level sizes causing oversampling relative to random baselines, and missing cost/discussion details.

QhTOcpy7d6.one_liner: Trains an autoregressive model on interleaved pre-image, action-text, and post-image triples to test whether visual transition simulation aids verb learning.
QhTOcpy7d6.problem: Static image-text alignment captures object percepts but does not model how actions transform world states, which may be necessary to ground result verbs.
QhTOcpy7d6.method: The authors train an autoregressive model on (pre-condition image, action description, post-condition image) triples with three objectives—inferring the action from the transition, predicting the post-condition image, and reconstructing the pre-condition image—and ablate visual simulation against language supervision.
QhTOcpy7d6.key_idea: Combines bidirectional visual state-transition prediction with action inference on pre/post image triples to supply causal state-change supervision for grounded verb acquisition.
QhTOcpy7d6.evidence: Controlled ablations across training mixtures, sequence orders, visual losses, and real-video data measuring lexical acquisition across nouns, result verbs, and manner verbs.
QhTOcpy7d6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the linguistically motivated hypothesis linking world-state simulation to result-verb versus manner-verb acquisition and the controlled ablation design.
QhTOcpy7d6.main_concern: Reviewers question whether lexical-surprisal and nAoA gains reflect genuine causal world modeling rather than auxiliary visual supervision or data augmentation, and note ambiguity in the unseen-word evaluation.

hjSsB7ZTL9.one_liner: Decouples visual depth from backbone depth in encoder-free MLLMs via a deep, narrow visual expert initialized from pretrained encoders.
hjSsB7ZTL9.problem: Shallow encoder-free MLLMs eliminate vision-encoder prefill latency but suffer from weak multimodal accuracy due to insufficient visual processing depth.
hjSsB7ZTL9.method: After analyzing the accuracy-latency design space of encoder-free MLLMs, the authors introduce DeCoVE, which trades visual branch width for greater depth independently of backbone depth and initializes visual layers from pretrained vision encoders to build DeCoVE-3B.
hjSsB7ZTL9.key_idea: Trades visual branch width for depth in an encoder-free MLLM backbone and initializes the deep compact visual expert from pretrained vision-encoder weights.
hjSsB7ZTL9.evidence: Design-space analysis, architectural ablations, and evaluation of DeCoVE-3B across 13 multimodal benchmarks against encoder-free baselines and Qwen3.5-VL 2B.
hjSsB7ZTL9.claimed_gains: DeCoVE-3B reduces prefill latency by 41.5% across 13 benchmarks while remaining competitive with Qwen3.5-VL 2B.
hjSsB7ZTL9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the systematic design-space analysis diagnosing shallow visual depth and the practical accuracy-latency trade-off across 13 benchmarks.
hjSsB7ZTL9.main_concern: Reviewers note inconsistent implementation details (convolution strides and learning rates), under-documented latency protocols, modest absolute TTFT savings over total generation time, and static-image-only scope.

6F334RnMBT.one_liner: Extracts a 13-factor preference library from user histories and dynamically selects relevant factors to guide personalized LLM generation.
6F334RnMBT.problem: Existing LLM personalization methods rely on surface-level interactions or undifferentiated user histories, missing reusable preference mechanisms shared across tasks.
6F334RnMBT.method: PersonaFactor mines evidence-grounded rationales and clusters recurring patterns across tasks into 13 interpretable preference factors, then uses a dynamic selector at inference time to choose relevant factors for each user history and request, complemented by representation analyses.
6F334RnMBT.key_idea: Distills cross-task user histories into a 13-factor preference library and dynamically selects request-relevant factors to condition prompted LLM generation.
6F334RnMBT.evidence: Evaluated across four personalization benchmarks (including LaMP, LaMP-QA, PersonalLLM, and LongLaMP) and four open and proprietary LLM backbones, plus representation analyses.
6F334RnMBT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple prompt-based design requiring no model training and its consistent evaluation across four benchmarks and multiple LLM backbones.
6F334RnMBT.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the heuristic 13-factor library outperforms existing factor sets like CoPA, note input/prompt confounds on LongLaMP, and miss a cost-benefit analysis of dynamic selection.

D8ht0aXHGC.one_liner: Places video, audio, silence, and text tokens on one append-only 80-ms causal timeline for continuous duplex video-language interaction.
D8ht0aXHGC.problem: Turn-based video-language models defer newly arriving observations until the next turn, preventing continuous real-time perception during response generation.
D8ht0aXHGC.method: Aero Realtime (4B) removes turn boundaries by interleaving visual states, 80-ms audio slots, and single lexical or silence tokens in one append-only causal stream, trained on 1.5M QA samples over 713K videos with silence-label masking and served incrementally.
D8ht0aXHGC.key_idea: Interleaves incoming visual states, 80-ms audio slots, and predicted lexical or silence tokens on a single append-only causal timeline trained with silence-label masking.
D8ht0aXHGC.evidence: Trained on 1.5M QA samples across 713K videos and evaluated on OVOBench and 20-minute streaming latency benchmarks.
D8ht0aXHGC.claimed_gains: Achieves 48.31 on OVOBench with 84-ms median and 173-ms P95 processing lag over the first 20 minutes.
D8ht0aXHGC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the unified append-only causal-stream formulation and the end-to-end system covering architecture, data, training, and incremental serving.
D8ht0aXHGC.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments do not directly verify whether newly arriving evidence during generation improves ongoing responses, and point out lower OVOBench accuracy than baselines plus unsupported user interruptions.

lXCjZCE3aF.one_liner: Adapts LVLMs to missing modalities via frozen-teacher LoRA self-distillation paired with Fisher-information drift detection and restoration.
lXCjZCE3aF.problem: Autoregressive LVLMs degrade under missing or noisy test-time modalities, while entropy-based test-time adaptation fails and continual updates accumulate drift.
lXCjZCE3aF.method: TTSD-FAR uses a complete-modality frozen teacher to distill into a LoRA student fed synthetically masked views, updating minimal parameters. Fisher-Anchored Restoration (FAR) monitors Fisher information stability to halt adaptation at convergence and reactivate/restore upon distribution shift.
lXCjZCE3aF.key_idea: Distills a frozen complete-modality teacher into a masked-input LoRA student while gating continual updates and restoration using Fisher information stability.
lXCjZCE3aF.evidence: Evaluated across three affective computing datasets under multiple missing-modality ratios with FAR, LoRA-rank, and smaller-backbone ablations.
lXCjZCE3aF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find parameter-efficient feature-level self-distillation for missing-modality LVLMs practical and well-evaluated across datasets and missing ratios.
lXCjZCE3aF.main_concern: Reviewers note that updates require complete-modality samples at test time (preventing adaptation on purely incomplete streams), cite strong overlap with prior work (MiDl, EATA), and question FAR's convergence guarantees.

vCvi6faXfo.one_liner: Jointly trains one policy as solver and self-refiner under GRPO using wrong-first sampling, answer-free prompts, and binary verifiers.
vCvi6faXfo.problem: Outcome-only RLVR never teaches models to inspect and fix intermediate reasoning errors, while prior self-refinement training requires external teachers, step annotations, or separate critics.
vCvi6faXfo.method: SR-GRPO trains a single shared policy jointly as solver and refiner via GRPO using only the binary outcome verifier. It combines wrong-first sampling to focus refinement on genuine errors, a ground-truth-free refinement prompt deployable at inference, and self-distillation recycling verified refinements back into solver updates.
vCvi6faXfo.key_idea: Jointly optimizes a single solver-refiner policy via GRPO using wrong-first sampling, answer-free refinement prompts, and self-distilled verified refinements.
vCvi6faXfo.evidence: Evaluated on mathematical benchmarks (including AIME, HMMT) plus GPQA Diamond and MMLU-Pro across DeepSeek-1.5B, Nemotron-1.5B, and Qwen3-4B with ablations.
vCvi6faXfo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the strong direct-solving empirical gains (4.1–8.5 points over GRPO across three backbones) without requiring inference-time refinement or extra critics.
vCvi6faXfo.main_concern: Reviewers show that subtracting initial correctness in the refinement reward cancels out under GRPO group normalization and find the off-policy cross-context recycling update underspecified.

sjGaLWeD8i.one_liner: Detects surface-feature label leakage in binary-choice truth benchmarks via a logistic classifier and prunes leakage-reinforcing pairs.
sjGaLWeD8i.problem: Binary-choice truthfulness benchmarks contain systematic surface-level differences between true and false answers, letting models score above chance without reasoning.
sjGaLWeD8i.method: The authors train a six-feature logistic classifier to detect surface-level answer leakage without seeing the question, then propose Audit-Prune to iteratively remove the most leakage-reinforcing pairs. They release a cleaned version of TruthfulQA with surface leakage reduced near chance.
sjGaLWeD8i.key_idea: Audits binary-choice benchmarks with a question-free six-feature logistic classifier and greedily prunes pairs that reinforce surface-feature leakage.
sjGaLWeD8i.evidence: Audited TruthfulQA and additional benchmarks with the six-feature classifier and evaluated leakage reduction after Audit-Prune.
sjGaLWeD8i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree benchmark surface-feature leakage is a real issue and find the diagnostic and pruning procedure simple and interpretable.
sjGaLWeD8i.main_concern: Reviewers question pruning ~40% of TruthfulQA (shifting categories), treating natural misconception features like negation as pure bias, and using global rather than within-question audit metrics.

HlTI2ytUkO.one_liner: Trains an end-to-end DINOv2-initialized Vision Transformer on large synthetic corpora for stereo matching without cost volumes or GRU refinement.
HlTI2ytUkO.problem: Stereo reconstruction still relies heavily on stereo-specific architectural inductive biases like cost volumes and iterative GRU refinement, assumed necessary for accuracy and speed.
HlTI2ytUkO.method: NBS (No Bias Stereo) removes stereo-specific architectural components and trains a minimalist end-to-end DINOv2-initialized Vision Transformer (with a DPT head) on large-scale synthetic stereo corpora to directly regress disparity.
HlTI2ytUkO.key_idea: Replaces stereo cost volumes and iterative refinement with a DINOv2-initialized Vision Transformer trained end-to-end on large-scale synthetic stereo data.
HlTI2ytUkO.evidence: Evaluated on ETH3D and four additional stereo benchmarks, plus runtime comparisons against specialized stereo models.
HlTI2ytUkO.claimed_gains: Ranks first on ETH3D, leads on most metrics across four other benchmarks, and runs 4x faster than the previous best method.
HlTI2ytUkO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the ETH3D accuracy and 4x runtime speedup empirically impressive and practically relevant.
HlTI2ytUkO.main_concern: Reviewers argue the ViT+DPT recipe is anticipated by CroCo v2, DA3, and VGGT, overstates being bias-free given DINOv2 pretraining, and lacks ablations disentangling architecture from data scale.

FiYnuRoyrD.one_liner: Decomposes Neural ODE adjoint gradients for Lyapunov-certified online training and derives a derivative-free stored-segment Gauss-Newton algorithm.
FiYnuRoyrD.problem: Online streaming training of Neural ODEs lacks Lyapunov stability guarantees because adjoint trajectory gradients appeared to lack regressor-times-parameter-error structure.
FiYnuRoyrD.method: The authors decompose Neural ODE adjoint gradients into a positive semi-definite trajectory operator on parameter error plus a horizon-bounded nonlinear perturbation, yielding quadratic Lyapunov stability certificates. Extending to stored segments yields NODE-CL, a batched forward-sensitivity Gauss-Newton concurrent learning update requiring no state-derivative estimates.
FiYnuRoyrD.key_idea: Decomposes adjoint gradients into a PSD trajectory operator plus bounded perturbation to certify Lyapunov stability and derive derivative-free stored-segment Gauss-Newton updates.
FiYnuRoyrD.evidence: Constructive Lyapunov convergence proofs plus empirical evaluation on four DeepMind Control Suite domains under clean and noisy velocity measurements.
FiYnuRoyrD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value bridging Neural ODE trajectory gradients with Lyapunov adaptive-control analysis and deriving a derivative-free concurrent learning method.
FiYnuRoyrD.main_concern: Reviewers point out that experimental gains are tuned for performance rather than verified to satisfy the conservative theoretical stability conditions, and note missing component ablations.

S2KSOSEFaH.one_liner: Computes column-wise one-sparse ternary steepest-descent updates under a normalized 1-to-1 operator norm using compact low-precision gradient histories.
