S2KSOSEFaH.problem: Full-parameter LLM fine-tuning incurs heavy optimizer state memory, while matrix-valued alternatives like Muon alter update geometry relative to AdamW-pretrained models.
S2KSOSEFaH.method: TACO derives the exact steepest-descent direction under a dimension-normalized 1-to-1 operator norm, selecting the sign of the maximum-magnitude entry per column of 2D weight matrices. Its practical implementation tracks only a small set of low-precision (FP8) gradient candidates per column with immediate gradient release.
S2KSOSEFaH.key_idea: Updates only the sign of each column's maximum-magnitude gradient entry as exact 1-to-1 operator-norm steepest descent, storing only a compact candidate subset.
S2KSOSEFaH.evidence: Theoretical convergence and winner-preservation analysis plus LLM fine-tuning memory and downstream accuracy benchmarks up to OPT-13B/30B scale.
S2KSOSEFaH.claimed_gains: Reduces persistent optimizer state by 174x relative to AdamW8bit (from 27.7 GB to 0.16 GB) and peak training memory by 2.9x (from 80.6 GB).
S2KSOSEFaH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the principled operator-norm derivation of column-wise one-sparse ternary updates and the large persistent state reduction.
S2KSOSEFaH.main_concern: Reviewers note that peak-memory savings over low-state baselines like Adafactor are confounded by autograd gradient-release hooks, and TACO trails Adafactor substantially on several NLP tasks.

5ASjSA2COO.one_liner: Benchmarks VLM visual graph perception and algorithmic reasoning across real-world domains and controlled layout/label visualization variants.
5ASjSA2COO.problem: Text-based graph benchmarks do not test whether vision-language models can visually perceive graph structures and perform algorithmic reasoning across varying visualizations.
5ASjSA2COO.method: Visual Graph Harness (VGH) pairs fine-grained graph perception tasks (node/edge existence and counts) with algorithmic tasks (shortest path, diameter, clique, TSP, etc.) across knowledge graphs, route maps, social networks, and topology commutative diagrams. Each graph is rendered under multiple layout and label-anonymization variants.
5ASjSA2COO.key_idea: Varies graph layout and label semantics on identical underlying graphs—including commutative diagrams—to test visual graph perception and algorithmic reasoning.
5ASjSA2COO.evidence: Diagnostic evaluation of VLMs using parsability gates, strict/soft accuracy, response-bias ratios, and constraint violations across domains and visualization variants.
5ASjSA2COO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the multi-variant layout-and-anonymization design, inclusion of commutative diagrams, and diagnostic error metrics.
5ASjSA2COO.main_concern: Reviewers note that omitting a text-only LLM baseline prevents separating perception from reasoning, promised cross-task consistency experiments are missing, and writing/related-work framing needs improvement.

nFLnHIUMlx.one_liner: Calibrates GEMM outlier orientations to apply Inner Hadamard Transforms in MXFP4 while extracting scaling-axis blind-spot outliers to BF16.
nFLnHIUMlx.problem: Hadamard transforms fail to eliminate MXFP4 quantization error when outliers align with the 32-element scaling axis, affecting 97.8–100% of weight-gradient GEMMs.
nFLnHIUMlx.method: AdaHOP calibrates stable row-wise, column-wise, or absent outlier patterns per GEMM operand, uses an Inner Hadamard Transform as the MXFP4 backbone, and selectively extracts only scaling-axis-aligned blind-spot rows or columns into a small BF16 path via fused Triton kernels.
nFLnHIUMlx.key_idea: Classifies per-GEMM outlier orientations relative to the scaling axis and routes only scaling-axis-aligned outlier rows/columns to a small BF16 path.
nFLnHIUMlx.evidence: Outlier-orientation measurements across three model families plus 1B–8B LLM training accuracy, activation memory, and Llama3.1-8B end-to-end speed benchmarks.
nFLnHIUMlx.claimed_gains: AdaHOP-Lv1 executes <1% of GEMM FLOPs in BF16, trails BF16 by 0.23 points in average zero-shot accuracy across 1B–8B models, reduces Llama3.1-8B activation memory by 3.6x, and speeds up training by 1.45x over BF16.
nFLnHIUMlx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the concrete measurement study of scaling-axis outlier orientations across GEMMs and the real Triton-kernel systems validation.
nFLnHIUMlx.main_concern: Reviewers question the theoretical proof details, note unclear efficiency advantage over optimized FP8/MXFP8 and limited scale comparison with Quartet, and cite overlap with TetraJet-v2 outlier extraction.

vmTnFtHN8S.one_liner: Selectively targets specific diffusion timesteps and frequency bands during data unlearning and proposes a normalized SSCD dissimilarity metric.
vmTnFtHN8S.problem: Uniformly applying loss-maximization unlearning across all diffusion timesteps and frequencies degrades generation quality or causes incomplete forgetting.
vmTnFtHN8S.method: Based on an analysis of uneven forgetting across diffusion stages and frequency components, the method restricts unlearning updates selectively to specific timesteps and frequency regions. The authors also introduce a normalized perturbation-distance SSCD metric for evaluating unlearning dissimilarity.
vmTnFtHN8S.key_idea: Concentrates diffusion data unlearning updates on selected timesteps and frequency bands rather than applying uniform loss maximization across the denoising process.
vmTnFtHN8S.evidence: Theoretical distortion/trade-off analysis and conditional/unconditional diffusion unlearning experiments (including CelebA-HQ per reviews).
vmTnFtHN8S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the diffusion-stage analysis showing uneven forgetting across timesteps and the simple plug-in selective design.
vmTnFtHN8S.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing comparisons to recent 2026 diffusion-unlearning baselines, lack of hyperparameter sensitivity ablations, limited dataset diversity, and unvalidated correlation of the proposed SSCD metric.

ExzCs8jaKl.one_liner: Uses LLM-grounded conservative cost functions and learned dynamics rollouts to synthesize counterfactual unsafe transitions for offline safe RL.
ExzCs8jaKl.problem: Offline safe RL methods fail on safety-critical datasets with few or no violation samples because they treat safe-but-infeasible states as safe.
ExzCs8jaKl.method: PROCO learns a dynamics model from offline data and prompts an LLM with natural-language safety descriptions to generate a conservative cost function. It then performs model-based rollouts to synthesize counterfactual unsafe transitions for training downstream offline safe RL algorithms.
ExzCs8jaKl.key_idea: Grounds natural-language safety constraints via an LLM into a conservative cost function and runs learned-model rollouts to synthesize counterfactual unsafe data.
ExzCs8jaKl.evidence: Plug-in evaluation across 17 tasks and three offline safe RL algorithms with ablation studies.
ExzCs8jaKl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree learning safe policies from violation-scarce offline data is practical and appreciate PROCO's plug-in compatibility and violation reductions.
ExzCs8jaKl.main_concern: Reviewers question what the LLM adds over manually tightened safety thresholds (missing non-LLM controls), note reliance on an unsafe validation set, and highlight that short 1-step rollouts/relabeling narrow generality.

Rd0dxUJuas.one_liner: Probes Muon's matrix-representation advantage over nSGDM via reshaping/shuffling interventions and heterogeneous row-block curvature convergence analysis.
Rd0dxUJuas.problem: It is unclear what matrix representation contributes to Muon's optimization advantage beyond the vector normalization of normalized SGD with momentum (nSGDM).
Rd0dxUJuas.method: Muse intervenes on the matrix representation used for Muon updates via order-preserving reshaping and fixed-shape entry shuffling. The authors analyze single-step progress via nuclear support and update alignment, and prove stationarity bounds under heterogeneous row-block curvature for exact polar and five-step Newton-Schulz updates.
Rd0dxUJuas.key_idea: Separates matrix shape from entry organization via reshaping/shuffling interventions and links Muon's advantage to spectral row-energy limits under heterogeneous row-block curvature.
Rd0dxUJuas.evidence: Theoretical stationarity bounds plus controlled row-block problems and 130M/600M language-model pretraining experiments.
Rd0dxUJuas.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clean reshaping-versus-shuffling interventions separating shape from entry organization and the curvature-sensitive analysis.
Rd0dxUJuas.main_concern: Reviewers note that no alternative representation beats native Muon, the curvature mechanism is only partially verified in LM experiments (leaving MLP matrices unexamined), and the theoretical comparison depends on norm relaxations.

NBi7fzfXcw.one_liner: Task-agnostic output head POINT predicts tabular classification and regression by placing a probability distribution over labeled support examples.
NBi7fzfXcw.problem: Tabular in-context learning models lack a unified prediction head that simultaneously supports adaptive classification, strong scalar regression, and native multi-output regression.
NBi7fzfXcw.method: POINT treats the in-context labeled support set as the output simplex, summing support probabilities per class for classification and taking expectations over continuous support labels for scalar or vector regression. It trains both tasks jointly via POINT-CE, a support-distribution cross-entropy loss using a moment-preserving teacher, with theory showing conditional probability and mean recovery.
NBi7fzfXcw.key_idea: Predict over the simplex of in-context labeled support rows using a unified support-distribution cross-entropy loss (POINT-CE) for both classification and multi-output regression.
NBi7fzfXcw.evidence: Theoretical consistency analysis under support coverage and empirical evaluations on tabular classification, scalar regression, and multi-output regression benchmarks.
NBi7fzfXcw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the unified support-simplex prediction interface and the principled theoretical link between support-level cross-entropy and both classification and regression targets.
NBi7fzfXcw.main_concern: The empirical gains of POINT-CE are not cleanly isolated from loss weighting, retrieval differences, and teacher choices, and the global softmax bandwidth does not adapt to per-dataset representation scale.

JmVHT6MxWn.one_liner: Sheaf-inspired 4.5M-parameter selector propagates text-visual relevance over a visual graph with degree correction for one-shot visual token pruning.
JmVHT6MxWn.problem: Processing all visual tokens in multimodal LLMs causes high prefill cost, while token-wise saliency ignores inter-token dependencies and graph propagation can be skewed by node degree.
JmVHT6MxWn.method: SheafPrune uses learned modality-specific projections and a sparse text-visual graph to seed token relevance, propagates scores on a visual similarity graph with degree correction, and keeps a hard top-k subset before the frozen LLM. A 4.5M-parameter retention-ratio-conditioned selector is trained end-to-end through frozen LLaVA-NeXT-8B using the language-modeling loss.
JmVHT6MxWn.key_idea: Transfer text-visual relevance via modality projections onto a visual graph, propagate scores with node-degree correction, and prune top-k tokens once via a budget-conditioned selector.
JmVHT6MxWn.evidence: Evaluated across four MLLM backbones, ten benchmarks, and seven pruning ratios under a unified re-implemented baseline protocol.
JmVHT6MxWn.claimed_gains: Achieves best retention in 22 of 28 backbone-budget settings, and retaining 10% of visual tokens on LLaVA-NeXT yields a 5.15× net prefill speedup and an 84.0% end-to-end FLOPs reduction.
JmVHT6MxWn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the unified re-implementation across four backbones and ten benchmarks, transparent latency/FLOPs reporting, and clear separation of propagation normalization and degree correction.
JmVHT6MxWn.main_concern: Headline results select the best test-time hyperparameter delta per evaluation point rather than via held-out validation, and the sheaf framing adds little over standard learned projections and graph smoothing.

PjKU7RX3Eq.one_liner: Verbalized self-distillation (VSD) prompts a writer for error-diagnosis instructions to condition a teacher that reweights GRPO negative advantages.
PjKU7RX3Eq.problem: GRPO assigns uniform negative advantage to every token in a failed rollout, penalizing valid reasoning steps alongside actual errors.
PjKU7RX3Eq.method: Given a successful rollout and a failed attempt, a writer model identifies the first divergence point and writes hindsight instructions. A teacher conditioned on these instructions computes per-token KL divergence against the current policy over the failed rollout to rescale negative token advantages in GRPO.
PjKU7RX3Eq.key_idea: Condition a self-distillation teacher on writer-generated failure-diagnosis instructions and use stop-gradient teacher-student KL divergence to reweight negative GRPO token advantages.
PjKU7RX3Eq.evidence: Evaluated on four mathematical reasoning benchmarks using Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B against GRPO, SDPO, RLRT, and raw-privilege controls.
PjKU7RX3Eq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find VSD simple and intuitive, noting consistent pass@1 gains over GRPO and raw-solution conditioning without requiring a process reward model or inference-time overhead.
PjKU7RX3Eq.main_concern: Comparisons match training steps rather than wall-clock time or FLOPs despite extra writer and teacher passes, and ablations do not isolate teacher reweighting from the 0.75 negative-advantage floor on Qwen3-4B.

DvQFeu3Rwn.one_liner: Gene2Brain-AE couples a genetic VAE to an NMF-style brain-imaging autoencoder via a directional predictor to disentangle atrophy axes.
DvQFeu3Rwn.problem: Neuroimaging alone cannot separate similar brain atrophy patterns driven by distinct genetic versus non-genetic biological mechanisms.
DvQFeu3Rwn.method: Gene2Brain-AE combines an NMF-style non-negative imaging autoencoder with a genetic VAE linked by a directional predictor mapping genetic embeddings into a subset of imaging latent factors. This decomposes imaging variation into genetically predictable and residual components while requiring only imaging at inference time.
DvQFeu3Rwn.key_idea: Directionally predict a subset of non-negative NMF imaging latent factors from a genetic VAE to separate genetically informed atrophy axes from residual variation without test-time genotypes.
DvQFeu3Rwn.evidence: Evaluated on semi-synthetic recovery benchmarks, ADNI discovery, and external clinical/cognitive/neuropathological validation across eight independent cohorts.
DvQFeu3Rwn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the biologically motivated directional coupling, spatially interpretable NMF decomposition, and unusually strong external validation across eight independent cohorts without genotypes.
DvQFeu3Rwn.main_concern: The framework lacks theoretical identifiability and disentanglement guarantees, has limited methodological novelty over multimodal shared-private autoencoders, and does not rule out that multiple genetic axes reflect a shared APOE signal.

CqwesbUXkY.one_liner: CoLU pairs confidence-weighted single-layer unlearning with brief subset-trial layer screening (BLS) to balance forgetting, retention, and memory.
CqwesbUXkY.problem: Full-model LLM unlearning damages retained knowledge and incurs high GPU memory cost, while the forgetting-retention trade-off varies sharply across transformer layers.
CqwesbUXkY.method: CoLU updates a single selected transformer layer using probability-weighted forgetting combined with retain regularization. To avoid exhaustive layer sweeps, Brief Layer Screening (BLS) ranks short unlearning trials on a data subset by a normalized forgetting-retention (NFR) score before full-data unlearning on shortlisted layers.
CqwesbUXkY.key_idea: Screen candidate layers via short subset unlearning trials ranked by a normalized forgetting-retention score, then apply confidence-weighted forgetting with retain regularization to one layer.
CqwesbUXkY.evidence: Evaluated on TOFU (six model/forget-split settings) and MUSE (Books and News) against NPO, SimNPO, SatImp, and FOM-UL, with GPU memory and screening-time measurements.
CqwesbUXkY.claimed_gains: Compared with full screening, BLS reduces total training time by 60.2% to 79.7% on TOFU, and CoLU improves forgetting and retention over NPO, SatImp, and GA-based FOM-UL in all six TOFU settings and over SimNPO in five.
CqwesbUXkY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical GPU memory savings of single-layer updates, end-to-end screening cost reporting, and strong retain-set scores on TOFU and MUSE.
CqwesbUXkY.main_concern: Layer and model selection optimize the same NFR forget/retain metrics reported as final test results without an independent validation split, and ablations omit matched-selection baselines like WGA and gradient selectors.

nLa4VzyllH.one_liner: Persistent LLM-objects (POLO) maintain self-authored structured state schemas updated per message instead of raw transcripts for stateful workflows.
nLa4VzyllH.problem: Transcript-based agent frameworks struggle to maintain accurate long-horizon state across interleaved events and mid-workflow rule changes.
nLa4VzyllH.method: POLO represents software as persistent LLM-objects defined in natural language that derive and revise their own structured state schemas, rewriting required state variables per incoming message while discarding processing traces. The authors also introduce FlowStateBench, a benchmark of multi-week stateful workflows with mid-stream rule changes.
nLa4VzyllH.key_idea: Replace agent conversation transcripts with persistent LLM-objects that infer, update, and revise private structured state schemas from natural-language definitions on each message.
nLa4VzyllH.evidence: Evaluated on the self-constructed FlowStateBench against LangGraph, Letta, CrewAI, and OpenClaw with state-vs-transcript ablations.
nLa4VzyllH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the reframing of LLM memory as self-authored program state and the dynamic FlowStateBench setting compelling and well motivated.
nLa4VzyllH.main_concern: Main comparisons are confounded because POLO uses a stronger model (GPT-5.4) and shared-state read tools unavailable to GPT-5-nano baselines, and single-object ablations outperform the multi-object design at lower cost.

fsLNlky4pP.one_liner: RePath segments gigapixel whole-slide tumors zero-shot by comparing patch class distributions to slide-specific anchors via Jensen-Shannon divergence.
fsLNlky4pP.problem: Independent patch-wise VLM scoring of gigapixel whole-slide images causes prompt sensitivity and spatially inconsistent tumor segmentation.
fsLNlky4pP.method: RePath uses text prompts only to seed slide-specific tumor, normal, and non-tissue anchor patches from the slide itself. It then computes intra-slide relational affinity via Jensen-Shannon divergence between each patch's class distribution and anchor distributions, and contrasts tumor against normal and non-tissue affinities via Differential Affinity Integration (DAI).
fsLNlky4pP.key_idea: Seed slide-internal anchor patches with text prompts, compute patch-to-anchor Jensen-Shannon divergence in class-distribution space, and contrast tumor versus non-tumor affinities.
fsLNlky4pP.evidence: Evaluated on 1,647 test slides across multiple organs and three VLM backbones (including CONCH) against zero-shot and 10-WSI few-shot baselines.
fsLNlky4pP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the simple, clinically motivated intra-slide relational reformulation and consistent IoU gains across organs and three VLM backbones.
fsLNlky4pP.main_concern: Main evaluation is restricted to tumor-bearing slides with only 8.6% specificity on tumor-negative Camelyon16 slides, and ablations do not cleanly separate representation space from the JSD metric.

0N6XKqoWwB.one_liner: RL-trained lightweight Chainer maps queries to open-loop multi-step prompt chains executed by a frozen LLM.
0N6XKqoWwB.problem: Single-call Chain-of-Thought scales intra-call test-time compute, but it is unclear whether multi-call prompt orchestration can be learned via RL to improve frozen LLMs.
0N6XKqoWwB.method: Chainer is a small model initialized with SFT and optimized with GRPO using end-task rewards, chain-quality signals, validity bonuses, and dynamic step costs to emit self-contained sub-prompt sequences for a frozen executor LLM. Execution is open-loop, attributing gains purely to the learned prompt trajectory.
0N6XKqoWwB.key_idea: Train a lightweight SFT+GRPO orchestrator to generate open-loop sub-prompt sequences for a frozen LLM under end-task, chain-quality, and step-cost rewards.
0N6XKqoWwB.evidence: Evaluated across six benchmarks (Arena-Hard, AIME, LiveCodeBench, GPQA, AA-Omniscience, IFBench) with reasoning enabled and disabled, including token-budget-matched comparisons.
0N6XKqoWwB.claimed_gains: With reasoning enabled, Chainer improves Arena-Hard (+17.3), AIME (+10.0), LiveCodeBench (+8.2), GPQA (+2.0), and AA-Omniscience (-2.9, lower is better) while degrading IFBench.
0N6XKqoWwB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate framing inter-call orchestration as a complementary test-time compute axis and the broad six-benchmark evaluation with SFT-vs-GRPO ablations.
0N6XKqoWwB.main_concern: Ablations fail to isolate learned decomposition from prompt rewriting or repeated calls, end-to-end compute including planner and input tokens is not matched, and Table 1 contains inconsistent swapped numbers.

uuvOdvPIqC.one_liner: Mining natural semantics-preserving code transformations from real commits measures and disrupts agentic vulnerability discovery.
uuvOdvPIqC.problem: Automated vulnerability-discovery agents can attack software at scale, yet their robustness across functionally equivalent code representations is poorly understood.
uuvOdvPIqC.method: The authors mine 21 recurring, functionality-preserving code transformations from real-world software commits and apply them individually and in composition to vulnerable repositories. They evaluate how these natural transformations affect frontier vulnerability-analysis agents using executable proof-of-concept validation, including adaptive attackers attempting to reverse them.
uuvOdvPIqC.key_idea: Mine recurring semantics-preserving code transformations from real commits and apply them to vulnerable repositories to disrupt agentic vulnerability discovery.
uuvOdvPIqC.evidence: Evaluated on real-world repositories with executable PoC validation across multiple frontier models and agent harnesses (including Codex with GPT-6 Sol).
uuvOdvPIqC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate grounding transformations in real-world commits rather than synthetic obfuscation and validating vulnerability preservation via executable PoCs.
uuvOdvPIqC.main_concern: Novelty over prior semantics-preserving code transformation catalogs is not clearly established, model and agent-framework effects are confounded, and statistical significance tests are omitted.

EZUV2EJjSi.one_liner: LiveTS-Suite benchmark and TimeOmni-Live model enable continuous stateful time-series understanding via stream-persistent memory and elastic synchronization.
EZUV2EJjSi.problem: Offline time-series language models process fixed windows independently without retaining cross-window state for continuous real-time streams.
EZUV2EJjSi.method: The authors define Continuous & Live Time Series Understanding (CL-TSU) and release LiveTS-Suite (over 5K streams, 2.2B timesteps, 15K response events across 18 tasks). They propose TimeOmni-Live, combining hybrid time-series encoding, a stream-persistent hybrid memory mechanism, and elastic stream-inference synchronization to reduce processing lag.
EZUV2EJjSi.key_idea: Pair hybrid temporal encoding with stream-persistent KV-snapshotted memory and elastic inference synchronization for continuous stateful time-series language modeling.
EZUV2EJjSi.evidence: Evaluated on LiveTS-Suite across 18 tasks measuring response timeliness, content accuracy, token consumption, real-time factor, and latency.
EZUV2EJjSi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the substantial engineering effort behind LiveTS-Suite, the practical streaming runtime design, and joint evaluation of timeliness, accuracy, and efficiency.
EZUV2EJjSi.main_concern: Baseline comparisons lack traditional statistical and native time-series foundation models as well as documented closed-source LLM prompts, while the method relies heavily on stacking existing components on largely synthetic/injected streams.

rKJBCTurUb.one_liner: Oscillatory Delta Networks transport matrix memory along volume-preserving SO(2) or SL(2) orbits via an input-dependent clock before delta-rule writes.
rKJBCTurUb.problem: Linear attention and delta-rule models generate highly correlated keys that overwrite each other, preventing fixed-size matrix memory from reaching full capacity.
rKJBCTurUb.method: ODN introduces an inductive bias to decorrelate keys by transporting the recurrent memory state along volume-preserving orbits before each delta-rule write. ODN-SO(2) uses one input-dependent clock per head to advance coupled 2D rotations, while ODN-SL(2) learns orbit geometry via special linear transformations, addressing key-value pairs by both key and internal write time.
rKJBCTurUb.key_idea: Transport delta-rule matrix memory along input-clocked SO(2) or SL(2) volume-preserving orbits before each write to phase-address and decorrelate correlated keys.
rKJBCTurUb.evidence: Theoretical capacity proofs (Propositions 1–5), lag-indexed overwrite recall tests, and language-modeling experiments on LongBench, LAMBADA, and WikiText-2 against Gated DeltaNet, Selective RoPE, and KDA.
rKJBCTurUb.claimed_gains: ODN-SO(2) leads in 12 out of 14 LongBench tasks and outperforms Gated DeltaNet, Selective RoPE, and Kimi Delta Attention.
rKJBCTurUb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clear diagnosis of key-correlation interference, zero state-size overhead, strong synthetic overwrite recall, and rigorous capacity theory.
rKJBCTurUb.main_concern: Language-modeling gains are modest with single-seed runs and mixed perplexity-accuracy trade-offs, no 1B+ scale results are shown, and presentation/relation to complex diagonal recurrences (LRU/MDN) is unclear.

Y1o3rWSDgk.one_liner: Virtual-depth supervision extrapolates late recurrent states from short rollouts to stabilize deep test-time medical image segmentation.
Y1o3rWSDgk.problem: Compact recurrent medical image segmenters trained with short rollouts suffer accuracy degradation when unrolled to deeper test-time refinement depths.
Y1o3rWSDgk.method: VD-Refine geometrically extrapolates late feature states from an eight-step rollout to initialize label-supervised two-step correction windows without backpropagating through long prefixes. It combines initial-state-conditioned FiLM, multi-start training, and an optional analytic inference mode that decodes the extrapolated state directly.
Y1o3rWSDgk.key_idea: Geometrically extrapolate late recurrent states from short rollouts to initialize two-step supervised correction windows and enable one-shot analytic inference.
Y1o3rWSDgk.evidence: Evaluated on BraTS, LiTS, and DRIVE with a 4.40M-parameter model, including rollout stability tests up to 256 full-volume steps and 1,024 patch steps.
Y1o3rWSDgk.claimed_gains: Surpasses all evaluated baselines in mean Dice on BraTS, LiTS, and DRIVE (4.40M parameters on BraTS), stays stable through 256 full-volume and 1,024 patch steps, and analytic inference matches 32-step accuracy at about half the FLOPs on BraTS.
Y1o3rWSDgk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple, low-cost virtual-depth formulation and thorough stability diagnostics across extreme rollout depths.
Y1o3rWSDgk.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate geometric extrapolation from training on gradient-free exact late starts, and practical accuracy gains beyond eight steps are very small (around 0.07 Dice on BraTS).

wC9uDfAKkZ.one_liner: RaLiMPs linearize MLPs using low-degree rational activation approximations and separable partial-fraction random-feature kernels.
wC9uDfAKkZ.problem: Polynomial-based MLP linearization requires high degrees to accurately approximate standard activations, inflating kernel bottleneck widths and inference cost.
wC9uDfAKkZ.method: Rationally Linearized Multilayer Perceptrons (RaLiMPs) replace standard activations with low-degree rational approximations converted via partial-fraction and Laplace representations into separable random-feature kernels with narrow bottlenecks. This preserves input-weight separability for efficient layer fusion across MLP layers.
wC9uDfAKkZ.key_idea: Approximate MLP activations with low-degree rational functions in a separable partial-fraction random-feature form to construct narrow-bottleneck linearized layers.
wC9uDfAKkZ.evidence: Single-layer approximation error and variance analysis, plus empirical evaluations spanning implicit 3D models and large language models (including AIME and MATH500).
wC9uDfAKkZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize that the partial-fraction rational construction preserves input-weight separability for layer fusion while supported by error and variance analysis.
wC9uDfAKkZ.main_concern: Reported AIME24/AIME25 pass@16 numbers are mathematically incompatible with the stated 30-problem evaluation protocol, and comparisons against other rational activation methods are missing.

s3IIG3F8U5.one_liner: World Boundary Bench probes language world models across Causal Forking, World Commitment, and Role Boundary tracks in executable environments.
s3IIG3F8U5.problem: Interactive language world models fail unpredictably on decisive environment details, long-horizon state consistency, and prompt-injection-like embedded text.
s3IIG3F8U5.method: World Boundary Bench (WBB) spans Terminal, MCP, and Web environments with executable checks across three tracks: paired Causal Forking tests, underspecified World Commitment consistency episodes, and Role Boundary instruction-injection tests. The authors also run a sim-to-real rejection fine-tuning study on ToolSandbox.
s3IIG3F8U5.key_idea: Evaluate language world models with paired causal transitions, self-committed state consistency checks, and embedded-instruction boundary tests using executable verifiers.
s3IIG3F8U5.evidence: Evaluated 13 proprietary and open-source models across 100 Causal Forking pairs, 200 World Commitment episodes, and 100 Role Boundary pairs, plus a sim-to-real replay study.
s3IIG3F8U5.claimed_gains: In the sim-to-real study, rejection fine-tuning on LWM self-reported success trajectories improves real-environment success from 2.81% to 4.41%.
s3IIG3F8U5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the three complementary executable diagnostic tracks, the self-committed consistency design, and the real-environment replay audit.
s3IIG3F8U5.main_concern: The benchmark is small and built from only five underlying causal mechanisms, and it does not demonstrate that WBB scores predict real-replay or downstream training gains.

WLStKyK5Qp.one_liner: Speculative Rollback Correction uses environment reset-and-replay at teacher-selected recoverability drops to collect counterfactual GUI imitation data.
WLStKyK5Qp.problem: Interactive imitation learning flags errors by disagreement with a reference teacher, wrongly penalizing valid alternative trajectories in multi-solution GUI tasks.
WLStKyK5Qp.method: The authors define action harm as reduction in optimal task recoverability and derive a Doob decomposition for per-step harm. Instantiated as SRC, the student executes a short speculative segment, a teacher accepts it or picks a rollback point where feasibility drops, and environment reset-and-replay collects verified corrections for SFT.
WLStKyK5Qp.key_idea: Run speculative student segments, let a teacher localize feasibility-reducing rollback points, and reset-and-replay the environment to collect verifier-filtered corrections.
WLStKyK5Qp.evidence: Theoretical Doob-decomposition analysis and GUI agent imitation experiments across three benchmarks (including OSWorld and WebArena) comparing against Expert SFT and LEAP-style baselines.
WLStKyK5Qp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate isolating teacher queries and resets to training time, reducing teacher queries over LEAP, and achieving teacher-free gains over Expert SFT.
WLStKyK5Qp.main_concern: The implementation prompts a heuristic teacher that also rejects reversible or unnecessary actions without estimating the theoretical recoverability quantities, creating a wide gap between theory and practice.

PC9bqhW05Q.one_liner: SUITE annotates fine-grained forget-retain boundaries for LLM unlearning, paired with JensUn++ for coherent refusal-based unlearning.
PC9bqhW05Q.problem: Coarse LLM unlearning benchmarks hide under-forgetting under paraphrased or indirect queries and over-forgetting of unrelated knowledge due to unannotated forget-retain boundaries.
PC9bqhW05Q.method: The authors build SUITE, a training corpus and evaluation protocol explicitly annotating diverse forget-query formulations alongside semantic, syntactic, and lexical retain probes for real-world factual domains. They also introduce JensUn++, an unlearning algorithm designed to produce coherent refusals instead of gibberish.
PC9bqhW05Q.key_idea: Explicitly annotates fine-grained forget-retain boundaries in training and evaluation data (SUITE) and trains refusal-based unlearning (JensUn++) across them.
PC9bqhW05Q.evidence: Evaluated across three LLMs in sequential and joint unlearning settings, with ablations, adversarial queries, relearning, and quantization tests.
PC9bqhW05Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that fine-grained forget-retain evaluation is needed, that the LKF-to-SUITE data ablation is compelling, and that empirical testing across models and settings is thorough.
PC9bqhW05Q.main_concern: Reviewers note that JensUn++ still degrades the semantically closest retain tier (s0), that refusal training may suppress rather than remove knowledge, and that components of SUITE and JensUn++ largely combine prior work.

wY77eYNMsw.one_liner: Global Concept Gating learns a single sparse concept mask shared across all inputs and classes for unsupervised concept bottleneck models.
wY77eYNMsw.problem: Existing sparsity mechanisms in unsupervised concept bottleneck models only constrain per-input or per-class activations, leaving large, redundant global concept vocabularies that hurt inspectability.
wY77eYNMsw.method: Global Concept Gating (GCG) attaches a learnable sparse mask shared across all inputs and classes to any unsupervised CBM, jointly selecting a compact task-specific concept vocabulary while training the downstream classifier.
wY77eYNMsw.key_idea: Learns a global sparse gate shared across all inputs and classes to prune the concept vocabulary jointly with classifier training.
wY77eYNMsw.evidence: Evaluated across multiple concept bottleneck architectures and image classification tasks, measuring concept set size, accuracy, semantic grounding, and information leakage.
wY77eYNMsw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that measuring and reducing global concept vocabulary size addresses a real gap in unsupervised CBMs while maintaining predictive accuracy.
wY77eYNMsw.main_concern: Reviewers argue that experiments lack qualitative inspection of removed concepts, do not cleanly isolate GCG from general global feature selection and refitting, and do not convincingly prove interpretability gains from global vocabulary reduction.

U1ufyCV4Wa.one_liner: Language to Design pairs LLM design proposals with finite-difference physics Jacobian updates over a cross-robot MJCF co-design space.
U1ufyCV4Wa.problem: Robot design requires joint mechanical and control expertise and relies on slow manual cycles of guessing, prototyping, and testing.
U1ufyCV4Wa.method: Language to Design (L2D) is a training-free co-design framework where language proposes what to change and simulation-grounded physical-descriptor Jacobian updates decide how much. It operates over a unified MJCF co-design space covering kinematics, motors, added joints, and continuous contact shapes across five robot families, producing load-optimized 3D-printable parts.
U1ufyCV4Wa.key_idea: Combines LLM-generated qualitative design edits with finite-difference physical-descriptor Jacobian updates in a unified cross-robot MJCF design space.
U1ufyCV4Wa.evidence: Demonstrated on 15 tasks across five robot families (arms, grippers, hands, quadrupeds, humanoids), round-trip reconstruction on unseen MuJoCo Menagerie models, and two real-hardware tasks.
U1ufyCV4Wa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the broad cross-robot MJCF design space and the clear technical motivation of combining language priors with physics-based Jacobian updates.
U1ufyCV4Wa.main_concern: Reviewers find baseline comparisons confounded because budgets match LLM spend rather than design evaluations or simulation effort, and note that ablations do not isolate the inverse-Jacobian update or substantiate broad automation claims.
